title: 21 dots in the Korean version of the dot plot — If three dots mark 3.75%, the loan interest rate will change in 2027
deck: On November 26, 2026, the Monetary Policy Committee will issue a new dot plot containing the outlook for the next six months along with whether to raise the base interest rate from 3.00% to 3.25%. In August, 3.25% was the most with 10 out of 21 points. How many 3.75% are recorded this time and where the median goes will determine the upper end of treasury bond and variable loan interest rates in 2027.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: The Bank of Korea's Monetary Policy Committee will set the base interest rate at the last meeting of the year on November 26, 2026, and announce a dot plot containing the outlook for the next six months and a revised economic outlook. The current base interest rate is 3.00% per annum, raised by 0.25% points each in July and August and then frozen on October 22.

In the December Bond Market Index (BMSI) published by the Korea Financial Investment Association on November 24, 54 out of 100 bond market workers chose an increase and 46 chose a freeze. The background is consumer prices of 2.8% in October (original 2.8%) and real GDP growth of 1.0% in the third quarter compared to the previous quarter. The IMF raised its growth forecast for this year to 3.9%, and KDI raised its growth forecast to 3.8%.

The dot plot in August was 5 at 3.00%, 10 at 3.25%, and 6 at 3.50%, with the median being 3.25%. How many dots are added to 3.75% this time and whether the median rises to 3.50% will determine the direction of the 3-year treasury bond (3.50-3.85% forecast) and variable mortgage interest rates at the end of the year. The forecasts of securities companies range from 0 to 3 to 4 at 3.75%.
body:
On the afternoon of November 26, 2026, the Bank of Korea's Monetary Policy Committee sets the last base interest rate of the year. The market's interest is shifting from 'whether to raise prices' to 'where to post six months from now.' It is a dot plot that depicts the outlook for the base interest rate six months from now with a total of 21 dots, 3 each for 7 members of the Monetary Policy Committee.

![Interest rate pressure gauge and city model. Ahead of the Monetary Policy Committee meeting on November 26, 2026, the market is watching the increase in the base interest rate from 3.00% to 3.25% and the movement of the median value of the dot plot. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/bok-dotplot-375-nov26-2026.jpg)

## 21 points in August — 3.25% was the most

The previous dot plot was released in August. 5 were taken at 3.00%, 10 at 3.25%, and 6 at 3.50%. The median was 3.25%. Since the structure is such that 7 members present 3 items each, the difference of 1 space is the intensity of expectation for ‘one more increase’.

There are two things the market sees at this meeting. The question is whether the base interest rate itself will be raised from 3.00% to 3.25%, and whether the median value of the new dot plot will remain at 3.25% or rise to 3.50%.

## 3.75%, how many dots are there?

On the 25th, bond market experts differed in their opinions on whether the 3.75% mark should be marked. Kang Seung-won, a researcher at NH Investment & Securities, expected 2 to 3. It is believed that if the gross domestic product (GDP) gap and core price forecasts are increased in the revised economic outlook, hawkish members can open it up to 3.75%. Min Ji-hee, a researcher at Mirae Asset Securities, saw a maximum of three to four. Lim Jae-gyun, a researcher at KB Securities, predicted that there would not be a dot at 3.75%.

This is why it is pointed out that the distribution is more important than the numbers themselves. Even if 3.75% is recorded as 3, if 3.25% prevails, the market reads that there is room to adjust the pace of tightening. Conversely, if the median rises to 3.50%, it is not a signal of 'one more time' but of 'the final interest rate is higher'.

## 54 to 46 for the impression — tighter, but heavier for the impression.

In the December Bond Market Index (BMSI) announced by the Korea Financial Investment Association on the 24th, 54 out of 100 bond market workers chose the Monetary Policy Committee to raise the base interest rate on the 26th, and 46 chose to freeze it. Although it is slight, the impression takes precedence.

The numbers on which it is based are prices and growth. The consumer price inflation rate in October was 2.8% compared to the same month last year, and the core price excluding food and energy was 2.8%, exceeding the Bank of Korea's target (2.0%). Real gross domestic product in the third quarter increased by 1.0% compared to the previous quarter, exceeding the Bank of Korea's August forecast (0.3%) by more than three times. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) raised its growth forecast for this year from 3.3% to 3.9%, and the Korea Development Institute (KDI) raised its growth forecast from 3.2% to 3.8%.

The Bank of Korea raised the base interest rate by 0.25% points each in July and August to 3.00% per annum and then froze it on October 22. This is the last meeting of the year, and the revised economic outlook and dot plot are released on the same day.

## The median price will determine the loan interest rate in 2027

The dot plot determines the ‘top’ of Treasury bond interest rates. The outlook for 3-year Treasury bonds at the end of the year varies between 3.50 and 3.85%. If there is a minority opinion on freezing along with the decision to raise the rate, and the median value of the dot plot remains at 3.25%, there is a forecast that the 3-year bond could go down to 3.50%. Conversely, the calculation is that the median value is set at 3.50%, and if it is hawkish, it can rise to 3.75%.

This leads to the loan interest rate. Commercial bank variable housing mortgage loans are linked to COFIX or 6-month financial bonds, and fixed loans are linked to 5-year financial bonds. When short-term interest rates rise and long-term interest rates fall, a reversal occurs where variable types become more expensive than fixed types even within the same bank. In fact, as of November 17, the top five major banks' variable mortgage loans were at 4.44~6.51% per annum, and 5-year fixed loans were at 4.47~6.40% per annum.

## Confirmed and unconfirmed

What was confirmed was the distribution of the August dot plot (5 at 3.00%, 10 at 3.25%, 6 at 3.50%, median 3.25%), the October price level of 2.8%, the third quarter growth rate of 1.0%, and the 54 to 46 vote of the Korea Gold Investment Association survey.

What has not been confirmed are the results. The dot plot is a member's individual conditional outlook, not a policy promise, and the number of 3.75% points is only a securities company's estimate. The U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on December 8-9 and the new COFIX announcement next month have not yet arrived. Three numbers announced on the afternoon of the 26th — the base interest rate, the midpoint of the dot plot, and whether there is a minority opinion to freeze — will determine the cost of funds until the first quarter of 2027.

factCheck.note: The base interest rate of 3.00%, an increase of 0.25 percentage points each in July and August, and a freeze on October 22 were confirmed by the Bank of Korea's monetary policy direction press release and multiple media reports citing it. The August dot plot distribution (5 at 3.00%, 10 at 3.25%, 6 at 3.50%, median 3.25%) is a value compiled by E-Today and Current Affairs Journal e from the Bank of Korea data. Price and growth indicators are based on the National Data Center's consumer price index (2.8% in October) and the Bank of Korea's 3rd quarter GDP preliminary figure (1.0% compared to the previous quarter). How many dots there will be at 3.75% and where the median will go are all the predictions of securities research institutes and are not confirmed results. The dot plot is a conditional forecast of an individual member of the Monetary Policy Committee and is not a policy promise, and the results have not been confirmed until the announcement on the 26th. The 3-year Treasury bond outlook (3.50-3.85%) and the variable/fixed mortgage loan figures are at the time of quotation (November 17-25), and the actual applied interest rate varies depending on the additional and preferential interest rates for each bank and the time of recalculation.

title: Loans 5.02%, deposits 3.62% — what happened in the month when the gap narrowed by 0.10 percentage points
deck: In October 2026, the interest rate on bank household loans was 5.02% per annum, exceeding 5% for the first time in 2 years and 11 months since November 2023. Mortgage loans are at 4.98%, the highest since March 2012. However, in the same month, deposit interest rates rose faster than loan interest rates, narrowing the new loan-deposit rate spread to 1.02% points. What does it mean that loans are rising but the gap is shrinking?
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: In the 'October 2026 Weighted Average Interest Rate for Financial Institutions' announced by the Bank of Korea on November 25, 2026, the household loan interest rate based on the new transaction amount was 5.02% per annum, up 0.06 percentage points from the previous month (4.96%). It has exceeded 5% in 2 years and 11 months since November 2023 (5.04%). Mortgage loans are at 4.98%, the highest in 14 years and 7 months since March 2012 (5.00%), and have risen for six consecutive months since May.

In the same month, the savings deposit interest rate rose 0.17 percentage points to 3.62%, more than twice the increase in loan interest rates (0.07 percentage points). The proportion of term deposits of 4.0-5.0% per annum increased from 10.6% in September to 29.0% in October. The interest rate difference between deposits and loans based on the new amount has narrowed from 1.12 percentage points to 1.02 percentage points, and the interest rate difference based on the balance is 2.20 percentage points.

Fixed mortgage loans were 5.13% and variable mortgage loans were 4.90%, reducing the gap from 0.35 percentage points to 0.23 percentage points. This is the result of a rise in short-term interest rates (Cofix 3.18 → 3.31%) and a fall in long-term interest rates (4.53 → 4.34% for 5-year bank bonds). Ahead of the Monetary Policy Committee meeting on the 26th, 3-month MSRP (3.323%) and 3-month CD (3.390%) are already reflecting a 0.25% point increase.
body:
The average interest rate for new household loans received from banks in October 2026 was 5.02% per year. It has exceeded 5% in 2 years and 11 months since November 2023 (5.04%). Mortgage loans are at 4.98%, the highest in 14 years and 7 months since March 2012 (5.00%). In the same month, the deposit interest rate rose 0.17 percentage points to 3.62%. When loans rise by 0.07% points, deposits rise by 0.17% points. In that gap, the loan-deposit rate spread was 1.02% points, narrowing by 0.10% points compared to September (1.12% points). This is the number of the ‘Weighted Average Interest Rate for Financial Institutions for October 2026’ published by the Bank of Korea on the 25th.

![A man in his 50s holding a loan statement and a savings account in both hands and looking at them alternately at the bank consultation counter. In October 2026, the interest rate for new household loans was 5.02% per annum and 1-year term deposits were 3.77%, narrowing the gap to 1.02 percentage points. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/loan-rate-502-deposit-362-gap-2026.jpg)

## 5.02% — A line crossed again after 3 years

It is housing mortgage loans that have driven up household loan interest rates. It rose by 0.10 percentage points to 4.98%, rising for six consecutive months since May (4.32%) and the highest since March 2012. Guaranteed loans (4.56%) and deposit loans (4.63%) also rose. On the contrary, general credit loans fell 0.06 percentage points to 6.43%, falling for the first time in five months. The Bank of Korea explained that this was due to the lowering of the additional interest rates that some banks had previously raised. 31.0% of new household loans are in the 5-6% annual range (23.0% in September). Less than 4% is 9.7%, or one in ten cases.

## Fixed 5.13%, variable 4.90% — gap reduced by 0.12 percentage points

Housing mortgage loans are fixed 5.13% (+0.02% points) and variable 4.90% (+0.14% points). The fixed type rose for 13 consecutive months (the longest in history) from October 2025 (3.97%), and the variable type rose for 5 consecutive months from June (4.27%). The range of increase was greater in the fluctuation type. The gap narrowed from 0.35 percentage points in September to 0.23 percentage points in October. This is the result of short-term and long-term interest rates moving in opposite directions. The new COFIX, which is the standard for the variable type, is 3.18% → 3.31%, and the 5-year bank bond (AAA) linked to the fixed type is 4.53% → 4.34%. This is the result of the market pricing in ‘one more raise and it won’t last long’. The proportion of fixed interest rates in new mortgage loans increased from 34.2% to 38.1%, but 61.9% are still variable interest rates.

## Deposits moved first — 4% term deposits increased from 10.6% to 29.0%

The savings deposit interest rate is 3.62% (+0.17 percentage points), one-year term deposit is 3.77% (+0.20 percentage points), and market-type financial products are 3.83% (+0.14 percentage points). Among term deposits, the proportion receiving an annual interest rate of 4.0-5.0% nearly tripled from 10.6% in September to 29.0% in October, while the 3.0-4.0% range decreased from 70.8% to 53.9%. It is higher in secondary financial institutions. Based on one-year maturity, Mutual Savings Bank is 3.90% and Saemaeul Geumgo is 3.71%. The fact that the deposit interest rate rose 0.17% point while the lending interest rate rose 0.07% point means that the bank's funding costs rose first.

## Balance 2.20% points, new 1.02% points

Based on balance, total receipts are 2.36% and total loans are 4.56%, resulting in an interest rate difference of 2.20 percentage points. It is more than twice the new standard. The balance standard includes demand deposits with low interest rates (0.56%), and the Bank of Korea excludes demand deposits, direct deposit and withdrawal deposits, and negative bank account loans from the new statistics. This is why ‘My loan interest rate is less than 5%’ and ‘The average for October is 5.02%’ are both correct.

## 5 months, 9 months, 15 months — bills that haven't arrived yet

There is an estimate made by the Bank of Korea on the ‘financial stability situation’ in September. When the base interest rate is raised, the balance-based loan interest rate reacts the most after about 5 months, the overall delinquency rate reacts the most after about 15 months, and the delinquency rate for vulnerable household borrowers and small and medium-sized businesses reacts even faster at about 9 months. Substituting the July and August increases, the most painful months for vulnerable borrowers will be April and May 2027 (calculated). The starting line is also high. At the end of the second quarter, the delinquency rate for vulnerable borrowers was 10.39% (0.98% for all households) and 12.71% for vulnerable self-employed borrowers.

## On the 26th, the day before the Monetary Policy Committee meeting

A day before the Monetary Policy Committee meeting on the 26th, the market sees the increase as a fait accompli. The 3-month MSRP (3.323%) and 3-month CD (3.390%) on the 24th are higher than the base interest rate of 3.00% plus 0.25% points. On the other hand, Goldman Sachs predicted a hawkish freeze in its report on the 20th. On the 25th, long-term treasury bonds of 3.632% and 10-year treasury bonds of 3.781% also fell further, and KOSPI plummeted by 5% around 11 a.m. and the exchange rate was around 1,343 won. This is why prices, growth, and financial stability must be weighed in one meeting.

> “Loan interest rates can show different patterns for each product depending on whether they follow short-term or long-term loans” — Kim Seong-jun, head of the financial statistics team at the Bank of Korea

The number to check is three. Is the base interest rate of my loan a COFIX or a 5-year bank bond, when is the interest rate set again, and is the deposit maturity before or after October when the 4% level peaks?

title: It says ‘I am an AI assistant’ — what 200,000 users’ calls are missing is a signed mandate
deck: SK Telecom, KT, LG Uplus and Naver decided on Nov 23 to stop taking customer-service calls placed by AI agents. While calls from a service used by 200,000 people within a month of launch stall at identity checks, the payments market introduced cryptographically signed mandates in September 2025.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: SK Telecom, KT, LG Uplus and Naver said on Nov 23 they will not handle customer-service calls placed by AI agents acting for users, citing the difficulty of identity checks and of confirming delegated authority, and the unclear liability when something is handled wrongly.

Pickle, the service making those calls, passed 200,000 monthly active users within a month of its Oct 14 iOS beta. Reports described restaurants hanging up on AI reservation calls as spam and hospital consultations taking more than twice as long, and Korail has blocked automated programs from its ticket system.

Article 114 of Korea's Civil Act presupposes a declaration of intent by an agent who holds authority, and lawyers generally treat AI agents as tools rather than agents. In payments, by contrast, AP2, published by Google in September 2025, verifies authority, intent and liability through cryptographically signed mandates for intent, cart and payment.
body:
On Nov 23, SK Telecom, KT, LG Uplus and Naver closed their doors in the same direction: customer-service centres will not take calls placed by an AI agent on a user's behalf. Identity checks and confirming the scope of delegated authority are the reasons all four give.

The service placing those calls gathered 200,000 monthly active users within a month of launch. Two hundred thousand delegations arrive at the counter without a single sheet of paper. The payments market has been turning that paper into cryptography for a year; the receiving end of a phone call still has no such format.

![One unsigned delegation letter on a service-counter desk, and beyond it an office where an AI voice spills from a speaker. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/ai-agent-call-mandate-gap-2026.jpg)

## The line four companies drew

When an AI agent calls, SK Telecom checks the account holder's contact number, says a counsellor will call the holder directly, and ends the call. KT tells customers to contact the centre themselves when identity checks are required. LG Uplus does not take calls from AI agents as a rule. Naver adopted a policy of not responding to anyone but the account holder, and will not proceed once an AI identifies itself as 'an AI agent'. Kakao runs no phone support at all, and there is no official integration between KakaoTalk and outside agents.

The four give the same reason. Even when a user has delegated authority, there is no basis for treating the AI as a lawful representative, and if the user disowns a cancellation or refund the AI processed, no one is left to hold responsible. Carriers add that AI agents repeat the same questions and push other customers' consultations back.

## Where 200,000 delegations arrived

Pickle passed 200,000 monthly active users within a month of starting its iOS beta on Oct 14. Ask it to check a gym's membership prices and the AI says 'this is an AI assistant' and makes the call; in a case the JoongAng Ilbo reported on Nov 10, the gym took the call for spam and hung up several times.

The Korea Economic Daily reported a hospital case where repeated AI questions stretched a consultation to more than twice the usual time. Customer-service centres are not the only doors closing. Korail has blocked automated programs from its ticket system, and Kakao has raised the possibility of legal action over a KakaoTalk integration released without prior consultation. At home, Pickle, Buoy and Keyring compete for the same market.

## What is blank is not the price list but the representative field

Article 114 of the Civil Act begins like this: 'A declaration of intent made by an agent within the scope of the agent's authority, showing that it is made on the principal's behalf, is effective directly against the principal.' The clause presupposes a declaration of intent by a person who holds authority.

> "For agency to hold, the party holding the right of representation must have legal personality, but an AI agent is nothing more than a system and a tool." — Lee Sang-jik, attorney at Bae, Kim & Lee, Law Times, Aug 7, 2026

Most lawyers treat an AI agent as a tool, not an agent. What the AI said is attributed to the user, but whether the receiving side can verify that authority during the call is a separate problem. Korean law also has no provision governing a platform's power to control outside agents' access, or the limits of that power. That leaves two options — refuse, or take the call and confirm with the account holder afterwards — and the four companies chose both.

## In payments, the mandate already exists

Payments solved the same problem with a format. Google published the Agent Payments Protocol (AP2) with more than 60 organisations on Sept 16, 2025, and by late October more than 100 had joined. Its core is a mandate — a cryptographically signed record of the user's instruction. An intent mandate states what the user wants, a cart mandate binds the approved basket, and a payment mandate authorises the payment, all written as W3C Verifiable Credentials. The protocol answers three questions: was there authority, does the request match the user's intent, and who is liable when it goes wrong.

The U.S. National Cybersecurity Center of Excellence (NCCoE) at NIST also issued a concept paper on agent identity and authorisation in February and had gathered more than 600 comments by September.

A phone call has no such layer. All a counsellor can check at the start of a call is a voice and the answers to identity questions. In place of a mandate there is a notice — 'I am an AI' — and that notice becomes grounds for refusal.

## If refusal lasts, the door that remains

Refusal is half a solution. Next month SK Telecom will turn its AI service A.Dot into A.Dot All, an action-taking agent, and says it will offer a service like Pickle's. If outside AI is blocked while its own agent places the same calls, the door that remains is one only one company's agent can pass.

Lee Sang-jik said that if a platform allows only its own agent and blocks outside access, questions of competitive restriction or abuse of dominance could arise.

## The ten seconds the next call needs

As agents multiply, what is needed is not a list of four refusals but a delegation signature the other side can verify in the first ten seconds of a call. Payments settled that format a year ago; access inside companies was settled with OAuth. The phone call has not been settled. Until it is, doors close one by one, and a closed door belongs to the company that holds it before it opens again.

factCheck.title: Fact check & sources
factCheck.note: The consultation restrictions at the four companies were confirmed by reports from November 23rd to 24th citing explanations from officials at each company, and we could not find anything disclosed by the company in an official policy document. The statement that 'AI repeats the same question, resulting in a backlog of other customer consultations' and the case that 'hospital consultations took more than twice as long' are reported values ​​based on statements from communications and medical field officials, and are not measured statistics. Pickle's 200,000 monthly active users and the launch of iOS beta on October 14th are figures derived from media reports, and data published by the company has not been confirmed. ‘Calls entrusted to 200,000 people’ refers to the number of subscribers and does not refer to the number of calls handled. Article 114 of the Civil Act is a general legal agency regulation, and there has been no confirmed precedent that it applies directly to AI agents. The views of lawyers Lee Sang-jik and Lee Gwang-wook are statements from individual interviews and are not the authoritative interpretation of the court or government. Concerns about competition restrictions are also the lawyer's personal opinion and do not imply a judgment or investigation by the Fair Trade Commission. AP2 is a payment protocol and is not a standard applied to phone consultations or customer service center identity verification. This article compares the two areas of verification and does not claim that AP2 is the solution to the phone problem. The number of AP2 participating organizations (more than 60 in September 2025, more than 100 at the end of October) is quoted directly from the Google blog. The NIST NCCoE concept paper prioritizes internal corporate agents and leaves external and personal agents as future work, so it should not be read as a certification standard for public Internet phone consultations that has already been established. KORAIL's access blocking and Kakao's suggestion of legal action were facts at the time of reporting on November 17, and it has not been confirmed whether the two sides reached an agreement afterward.

title: The same 61 days, 17 days apart — January 10 and January 27, the two ends of the postponements
deck: China's Commerce Ministry postponed the ban on gallium, germanium and antimony exports to the US until January 27, 2027. The rare earth suspension it extended two weeks earlier ends on January 10. Both reprieves run 61 days, but they start 17 days apart, so they end 17 days apart too — and in between, European dysprosium has risen to 15-19 times the Chinese price.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: On November 24 China's Ministry of Commerce published Notice No. 59, suspending the ban on exports of gallium, germanium and antimony to the United States (paragraph 2 of Notice No. 46 of 2024) from November 28, 2026 to January 27, 2027. The rare earth suspension extended two weeks earlier under Notice No. 58 ends on January 10.

Both reprieves run 61 days. They start 17 days apart, so they end 17 days apart. The April 2025 licensing regime for seven rare earths has never been suspended, and European dysprosium oxide trades at 15-19 times the Chinese price ($3,300-4,200 against $215-220).

Korea buys 89.4% of its rare earth raw materials (January-September 2025) and 99.3% of its permanent magnets, by weight, from China. The government has raised the core minerals list to 51 and the stockpile target to up to 365 days, but the dedicated storage base is only targeted for completion in October 2028.
body:
The Ministry of Commerce of China issued Notice No. 59 of 2026 on November 24. One sentence states that the implementation of paragraph 2 of Notice No. 46 of 2024 will be suspended from November 28 to January 27, 2027.

Paragraph 2 is a provision that, in principle, disallows dual-use exports of gallium, germanium, antimony, and ultra-hard materials to the United States and strengthens the screening of graphite. After being introduced in December 2024, it was postponed from November 2025, and this is the second extension.

![Germanium ingots and stainless steel drums in a bonded warehouse at dawn, and magnetic blocks on shelves. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/gallium-rare-earth-two-deadlines-2027.jpg)

## The same 61 days, 17 days apart

There was a similar notice two weeks earlier. Notice No. 58 of November 9 fixed the suspension of six measures issued in October 2025 to run from November 11, 2026 to January 10, 2027. They cover five heavy rare earths, licensing rules for magnets and targets made outside China with 0.1% or more Chinese rare earths by value, processing equipment and technology, lithium batteries and synthetic graphite anode materials.

The two grace periods are the same length: November 11 to January 10, and November 28 to January 27, are both 61 days. Because they start 17 days apart, they end 17 days apart. That gap is not a product of the negotiations; it comes from the dates on which each suspension originally began.

## What was not suspended

What was not postponed matters more than what was. The April 2025 licensing regime (Notice No. 18) for seven elements - samarium, gadolinium, terbium, dysprosium, lutetium, scandium and yttrium - has never been suspended. Every shipment needs a licence, and where the end use is military or semiconductor the review is longer. Paragraph 1 of Notice No. 46, the ban on exports for US military use, is also not part of the suspension.

## Prices split first

The market did not wait for either deadline. European spot dysprosium oxide was assessed by SMM on November 5 at $3,300-4,200/kg, against $215-220/kg in China the same day: 15 to 19 times. Terbium oxide is $7,300-8,300 in Europe against about $951 in China. Platts put North American dysprosium oxide at $4,100 on October 30, 242% above its first assessment of $1,200 at the end of March.

> "Europe's inventory of heavy rare earths continues to decrease and trading volume is low. Dysprosium, terbium, and gadolinium are valuable, but are close to being unavailable." — SMM, November 5, 2026

Gallium is $228/kg inside China and $440/kg FOB (November 4, SMM). Germanium ingots passed 30,000 yuan/kg for the first time on November 16, and European warehouse material of 99.99% averaged $8,650/kg on November 24. Antimony 0-grade ingots fell to 88,000 yuan a tonne on November 23, while Europe was at $17,500 a tonne on November 6. Licensing made these prices, not supply and demand.

## How much can be made outside China

Benchmark Mineral Intelligence estimates that China makes about 86% of refined gallium and about two-thirds of refined germanium. S&P Global calculated that more than 90% of germanium refining capacity and 91% of primary production are in China, and that an additional 103 tons could be added to the 73 tons of primary capacity outside of China in Canada, the United States, and Korea.

## Korea's numbers

According to the Korea Customs Service, 89.4% of rare earth raw material imports from January to September 2025 are from China. According to the Korea International Trade Association, the dependence on China for rare earth permanent magnets in 2025 is 99.3% by weight and 80% for rare earth metals.

In oxide, the map moved slightly. Of the $89.53 million in rare earth oxide imports from January to July 2026, 21.2% came from the United States, more than double the annual figure in 2025 (9.7%), and the share from China fell from 49.0% to 47.5%. The source of raw materials has changed and the ability to make magnets is different.

The government's answer is inventory and paperwork. On September 23 the resource security plan raised the core minerals list from 38 to 51 (adding 10 rare earths, fluorite, phosphorus and germanium), stockpiled items from 24 to 29, and the target for vulnerable minerals from 180 days to up to 365. Korea has secured more than six months of yttrium and dysprosium and plans to raise that to 18 months. The Saemangum storage base meant to hold it has been pushed back twice, with completion now targeted for October 2028, and the project's 2025 budget execution rate was 17.6%.

## From the plastics side

Antimony is a raw material for antimony trioxide used in flame-retardant ABS/PC compounds. On November 23, the price of antimony trioxide also fell to 73,500 yuan per ton. When the grace period ends and exports to the US are blocked again, the gap with the offshore price widens, and the gap comes down to the cost of flame retardant compounds.

## Two dates left

The two leaders meet again at the G20 in Miami on December 14-15. Then January 10 and January 27 arrive. A suspension does not remove a tariff; it moves the date, and the market has already priced that date in. What a contract writer can do now is put the two dates in as different lead times: rare-earth content against January 10, gallium, germanium and antimony against January 27. Seventeen days is a coincidence made of paperwork, but the day a ship sails is not decided by coincidence.

factCheck.title: Fact check & sources
factCheck.note: Both dates were confirmed in the original notice. No. 59 was published and issued on November 24, 2026, and took effect on November 28, and No. 58 was published from November 11 to January 10, 2027. Note that both grace periods are 61 days long, and the 17-day difference is calculated by including the end dates (61 days from November 11 to January 10, 61 days from November 28 to January 27). The reason for this gap is interpreted to be that the original start dates of the two deferrals were different: November 11, 2025, and the day after November 27, 2025, and the Chinese announcement explaining the two documents together was not confirmed. Prices vary by rating agency. Dysprosium in Europe and China 15 to 19 times is the division of the two values ​​evaluated by SMM on the same day (November 5), and SMM itself stated that it is an asking price and that transactions are rare. Platts' $4,100 (October 30, North America) and 242% increase rate are values ​​quoted from Platts' evaluation in secondary literature, so the original text could not be directly verified. Yuan denominations (germanium 30,000 yuan/kg, antimony 88,000 yuan/t, antimony trioxide 73,500 yuan/t) and dollar denominations (European warehouse $8,650/kg, European antimony $17,500/t) were not converted using the exchange rate. The dates are different, so this is not a comparison of two markets on the same day. Korea's 89.4% was based on Seoul Economic Daily and Maeil Business News articles that reported the Korea Customs Service's January to September 2025 values, and some media outlets wrote this as 2026, but were unable to directly check the Korea Customs Service's original data. Permanent magnet 99.3%, metal 80% is a value quoted by the Korea International Trade Association based on weight for 2025. The proportion of oxide imports (US 21.2%, China 47.5%) is limited to rare earth oxides and is not in the same range as all rare earths or magnets. The 6-month stockpile and 18-month expansion plans are reported values ​​quoted from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, and the stockpile base schedule and execution rate are reported values ​​submitted to the National Assembly by the Korea Mine & Reclamation Corporation. The proportion of gallium and germanium production is different estimates from Benchmark and S&P Global. The statement that antimony trioxide is a raw material for flame-retardant ABS/PC compounds is a common fact in the industry, and there is no numerical data confirming the causality between this delay and the cost of flame-retardant compounds.

title: Year-end tax settlement with a real deadline of December 31st — Card limit of 4 million won and deductions that disappear after that day
deck: Year-end tax settlement for 2026 will be made in January 2027. However, the irreversible date is December 31st. The basic credit card income deduction limit is 3 to 4 million won depending on the number of children, pension savings and IRP are 9 million won, and the marriage tax credit is the last this year.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: Year-end tax settlement for 2026 will be made in January 2027, but the irreversible deadline is December 31. Pension savings, IRP payments, card use, marriage registration, donations, and monthly rent expenses all end on that day.

Starting in 2026, the basic limit for income deductions such as credit cards will increase depending on the number of children. If the total salary is less than 70 million won, it is 3 million won for no children, 3.5 million won for one child, and 4 million won for two or more children.

A tax deduction of up to KRW 9 million including pension savings of KRW 6 million and IRP is applied, and 16.5% of total salary under KRW 55 million and 13.2% of gross salary exceeding KRW 55 million are applied. If you pay 9 million won, you will receive up to 1,485,000 won back.

The September 2026 government tax law amendment (monthly rent of 12 million won, 17% for young people) has not been passed by the National Assembly, so it has not been confirmed whether it will be applied in 2026.
body:
November 25, 2026, there are 36 days left until December 31. The company will make year-end tax settlements for 2026 in January 2027. However, the actual date by which office workers have to make a decision is one month before that. There are some items that cannot be returned after December 31, and the changed deduction standards starting from 2026 only apply to this year's expenditures.

The National Tax Service has been operating a ‘year-end tax settlement preview’ on Hometax since October 28th. This service runs until December 18th. The expected tax amount to be settled in January 2027 is calculated by adding the card usage amount from January to September to the expected spending from October to December, but it is not a confirmed amount.

## Four things that have changed in 2026

Among the revised laws promulgated on December 23, 2025 and April 21, 2026, there are four items that affect the settlement of wage and salary income earners. Since they all apply from the 2026 tax period (or payment/use in 2026), the standards are different from the attribution settlement in 2025.

|items|Attribution in 2025|Attribution in 2026|
|---|---|---|
|Basic income deduction limit for credit cards, etc. (gross salary 70 million won or less)|3 million won|3.5 million won per child / 4 million won for 2 or more children|
|Basic income deduction limit for credit cards, etc. (gross salary exceeding 70 million won)|2.5 million won|2.75 million won per child / 3 million won for 2 or more children|
|Age eligible for child tax credit|Ages 8 and above|Age 9 or older (excluding those born in 2017)|
|Education Expense Tax Credit|School fees for preschool children|Additional arts and sports facility tuition fees for 1st and 2nd grade elementary school students|
|Monthly rent tax deduction|1 head of household|Spouses with different addresses can also deduct each (couple 10 million won combined)|
|Hometown Love Donation|15% for exceeding 100,000 won|Over 100,000 won ~ 200,000 won or less 40%|

The threshold and deduction rate for credit card deductions remain the same. Annual spending must exceed 25% of total salary, and the excess amount is subject to 15% for credit cards, 30% for check cards and cash receipts, and 40% for traditional markets and public transportation.

## The limit of 1 million won is not the tax of 1 million won.

The extent to which the limit is increased and the actual tax reduction are different. According to estimates by the Ministry of Finance and Economy, even if a worker with a total salary of 60 million won and two dependent children meets the entire expanded limit, the tax burden reduction is about 150,000 won. This is because it is the amount multiplied by the increased limit by your marginal tax rate (15% if you are in the 15% range).

There are many cases where limit expansion is invalid. For households whose card deduction calculation does not reach the existing limit (3 million won), the money they receive in return will not change even if the limit is increased. If your total salary is 50 million won, you would need to spend about 32.5 million won to meet the 3 million won limit with a credit card alone. The amount is the threshold of 12.5 million won plus 3 million won ÷ 0.15.

The determination of the remaining period depends on the payment method. If you have not yet exceeded 25% of your total salary, it is better to take advantage of credit card benefits up to that point, and if you have already exceeded 25% of your total salary, it is better to transfer future expenses to a check card or cash receipt, as the deduction amount is larger.

## Pension savings/IRP 9 million won, payment due December 31

Pension savings are subject to a tax deduction of up to 6 million won per year, up to 9 million won including IRP. If the total salary is less than 55 million won, 16.5% including local income tax is applied, and if it exceeds it, 13.2% is applied. If you reach 9 million won, it will be reduced by up to 1.485 million won and 1.188 million won, respectively. Payment must be made by December 31 to be recognized as vested in 2026.

The benefits in return must also be checked. If you cancel early, the tax deducted so far will be reimposed as other income tax. If you withdraw from IRP for the purpose of purchasing or renting a house, 16.5% is applied, and if you withdraw to meet pension requirements, 5.5% (age 55-69) is applied. Even for the same withdrawal, the tax rate increases three times depending on the reason.

## This year is the last deduction.

The marriage tax credit is 500,000 won for each couple and a maximum of 1 million won combined. Under the current law, it only applies to cases where marriage registration is completed by December 31, and this year is the last year. The government is pursuing a plan to switch to a financial support method starting in 2027, but procedures for legal reform and budget security remain.

Only expenses for 2026 are recognized for donations, medical expenses, and monthly rent. If documents proving expenditure, such as contracts, transfer details, and donation receipts, are not submitted within December, they will be excluded from the settlement in January 2027.

## Not yet confirmed

The tax law revision bill confirmed at the Cabinet meeting on September 1, 2026 includes raising the monthly rent tax credit limit to 12 million won per year, applying 17% to young people aged 15 to 34, and increasing the income standard for basic deduction for dependents to 3 million won in income and 7.5 million won in total salary. It has not been passed by the National Assembly and no time has been set for its application. After the decision was made in early December, there is a difference in the supplementary provisions as to whether the 2026 portion will be applied.

The National Tax Service has not yet announced the opening date of the simplified settlement service in January 2027 and the deadline for company submission. The last settlement was held on January 15th, but it varies every year. The two dates must be confirmed with the National Tax Service notice from December to January.

## Three decisions to make before December 31st

First, decide how much of the 9 million won pension savings and IRP will be filled. Second, check whether card usage exceeds 25% of total salary and decide on a payment method for the remaining expenses. Third, prepare proof of dated items such as marriage registration, donations, and monthly rent. All three are not retroactive past December 31st.

factCheck.title: Fact check & sources
factCheck.note: The most confusing part is the ‘attribution year’. Settlement made in January 2026 will be attributed to 2025, and amounts spent and paid between January and December 2026 will be attributed to 2026 and will be settled in January 2027. The expansion of card deduction limits and changes to education expenses and monthly rent apply starting from use and payment in 2026, so they did not apply to settlement in early 2026. The actual savings (about 150,000 won) from the 1 million won limit increase is estimated by the Ministry of Finance and Economy and varies depending on the individual tax base range. The tax law amendment bill for September 2026 (monthly rent of 12 million won, youth 17%, income standard increase for dependents) has not been passed by the National Assembly and was not treated as a confirmed fact in the main text. The opening date of the simplified settlement service and the company's submission deadline in January 2027 were not announced by the National Tax Service, so they were marked as 'unconfirmed'.

title: Only 40,323 of 16.3 Million Switched — What Three Years at Half Price Changes, and What It Doesn't
deck: The indemnity contract conversion discount announced by the Financial Services Commission on November 19, 2026 and implemented on the 23rd, provides a 50% discount on 5th generation insurance premiums for 3 years to 16.3 million people who signed 1st and 2nd generation contracts before March 2013. In the example of a woman in her 60s, the amount will be reduced by 5.59 million won for 3 years, but from the 4th year, it will be the full amount, and the non-critical out-of-pocket cost will rise from 30% to 50%. As of the end of October, there were 40,323 1st and 2nd generation contracts that were replaced on their own.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: The indemnity contract conversion discount and optional discount special contract were implemented on November 23, 2026. The target population is approximately 16.3 million first- and second-generation households with no conditions for subscription or re-subscription before March 2013, and applications are due until May 22, 2027. If you switch to the 5th generation, 50% of the 5th generation insurance premium will be reduced for 3 years, and the conversion is, in principle, done without separate screening.

In the Financial Services Commission's example of a woman in her 60s, 176,982 won per month for a 1st generation becomes 43,241 won for a 5th generation, or 21,620 won when applying a 3-year discount. The difference in payment for 3 years is 5,593,032 won, and from the 4th year onwards, the full amount is 43,241 won. If the insurance premium remains the same, the total difference over 5 years is 8.8 million won.

For the 5th generation, the non-severe uncovered care limit is 10 million won per year, the co-payment rate is 50%, and manual therapy, extracorporeal shock wave, and uncovered care injections are excluded from the special contract. If you spend 2 million won per year on manual therapy (assuming a 5% self-pay for the first generation), you will pay an additional 5.7 million won over 3 years to offset the savings. By the end of October, the number of contracts moved from the 1st and 2nd generation to the 5th generation was 40,323 (9 non-life insurance companies, 8.7%).
body:
![Hands holding two insurance policies side by side, a calculator on the table and a bundle of three years’ worth of receipts. One book is thick and one book is thin — premiums and coverage move in opposition to each other. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/silson-gen5-switch-50-percent-3years-2026.jpg)

From November 23, 2026, among the 1st and 2nd generation indemnity health insurance policies signed up before March 2013, contracts without re-enrollment conditions (approximately 16.3 million people) will be able to transfer to the 5th generation. If you switch, 50% of the 5th generation insurance premium will be reduced for 3 years. Applications are due until May 22, 2027. However, before the system opened, there were 40,323 1st and 2nd generation contracts that were voluntarily moved to the 5th generation by the end of October.

## 40,323 cases out of 16.3 million people

The cumulative number of 5th generation subscriptions from 9 non-life insurance companies as of the end of October was 461,308. 291,563 new cases and 104,583 4th generation re-enrollments accounted for 85.9%. There were 15,662 contracts transferred from the first generation, and 24,661 contracts transferred from the second generation, or 8.7%. Even though it is a product announced to have insurance premiums at least 50% cheaper than the 1st and 2nd generation, the choice of 16.3 million people was in the 40,000 range before the half price was added for 3 years.

## Half price: 5.59 million won for 3 years

The starting point is the case of a woman in her 60s that the Financial Services Commission used as a standard for six large non-life insurance companies. The monthly insurance premium of 176,982 won for the 1st generation becomes 43,241 won if moved to the 5th generation, and 21,620 won if the 3-year discount is added. 87.8% lower than before. The 3-year payment amount is 778,320 won, or if left as is, it is 6,371,352 won. The difference of 5,593,032 won is the size of this system. The second generation (126,773 won per month) also becomes the same at 21,620 won after the discount.

Discount applies only to 5th generation insurance premiums. From the fourth year onwards, the full amount of 43,241 won will be paid. If set for 5 years, the difference is KRW 8.8 million, or KRW 10,618,920 for maintenance vs. KRW 1,816,104 for conversion (assuming the insurance premium remains the same). However, for the 5th generation, the coverage change cycle is up to 5 years, so coverage is checked again when you re-enroll.

## Declining side: Non-severe non-benefit coverage

In the 5th generation, the annual limit for non-critical uncovered care benefits changes from 50 million won to 10 million won, and the self-payment rate changes from 30% to 50%. For outpatient clinics, patients pay the greater of 50% of the treatment fee or 50,000 won. Manual therapy, extracorporeal shock waves, and non-covered injections are completely excluded from the non-severe special contract. On the other hand, the limit of 50 million won and 30% co-payment is maintained for severe uncovered care cases (special calculations such as cancer, cerebrovascular disease, heart disease, etc.), and for hospitalization in tertiary or general hospitals, the insurance company pays more for the portion exceeding 5 million won per year.

The break-even point is different here. Assuming the 1st generation self-payment rate is 5% and spending 2 million won per year on manual therapy, the current cost is 100,000 won, and the 5th generation will pay 2 million won. It costs 1.9 million won per year, or 5.7 million won over 3 years. This is a number that erases the savings of 5.59 million won. If you spend 5 million won per year on non-critical non-benefit benefits, you will pay 1 million won more per year, or 3 million won over 3 years, just by increasing the out-of-pocket rate by 20% points. Contractors who rarely visit hospitals are left with the same amount of 5.59 million won.

## Four conditions for the discount to end

- Same policy: If the indemnity is a special contract of another insurance, the discount ends when the main contract or special contract is canceled or reduced within 6 months before the conversion application date or during the discount period. This does not apply to contracts with different security numbers. An exception is made if cancellation is made before November 19, the date of the system announcement.
- Cancellation is done once: a consideration period of 2 business days, within 3 months without conditions, and within 3 to 6 months only if no insurance money has been received. If you withdraw, you cannot use the conversion discount again, and you may be subject to review even if you try to convert without the discount.
- Timing by insurance company: Most participate, but the window and start date are different. Some insurance companies plan to implement it on February 1, 2027.
- Optional discount special contract: Maintaining the contract but excluding only the options. Option 1 15-20%, Option 2 2-4%, Option 3 9-17%, if all are selected, the first generation is about 37% and the second generation is about 27%. You can only sign up once, and all additions, cancellations, and re-registration after withdrawal are blocked.

## Where to change it to my number

The first tab of Insight Brief's [3 types of insurance calculators](https://insightbriefnews.com/insurance.html) puts maintenance, 4th generation, and 5th generation side by side with total annual expenditure (insurance + deductible). If you enter salary/non-benefit medical expenses, serious/excluded coverage items, and non-benefit receipts for the previous year, even non-benefit premiums are reflected. If you turn on the '50% discount for 3 years of contract conversion' switch in the input box, the annual expenditures after the discount is applied for the 1st to 3rd years and the annual expenditures after returning to the full amount from the 4th year are displayed, and the accumulated difference for the 3rd and 5th years is also compared at once.

> The discount is attached to the 5th generation insurance premium, and the loss is attached to my hospital expenses. The value of 3 years and a half is the difference between the two.

You should check whether you are eligible by signing up for My Insurance (cont.insure.or.kr) and ask the insurance company if there are any conditions for re-enrolling. There are three things necessary for judgment. Insurance premiums paid now, indemnity health insurance payments received over the past three years, and treatment plan for the next three years. The first two come from the app, and I only know the third.

factCheck.note: 16.3 million people, 3 years 50%, application period, women in their 60s. Example (176,982 won → 43,241 won → 21,620 won) is based on the Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory Service press release (2026-11-19) and Q&A. The 5th generation structure (10 million won per year for non-severe cases, 50% self-pay, 50 million won for severe cases, 30%, 5 million won per year for hospitalization in tertiary and general hospitals, 10% accident-free discount, non-benefit differential system) is based on the Financial Services Commission's press release on the launch of the 5th generation (2026-05-06). The 461,308 cases at the end of October and the 40,323 cases (8.7%) of first- and second-generation conversions are the prices received by consumer-produced newspapers from the insurance industry, based on nine non-life insurance companies, and could not be cross-checked with official statistics from financial authorities. The difference between 5,593,032 won in 3 years and 8,800,000 won in 5 years is a value calculated assuming that the insurance premium in the example above remains the same, and the break-even figure of 2 million won per year for manual therapy is a calculation assuming the first generation deductible rate is 5% (the initial indemnity deductible rate is 0 to 10% for each product). The discount rate for each option of the optional discount special contract varies depending on the insurance company and product and can be adjusted within the range of ±25% on a yearly basis. The implementation date (2027-02-01) for some insurance companies is a single reporting standard. The contract conversion discount is a limited-time system that is reviewed for extension after 6 months of operation, and it has not been confirmed whether applications can be made after May 22, 2027.

title: Living expenses were protected up to 2.5 million won, but not observed for 3 years — 150,000 personal rehabilitation cases
deck: There were 124,703 personal rehabilitation applications from January to September 2026. Looking at the cases handled last year alone, 44,914 cases were dismissed, canceled, or abolished. The rate of abolition before approval rose from 10.1% to 15.2%, and the average reimbursement rate for approved cases fell to 42.2%. 17.6% points vary depending on the court of jurisdiction.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: Based on the monthly court statistics report, the number of personal rehabilitation applications from January to September 2026 was 124,703, an increase of 10.6% compared to the same period last year. In the 2025 processing results (2026 Judicial Yearbook), there were 92,502 cases of approval, 15,433 cases of dismissal before commencement, 16,542 cases of cancellation/revocation before approval, and 12,939 cases of abolition after approval. Including rejections and abolitions, there were 44,914 cases, or 30.1% of the applications received that year.

From January to August 2026, there were 12,292 cases of dismissal before commencement (+36.7% of the same period last year), and 13,398 cases of cancellation/revocation before approval (+29.9%), which was two or three times the increase rate of applications (12.2%). The national average reimbursement rate for licensed cases decreased from 47.9% in 2021 to 42.2% in 2025, and by court, it increased by 17.6 percentage points from 37.0% at the Ulsan District Court to 54.6% at the Gwangju Rehabilitation Court.

The system has expanded. On February 1, 2026, the living expenses account (prohibition of seizure of 2.5 million won per month) was implemented, and on January 30, the special exemption for vulnerable debtors was expanded to 50 million won of debt principal. The number of people confirmed for debt restructuring by the NHRCK was 97,199 in the first half of 2026, an increase of 56.1% in three years. However, the gap between completion rate and repayment rate has not yet improved.
body:
On November 19, the Seoul Bankruptcy Court posted a report on the results of a statistical survey on personal bankruptcy for the first half of 2026. Six days ago, on the 17th, the monthly court statistics report released the cumulative figures for January to September. If you put the two statistics side by side, the center of this year's personal rehabilitation story is not the explosion of applications. The fact is that three out of ten people who join leave before completing three years.

## 124,703 cases were received

Based on the monthly court statistics report, the number of personal rehabilitation applications from January to September 2026 was 124,703, a 10.6% increase from the same period last year (112,689 cases). Personal bankruptcies increased by 6.5% to 32,844. Last year, 83.6% of the annual number of applications (149,147) were filled in 9 months, so this year is likely to be the highest ever.

The problem lies after that. According to the 2025 processing results published in the 2026 Judicial Yearbook, there were 92,502 cases of approval, 15,433 cases of dismissal before the commencement decision, 16,542 cases of cancellation or abolition after commencement but before approval, and 12,939 cases of mid-term abolition after approval. Including dismissals and revocations, there were 44,914 cases, or 30.1% of the number filed that year. This ratio is approximate because filing and processing are not the same batch of cases, but the direction is clear.

This year, the departure is faster. From January to August, the number of cases dismissed before the start decision was 12,292, an increase of 36.7% from the same period last year, and the number of cancellations or cancellations before approval was 13,398, an increase of 29.9%. This is two or three times the increase in applications of 12.2% during the same period. The number of people who dropped out before and after the start, as reported by the Seoul Shinmun on August 9 using data from the National Court Administration, was 26,429 in the first half of the year alone.

> Among the personal rehabilitation cases processed in 2025, there were 44,914 cases that ended in dismissal, cancellation, or abolition. It is 30.1% of applications that year.

![Application forms, payment forms, calculators and calendars piled up on the table late at night — the repayment amount for personal rehabilitation is determined by subtracting the cost of living recognized by the court from income. Even if the rest is shaken for just one month, three years are lost. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/personal-rehabilitation-44914-dropout-2026.jpg)

## Pay it off over 3 years with the remaining money.

The structure is simple. The repayment amount is determined by ‘disposable income’, which is calculated by subtracting living expenses, taxes, and insurance premiums recognized by the court from income. According to a report by the Seoul Bankruptcy Court analyzing 10,840 cases initiated in the first half of 2025, the median total debt was 96.96 million won, the median monthly income was 2.36 million won, and the median repayment rate upon approval was 33.2%. 75.5% were salary earners and 78.2% were single-person households. In 58.5% of cases, the cost of living was recognized as 'less than 60% of the median income of a single-person household' (KRW 1,435,208 in 2025), and in 74.7% of cases there were no additional living expenses.

So, if the scope of recognition of dependents becomes narrower than expected, the repayment amount goes up immediately. As explained by a court official quoted by the Seoul Shinmun, abandonment occurs because the request to resubmit the repayment plan cannot be met. The Seoul Bankruptcy Court's statistics point in the same direction, stating that the first cause of personal bankruptcy is increased living expenses (48.7%), and the second is unemployment and decreased income (45.7%). When your income fluctuates, the first thing that is cut off is repayment.

## Same law, different answer

The national average reimbursement rate for approved cases fell from 47.9% in 2021 to 42.2% in 2025. However, by court in 2025, Ulsan District Court was 37.0%, Seoul Bankruptcy Court was 37.8%, Busan Bankruptcy Court was 41.6%, Suwon Bankruptcy Court was 42.5%, Incheon District Court was 44.7%, Daegu Bankruptcy Court was 48.6%, Cheongju District Court was 49.6%, and Gwangju Bankruptcy Court was 54.6%, with the highest and lowest difference being 17.6 percentage points. This is the figure released by Rep. Joo Jin-woo on October 9 after analyzing data submitted to the National Court Administration. This gap has been repeated for the fifth year, reaching 16.4%p in 2021 and 18.7%p in 2024. As of 2024, the rate of abolition within one year of approval was 1.6% in Ulsan and 6.1% in Cheongju, a difference of 3.8 times.

The speed also varies. According to a site reported by YTN in March, the average time it took for the Daegu District Court to decide on opening was over 460 days, while for other courts it was 3 to 6 months. With the opening of the Daejeon, Daegu, and Gwangju rehabilitation courts on March 1, the number of rehabilitation courts increased to six. Increasing the number of courts is a remedy aimed at the speed problem. There is still no cure for the repayment rate gap.

## Increased Safety Net

The system became wider this year. With the revision of the Civil Execution Act Enforcement Decree on February 1, a living expenses account (one account per person) was created that prevents seizure of up to 2.5 million won per month, and the minimum amount prohibiting seizure of salary claims also increased from 1.85 million won to 2.5 million won. From January 30, the special exemption for vulnerable debtors under the Financial Services Commission has been expanded to a debt principal amount of 50 million won.

The doors outside the courthouse were also widened. The number of people confirmed for debt restructuring by the NHRCK was 97,199 in the first half of 2026 alone, more than half of the number in 2025 (189,062) and an increase of 56.1% from 2022. As of the end of September, 221,160 people and 34.9066 trillion won had applied for the New Start Fund, and 156,660 people had pledged, and the average purchase-type principal reduction rate was 74%.

## Two bills

The debtor's bill is time. If it is abolished before three years, the money paid so far will be absorbed as interest, and the debt will remain almost the same. The creditor's bill is the recovery rate. The average repayment rate of 42.2% is 5.7 percentage points lower than five years ago, and according to statistics from the Seoul Bankruptcy Court, the number of cases with a repayment rate of less than 20% has increased to 25.1%. The rate of repayment of the entire principal is 5.3%.

Rep. Joo Jin-woo called for consistent repayment standards and review systems, saying, “The justification for a debtor’s recovery should not be a license to sacrifice creditors’ legitimate property rights.” On the other side, it is believed that the stigma and lack of information about bankruptcy pushes people who lack the ability to repay into personal rehabilitation. There is a Seoul Shinmun report on a case in which a debtor worth 20 million won, who was eligible for a delay of up to 6 months through rapid debt restructuring, chose personal rehabilitation by paying a fee of 6 million won, but the qualification disappeared as soon as he applied. As the number of systems has increased, it is still the responsibility of the private sector to tell people which door is theirs.

Some things remain unconfirmed. The annual confirmed figures for 2026 have been released from the Judicial Yearbook since December, and detailed figures from the report for the first half of 2026 published on November 19 were not confirmed within the scope of the original disclosure. When the two data come out, it will be determined whether the number of people who dropped out this year exceeds 50,000 and whether the gap in repayment rates has narrowed.

title: 566,665 TOPIK Applicants and 20 Million Visitors: How K-Pop and K-Dramas Turned Korean Learning Into a Real Economic Engine
deck: Korea broke two records six weeks apart in late 2026: a record number of people signed up to be tested on their Korean, and a record number of foreigners showed up to spend money in the country. The link between them is real — but smaller, and messier, than the headline numbers suggest.
author: Insight Brief Desk
summary: TOPIK applications reached 566,665 in 2025, 2.7 times the 2015 level, and 564,606 had already applied by 30 September 2026 (+10.2% year on year, 94 countries). From 2027 the test runs 15 times a year, and the government targets one million applicants a year by 2030.

Korea passed 20 million foreign visitors for the first time on 12 November 2026, and tourist card spending from January to September reached 15.94 trillion won (+47.7%). Spending per arrival rose about 21.5%, twice the growth in arrivals.

Hallyu content is the single largest stated trigger for interest in visiting Korea (42.3%), and the BTS concert analysis is striking — 8.7 days and 3.53 million won per foreign attendee — but the widely quoted 35-fold and 38-fold local surges compare different populations and scopes, and no agency decomposes how much of the 20 million is down to content.
body:
On 29 September, Korea's education ministry published a number that would have read as a misprint ten years ago. In 2025, 566,665 people applied to take TOPIK, the Test of Proficiency in Korean — the state-run exam that has existed since 1997. That is 2.7 times the 206,768 applicants of 2015, and the highest annual total on record. Of the 2025 figure, 319,192 applied from 88 countries outside Korea.

Not everyone who applies sits the paper. In 2025, 543,600 applied for the paper-based test and 421,046 actually took it. The gap matters later in this story: the number that travels in headlines is demand for a certificate, not the number of people who earned one.

Six weeks after that release, on 12 November, the culture ministry announced a second record. Korea had received its 20 millionth foreign visitor of the year — the first time an annual total has crossed that line. The ministry did not wait for New Year's Eve to say so: cumulative arrivals stood at a provisional 19.97 million on 11 November, and with a daily average of roughly 64,000, it declared the milestone on the day it expected to pass it.

Two ministries, two units, one story. The question worth asking is how much of the money that arrives with those 20 million people is being pulled in by a language that 566,665 people signed up to be tested on.

![An evening Korean-language class in Seoul. Adult learners from many countries work through listening and reading sections while a concert screen glows beyond the window — the two ends of the same pipeline. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/topik-566665-20-million-visitors-korean-learning-economy.jpg)

## A national exam that became a bottleneck

The 2026 numbers have not slowed. As of 30 September 2026, 564,606 people had applied for that year's tests — up 10.2% from the same point a year earlier — at 375 test sites in 94 countries, against 370 sites in 89 countries in 2025.

Demand has outgrown the calendar, and the government now says so in writing. In the same 29 September announcement, the education ministry and the National Institute for International Education laid out a plan to run TOPIK 15 times a year from 2027: paper-based tests six times, internet-based tests (IBT) six times, and the speaking test three times. A full redesign built on AI and digital assessment takes effect in 2029, with an explicit target of one million applicants a year by 2030.

The ministry's own diagnosis is blunt. It cites "limited test opportunities relative to demand at home and abroad", universities asking for a test of actual communication rather than memorised patterns, and cheating methods that have become more sophisticated. The IBT, introduced in 2023 and run in 12 countries including Korea in 2025, is the pressure valve. For now it is a small one: 22,531 of the 566,665 applicants in 2025 chose it.

## Vietnam overtook China. Uzbekistan grew elevenfold.

Look at where applications come from and this stops being a story about fandom.

Among paper-based tests in 2025, the largest single bloc was inside Korea itself: 224,408 applicants sat at domestic sites — foreign residents, exchange students, workers. Country rankings exclude them, which is why the numbers below look smaller than the headline.

Outside Korea, Vietnam became the largest source for the first time with 83,884 applicants, overtaking China at 70,267. In 2021 the order was reversed and the gap was huge: China 76,657, Vietnam 21,192. China's figure has since fallen about 8%, while Vietnam's has roughly quadrupled.

The fastest growth is in Central Asia. Uzbekistan went from 3,820 applicants in 2021 to 41,844 in 2025 — eleven times as many, and now the fourth-largest source in the world. Nepal grew 2.9-fold and Kazakhstan 2.7-fold over the same period. Japan, the third-largest source, rose from 40,957 to 49,290.

Read together, these are labour and education corridors, not streaming charts: Vietnamese and Uzbek students heading for Korean universities and factories, Mongolians and Myanmar nationals following the same route, and a Chinese market that has matured and slightly contracted.

## What a score actually buys

TOPIK is not a hobbyist's certificate. The education ministry describes it as the national test used for studying in Korea, for obtaining residence status, and for employment in Korea and abroad.

That is why the test calendar became an economic question. A student in Hanoi who cannot get a seat cannot finish a university application on time. A worker in Tashkent who needs a score to turn a job offer into a visa is waiting on the same scarce slots as a drama fan in Tokyo. When the ministry promises 15 sittings a year from 2027, it is promising to unblock applications and hiring, not only to satisfy curiosity.

## 20 million visitors, and spending that grew twice as fast

Between January and September 2026, 17.11 million foreigners arrived, 21.5% more than a year earlier. Their tourism spending — card spending compiled by the culture ministry — reached 15.94 trillion won, about $11.8 billion at 1,346.6 won to the dollar, up 47.7% from 10.79 trillion won.

Spending grew more than twice as fast as arrivals. Per arrival that works out to roughly 932,000 won (about $690), against 767,000 won (about $570) a year earlier — an increase of about 21.5% (Insight Brief calculation from the ministry's figures).

The growth also spread beyond Seoul. Arrivals through non-metropolitan airports reached 3.24 million in the first nine months, 19.0% of the total and up 37.4% year on year; sea ports handled 1.58 million, 9.2% of arrivals, up 14.5%.

"Crossing 20 million foreign tourists is the starting point for leaping forward as an irreplaceable tourism power," culture minister Chae Hwi-young said on 12 November, adding that the government would prepare capacity for a 30-million era.

## Content decides where the plane lands

The ministry is careful to spread the credit: visa waivers, more direct flights to regional airports, campaigns against price gouging, and a task force chaired by the president. But it keeps returning to content, and the survey data supports the emphasis.

In the Korea Culture and Tourism Institute's 2025 foreign visitor survey (third-quarter preliminary results), 42.3% of respondents named Hallyu content as the reason they became interested in visiting Korea — the single largest trigger. A separate Korea Tourism Organization survey of potential visitors in 2024 found that 45.2% said they came to know Korea as a travel destination by watching Korean programmes.

The 2026 Overseas Hallyu Survey, covering 27,400 respondents in 30 markets, put favourability toward Korean cultural content at 69.7%. Asked what is popular in their own country, respondents ranked Korean food first (55.1%), then music (54.0%), beauty (52.6%) and drama (51.3%). And 65% said Hallyu has a positive influence on their purchases of Korean products and services, up from 58% three years earlier.

None of that is a causal estimate. Interest is not a booking, and in 2026 the booking was also pushed by a visa-free window for Chinese group tours, short-haul flights re-routed during a fuel-price spike, and an exchange rate that made Korea relatively cheaper for Japanese travellers. The defensible version of the claim is narrower than "K-pop built Korean tourism": content raises the odds that someone already thinking about a trip chooses Korea.

## The BTS test case: 35 times, 38 times, and what the numbers leave out

The most quoted figures in this debate come from two BTS concerts. Around the Gwanghwamun show on 21 March and the Goyang stadium shows on 9, 11 and 12 April 2026, the culture ministry, the Korea Culture and Tourism Institute and the Korea Tourism Organization surveyed foreign attendees and analysed telecom and card data near the venues.

Foreign visitors to the Gwanghwamun concert stayed 8.7 days and spent 3.53 million won each (about $2,620), against 6.1 days and 2.45 million won (about $1,820) for the average foreign visitor in the first quarter — 1.4 times the stay and 1.4 times the spending. Goyang attendees stayed 7.4 days and spent 2.91 million won.

Then the neighbourhood numbers. In Daehwa-dong, the district beside the Goyang stadium, foreign visitors over the three concert days rose from 1,397 in the comparable period of 2025 to 48,581 — 35 times. Foreign card spending there rose from 8.9 million won to 337.8 million won (about $251,000), 38 times.

Those multiples travel well on social media and poorly in a methodology seminar. In October, a lawmaker's office obtained the underlying data and the Hankook Ilbo reported that the two agencies had counted different things. The research institute's on-site survey covered 2,328 visitors, 95.4% of whom attended the concert; the tourism organization's telecom and card data could not distinguish concert-goers from other foreigners. The per-person spending figure includes airfare, accommodation, concert tickets and merchandise — a whole trip, not a local spend — while the district-level card figure covers only spending in that neighbourhood. And the 35-fold comparison is the same three weekdays year on year, with no control for anything else that changed.

The lawmaker's conclusion was procedural: Korea needs a standard framework for measuring K-culture events. Until it has one, 35 and 38 are best read as an upper bound on enthusiasm, not a multiplier to plan budgets with.

## Screens that turn into queues

The softer evidence is a string of site-level jumps that all point the same way.

Netflix's animated film KPop Demon Hunters passed 300 million views in September 2025 — the first title on the platform to do so — and "Golden", from its soundtrack, became the first song from an animated film to top the Billboard Hot 100. The National Museum of Korea, whose aesthetics the film borrows and whose related goods sold out on arrival, recorded 6.5 million visitors in 2025, the most since it opened in 1945.

The drama When Life Gives You Tangerines did the same thing at smaller scale in Jeju. Jeju Tourism Organization data comparing the two months before and after its March 2025 release show navigation arrivals at Gimnyeong Beach rising from 2,442 to 4,775 (up 96%) and at Jeju Mokgwana from 198 to 347 (up 75%), while social media mentions of haenyeo — the island's women divers — rose about 41%, from a monthly average of 5,000 to 7,460.

## Where the arithmetic runs out

Two things none of this establishes.

First, nobody has decomposed the 20 million. The ministry's own list of causes includes visa policy, flights, fuel prices, exchange rates and marketing alongside content. The share of arrivals that would not have happened without a drama is unknown, and no Korean agency publishes an estimate.

Second, "Korean learning" has no measured economic value yet. No Korean agency publishes the size of the Korean-language education market or its contribution to output. What exists is test demand (566,665 applicants), the purposes the test serves, and the spending of the people who arrive — three separate series that are suggestive together and conclusive only in pieces.

Researchers make the same point about local effects. At a conference in Jeju in August 2026, Kim Yong-hee, a business professor at Sunmoon University, argued that the tangerine drama's effect on the island's tourism could not be separately identified, that the national evidence for "content leads to visits" is consistent, and that as much as a third of tourist spending in Jeju leaks out of the region because the production and supply chain sit elsewhere.

## What to watch in 2027

Three dates matter. From 2027, TOPIK runs 15 times a year, which will show whether the constraint was the calendar or the willingness to pay. In 2029 the AI-based redesign takes effect, changing what a score means to universities and employers. And by 2030 the government wants one million applicants a year — roughly double today's level, in a market where Vietnam, Uzbekistan and Japan, not China, now drive growth.

If visitors keep arriving while spending per head grows faster than headcount, the interesting question stops being whether K-culture sells Korea. It becomes whether Korea can sell the next layer — the language course, the degree, the job — to the people the content brought to the airport.
