title: Futures fell 12%, while spot premiums are at record highs — a split week for paper and warehouses
deck: While copper futures tumbled 12% in a week, Chinese mass production premiums hit a new all-time high of $500 per ton. Gold and silver were pushed to a 14-month low, Nafta fell 9.5%, but PC stopped at within 3%. The announced price followed the signal that this week's decline was not about demand but 'cash-making selling'.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: Copper futures collapsed to LME spot -10.14% and SHFE -12.1%, and in the same week, the mass production premium hit an all-time high from $360 to $500, and the Shanghai spot premium also hit 7,250 yuan per ton. Inventory increased by only 1.4% in LME and SMM social inventory decreased by 11.3%, showing that the cause of the decline was liquidation of positions, not volume.

Gold fell for 3 consecutive weeks at -8.92%, a 52-week low, silver -15.41%, Naphtha -9.53%, and WTI -5.17%. This week, in which the global and Chinese markets fell together, is the third phase that is neither 'speculation' nor 'recovery of Chinese real demand', and is caused by the strengthening of the dollar and the decline in risky assets due to the sharp decline in AI-related stocks.

Chinese PP fell 5.62%, PC fell 2.98%. PP was pushed back due to sluggish demand despite low utilization rates and inventory, and PC held on at a cost margin of 250 yuan per ton. Korea Environment Corporation's October price gap with new materials has narrowed to ±1% compared to the previous month, and November's prices will be announced on the 26th.
body:
Write the conclusion first. The raw materials market in the third week of November (11/16-20) **was not a week that fell because demand was down.** Oil prices, gold, copper, and Chinese balances were pushed all at once, but warehouse and spot premiums pointed in the opposite direction. While copper futures fell 12% in a week, Chinese warrant premiums hit a new all-time high of $500 per ton. It was a week where paper (futures) and warehouse (spot) were divided.

## Copper -12.1%, but the premium is at an all-time high

LME copper spot fell 10.14% from $13,610 to $12,230.50, and even based on 3-month futures ($12,163), it fell 8.90%. The problem is that China has fallen further. Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) copper fell 12.1% to 92,420 yuan. However, inventory moved in the opposite direction. SHFE copper inventories increased by 3,204 tons (11.6%) on the week to 30,846 tons, but were 43% less than a month ago, and LME stocks of 332,000 tons increased only 1.4%. SMM social inventory decreased by 11.3% to 54,000 tons, and bonded area inventory also decreased by 3,700 tons to 15,300 tons.

In the same week, the mass production premium jumped from $360 to $500, and the Shanghai spot premium hit an all-time high of 7,250 yuan per ton. SHFE total open interest increased by 10.1%, reaching the 91% percentile since 1995. Aluminum alone rose 1.08% to $3,184.50, and the spot price remained $353 more expensive than the 3-month contract, maintaining a reversal structure. This is also an item with dry warehouses. **The reason the price dropped is not because the volume was released, but because the position was liquidated**. The background is risk asset avoidance due to a sharp decline in AI-related stocks, weakening expectations for US copper tariffs, and the dollar index is at a 19-month high (96% probability of an interest rate increase in December).

There is a need to recheck the interpretation criteria. If the global market rises and China remains flat, it is speculation, and if the global market rises and Chinese futures and spot prices rise together, it is a recovery in real demand. This week is neither. This is the third case where Global and China fall together, and the cause is not demand, but finance. In a week like this, you should not read the decline in Chinese futures as a 'collapse in demand', but judge whether the spot premium and inventory are released together.

## Gold and silver at 14-month lows — the color of forced liquidation

Gold fell 8.92% to $3,538.19, a 52-week low, and silver plummeted 15.41% to $41.26. The gold-silver ratio increased from 79.6 times to 85.8 times. The reason gold fell even though the 10-year interest rate fell to 4.948% was due to a combination of forced liquidation to cover stock losses and the strengthening dollar. Although gold is outside our raw material chain, it is worth remembering that the won and dollar barely moved at 1,336.20 won in the same week. If the dollar rises further, the won-denominated import price offsets the decline in oil prices.

## Naphtha -9.5%, but PC stopped at -3%

WTI fell to $83.98 (-5.17%) and Brent fell to $92.57 (-3.41%) for three consecutive weeks. The background is that Hormuz transportation has returned to pre-war levels, U.S. crude oil inventories have increased by 3.4 million barrels, and the IEA has predicted a supply oversupply of 2 million barrels per day this quarter. NAFTA (CFR Japan) fell 9.53% from $890.75 to $805.88.

In China, PP fell 5.62% (−600 yuan) from 10,750 yuan to 10,083.33 yuan, and PC fell 2.98% from 14,550 yuan to 14,116.67 yuan. PP has a low operation rate and low inventory due to regular maintenance of oil and PDH, but the price has fallen. Demand for BOPP, packaging materials, and knitting was at the lowest level during the same period, so the decline was caused by demand, not supply. The polyolefin inventory of major Chinese producers was 800,000 tons, down 20,000 tons from the previous day, but PE inventory is accumulating as regular maintenance facilities return. On the other hand, PC was not pushed further as it was already within the cost line with an operating rate of 83.39% and an industry margin of 250 yuan per ton. As BPA has been lowered to 10,500 yuan, the cost burden has decreased, but this means that there is no room to defend the price.

Shipping was mixed. BDI fell to 2,898 points (-2.75%), but Panamax was 2,140 points (+1.04%), the highest since October 22. Those who import raw materials in bulk must confirm that the direction of cape (−4.6%) and panamax are different.

In Korea, the angle is different. The Asian NCC spread exceeded the break-even point ($300) at $337 per ton in November. This is an increase from $204 in the third quarter, which is the result of raw materials being withdrawn first and product prices being reduced less. However, the domestic NCC operation rate is still low at 62.4% at the end of September. If margin improvement soon leads to the resumption of operations, domestic supply may increase after December.

## Recycled raw materials: New materials are produced, but recycling remains the same.

In the Korea Environment Corporation's October announcement, PE compression was 471.7 won, PP compression was 378.1 won, and PET colorless flake was 1,133.3 won, which was within ±1% of the previous month. During the same period, the prices of new PP and PC fell by 3-6%, narrowing the price gap between remanufactured and new materials. From the perspective of selling remanufactured PCs as replacements for new ones, unit price competitiveness has weakened. Since November's information will be announced on the 26th, it is necessary to check whether the decline in new products is reflected in renewal at that time.

## Three things to watch next week

First, announcement of recycled raw materials on November 26. Second, OPEC+ 42nd Ministerial Meeting on November 29 (2027 production baseline). Third, the direction of Chinese copper inventory and production premium. If the premium breaks from $500 and imports come in, this decline will spread to spot products, and if the premium remains, it is a retracement of futures only. In practice, it is better to keep the December contract open linked to the Nafta and PP indices and buy only the necessary quantity.

![A week in which copper futures and spot premiums diverged — international benchmarks, Chinese spot premiums, and petrochemical raw material flows were summarized at the values ​​announced on November 20.](/assets/img/articles/weekly-commodities-2026-11-23.jpg)

title: If you are trapped in a tunnel, there is no light in your hand — Between 32 items of firefighting supplies and road tunnel disaster prevention guidelines
deck: Fixed emergency lighting is mandatory in tunnels longer than 500m, but portable emergency lighting to be carried by drivers who abandon their cars and escape on foot are not on the list of installation targets. The reason why the same standard for placing rooms in lodging establishments and every 25m in underground stations was found to be empty only in tunnels was followed through condolences and accident records.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: Annex 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Fire Services Act requires emergency lighting to be installed in tunnels longer than 500m (paragraph D, item 3), and only lodging facilities, movie theaters, large-scale stores, underground stations, and underground shopping malls are listed as targets of portable emergency lighting lights (paragraph E). Chapter 5 of the Road Tunnel Disaster Prevention Guidelines does not include portable lighting items.

Portable lighting duty began in underground spaces following the Daegu subway fire in 2003. In the 2022 Gwacheon Soundproof Tunnel fire (5 deaths) and the 2025 Galhyeon-Chilgapsan Tunnel fire, evacuees had to abandon their cars amidst the smoke, and there are no flashlights in the government's action guidelines.

Type approval for firefighting supplies is mandatory for 32 items, and new products outside the list cannot be used as firefighting facilities even if they receive performance certification and KFI recognition. AI smoke detection and suffocation fire extinguishing cover are examples of that threshold.
body:
Write the conclusion first. **Fixed emergency lighting is mandatory for road tunnels longer than 500m, but portable emergency lighting to be carried by drivers who abandon their cars and escape on foot is not mandatory.** Annex 4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Act on Installation and Management of Firefighting Facilities separates the two within the same article. Item D 3) requires emergency lighting to be installed in “tunnels with a length of 500 m or more,” and item E specifies only five places for portable emergency lighting: lodging facilities, movie theaters with a capacity of 100 or more, large-scale stores among sales facilities, underground stations among railroad and urban rail facilities, and underground shopping malls among underground streets. Tunnels are not on that list.

## Same criteria, different list

Article 4 (2) of the Fire Safety Performance Standard for Emergency Lighting (NFPC 304) specifically requires portable lighting. Accommodations and multi-use businesses have one per room, large-scale stores and movie theaters have three for every 50m of walking distance, and underground shopping malls and underground stations have three for every 25m. It has a height of 0.8~1.5m, can be located in the dark, turns on automatically when used, and the battery must last more than 20 minutes. It is a standard created based on the premise that a person can walk in a basement with a power outage by lifting the weight from the wall.

The document in charge of tunnels is the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport’s “Road Tunnel Disaster Prevention and Ventilation Facility Installation and Management Guidelines” (Regulation No. 461, effective April 30, 2026). Chapter 5 continues with 5.1 Emergency lighting, 5.2 Guidance lighting, and 5.3 Evacuation/evacuation facilities. Emergency lighting is at least 10lx from the roadway and sidewalk floor, guidance lights are at intervals of about 50m, and evacuation passageways are at intervals of 250m or less (for vehicles every 750m or less). Portable lighting is not an item itself. The guidelines apply NFPC/NFTC 304 to matters not mentioned, but the scope of application of 304 is also Items D and E of Appendix 4, so portable provisions do not follow in tunnels. As of the end of 2025, there are 4,003 road tunnels and underpasses nationwide, with an extension of 2,754 km.

## Where the list was created

Portable emergency lighting is a system that came from the subway, not the tunnel. Immediately after the Daegu subway fire in February 2003 (192 people dead), the Ulsan City Fire Department announced that portable emergency lighting would be required to be provided in public establishments, saying that passengers were unable to evacuate in the dark due to a sudden power outage in the disaster, resulting in significant casualties. The list has now expanded to include accommodation and an underground station, but there are no tunnels.

Tunnel fires were repeated thereafter. On December 29, 2022, 5 people died and 37 were injured in a fire in the Gwacheon soundproof tunnel on the 2nd Gyeongin Expressway. Although there were 70 fire extinguishers, 35 fire hydrants, and emergency lighting, the evacuation passageway was exempted because it was on a bridge, and the access barrier did not work due to a power outage on one side, so the dead were concentrated on that side. One person died in the Galhyeon Tunnel in Seongnam in March 2025, and two people died in the Chilgapsan Tunnel in Cheongyang in July.

The government's action instructions only guide people to evacuate "follow the guidance lights in the tunnel in the direction opposite to the smoke." Flashlights are not mentioned. According to a report citing National Fire Agency statistics, there were 96 tunnel vehicle fires between 2018 and 2022, and 576 highway tunnel traffic accidents (55 deaths) between 2020 and 2024.

![A person abandons his car and walks out of a tunnel on fire, a small flashlight in his hand, and a green evacuation light on a low wall.](/assets/img/articles/tunnel-portable-emergency-light-gap.jpg)

## 250m is not close

The tunnel light is attached to the wall. Emergency lighting of 10lx on the floor, guidance lighting that lasts for 60 minutes, and evacuation passageways every 250m. When blackout and smoke overlap, light remains on the walls and ceiling, and there is nothing in people's hands. If you walk 250m at 0.5m per second, it takes 500 seconds, or over 8 minutes.

Simulation studies show the limitations of the spacing. Under conditions where the evacuation exit distance was set at 500 m, an adult walking at 1.5 m/s reached the evacuation exit before the smoke reached him, but it was difficult for a crowd of people walking at 0.8 m/s and an elderly person at 0.5 m/s in the smoke to reach the exit. The critical wind speed that prevents the backflow of smoke reaches 3 m/s in most tunnels. The standard only requires 20 minutes, but there is no explanation as to why it is 20 minutes.

It is similar overseas. The EU directive (2004/54/EC) requires safety lighting, evacuation guidance lighting of less than 1.5m, and 500m spacing between emergency exits, but there is no portable lighting. Japan’s “Road Tunnel Emergency Facility Installation Standards” also include notification/warning, fire extinguishers at 50m intervals, guidance signs, evacuation routes, and smoke exhaust. Rather than a vacuum unique to Korea, it is an area that no country has yet established as regulations.

## Certification statement includes 32 items

Type approval of firefighting equipment is an obligation stipulated in Article 37 of the Act. 32 items, including fire extinguishers, detectors, guidance lights, and emergency lighting, are eligible, the processing period is 35 to 120 days (50 days for emergency lighting, etc.), and applicants must have testing facilities. Performance certification is a voluntary certification of items in Annex 7, and KFI recognition is a private certification. Products that have not received type approval cannot be sold or used in firefighting facility construction (Article 37 (6) of the Act). New products outside the list cannot be used as ‘firefighting facilities’ even if they receive performance certification and KFI recognition.

AI fire detection has a 'flame video analysis method' in the detector technical standards, so it is recognized as a flame detector when it receives type approval, but since there is no video method to classify smoke detectors, AI CCTV cannot replace statutory detectors and remains an auxiliary equipment. A review was published in an academic journal showing that there are no performance regulations in firefighting laws for suffocating fire extinguishing covers for electric vehicle fires, and the basic standards for firefighting equipment are subject to maintenance only in 2024.

The National Fire Agency and the Korea Fire Industry & Technology Institute announced that they opened a public-private task force starting in March 2025 and submitted 53 tasks, and reduced the burden worth 100 billion won per year by increasing the irregular testing cycle from 6 months to 1 year and lowering the fee. Article 37 (8) of the Act already provides a special provision that allows formal approval through different procedures for new technology. However, the Board of Audit and Inspection pointed out that the collection and inspection of distributed products in 2019 was conducted without sensitivity and corrosion resistance tests.

## One line left

Portable lighting in tunnels is not a matter of certification but of mandatory installation. Even if you modify the 32-item list, if you do not add a tunnel to the E-tree in Table 4, a flashlight will not appear next to the fire hydrant. Conversely, putting it in is not simple. Each of the 4,003 fire hydrant boxes must be equipped with lights that are constantly charged to maintain performance for 20 minutes, and discharged lights are as comforting as not having them at all.

There are three orders of complementation. A tunnel is added to the e-tree or a portable item is added to Chapter 5 of the guidelines, the 20-minute standard is recalculated from the evacuation time and the evacuation passageway interval, and a means that glows without power, such as a luminescent guidance beacon, is also installed. The luminous sign is a performance certification item, not a type approval.

This article only reports to the extent confirmed by condolences and documents. We have not been able to confirm all cases of self-installation in local government and private tunnels.

title: Regulations started on August 12, no calculations yet — 100 days into EU packaging regulations
deck: The 100mg/kg heavy metal and PFAS standards and the obligation to declare conformity have already been triggered. In fact, how to count the 35% of recycled raw materials must be announced by December 31, and raw materials recycled in Korea will not be recognized as EU performance until November 21, 2027.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
tags: Ban on export of waste plastic
summary: The EU packaging and packaging waste regulation (PPWR, 2025/40) came into effect on August 12, 2026. The four major heavy metals total 100mg/kg, food contact packaging PFAS 25ppb, 250ppb, total fluorine 50ppm, technical documentation (TD) and declaration of conformity (DoC) obligations began without delay. Inventory made before August 12th will also apply when released in the EU thereafter.

The implementation law for calculating and verifying the content of recycled raw materials (30, 10, 30, 35% in 2030, 50, 25, 65, 65% in 2040) has an adoption deadline of December 31, 2026, but has not been made public as of mid-November. In accordance with Enforcement Decision 2026/1425, only recycled raw materials from the EU and EEA regions are recognized for disposable PET beverage bottles, and raw materials from OECD countries such as Korea will be counted from November 21, 2027.

In a survey by the Korea International Trade Association (August-September 2026, 610 companies), 82.5% did not know the regulations at all or only knew roughly them, and 16.7% had undertaken application diagnosis. The government will hold regional consultations from November 16th to 25th and accept applications for strategic support until November 30th.
body:
From August 12th, new standards were imposed on all packaging materials appearing on the EU market. It has been more than 100 days since the packaging and packaging waste regulation (PPWR, Regulation (EU) 2025/40) took effect. The problem is that the speed of standards and standards are different. The hazardous substances and documentation obligations have already been triggered, but it has not yet been disclosed how the renewable raw material obligations for 2030 will be counted.

## Three things that have already been activated

The first is heavy metals. Article 5, Paragraph 4 prohibits the total amount of lead, cadmium, mercury, and hexavalent chromium in packaging materials from exceeding 100 mg/kg. The second is perfluorinated compounds (PFAS) in food contact packaging. If the individual fluoride content exceeds 25ppb, combined 250ppb, and total fluoride exceeds 50ppm, launch in the EU market will be blocked from August 12th. Third is documents. Article 15 requires manufacturers to prepare technical documentation (TD) and declaration of conformity (DoC) and submit them within 10 days when requested by authorities or buyers.

An issue report published by POSCO Management Research Institute (POSRI) on October 19 summarized that if documents are not provided, sales ban, customs clearance blocking, and even recall are possible. There is no reprieve. Even inventory made before August 12 will have to meet the new standards if it is released to the EU after that. The fact that it was produced in Korea is not grounds for exemption.

![Workers sorting recycled flakes and bales of compressed waste plastic — EU packaging regulations require proof of what percentage of this raw material is contained. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/eu-ppwr-100days-recycled-content.jpg)

## 2030 without standards

Recycled raw materials are different. PPWR mandates that post-consumer recycled raw materials be added to plastic packaging from January 1, 2030. 30% is contact-sensitive PET, 10% is other contact-sensitive plastics, 30% is disposable beverage bottles, and the remaining 35% is plastic packaging. In 2040, it will rise to 50, 25, 65, and 65%.

However, there is still no way to count that 35%. Article 7, Paragraph 8 requires the adoption of an enforcement law that will establish calculation and verification methods and technical document formats by December 31, 2026. The Executive Committee announced that it would prepare three follow-up laws by the fourth quarter, including calculation and verification of recycled raw materials, sustainability standards for recycling technology, and evaluation of equivalence of raw materials from third countries, but the details were not made public as of mid-November. The timing of application is also conditional. January 1, 2030 or 36 months from the enforcement of the Act, whichever is later.

The recyclability level is also the same. It is divided into A over 95%, B over 80%, C over 70%, and D·E under 70%. The structure prevents the release of D·E from 2030 and C from 2038, but the design delegation law for grading must be enacted by January 1, 2028. Regulations have begun, and the bill for 2030 is still empty.

## November 21, 2027 on Korean recycled raw materials

The most practical numbers are on disposable PET beverage bottles. The Commission adopted Implementation Decision (EU) 2026/1425 on June 30, 2026, establishing new methods for calculating, verifying and reporting recycled plastic content. Here, recycled plastic refers to plastic recycled within the EU, and also includes post-consumer plastic recycled in countries where the OECD decision applies from November 21, 2027. This door is open because Korea is a member of the OECD. However, if the EU evaluates the country's plastic waste management according to waste transportation regulations and finds it does not meet the standards, it will be omitted.

In other words, it does not mean that recycled pellets from Korean recycling companies cannot go to the EU. It is not a regulation blocking imports, but rather a failure to count the performance of EU customers in meeting their obligations. Third country equivalence standards on the PPWR side also depend on the implementation law, which has a deadline of December 31. There are still unconfirmed steps to take before domestic recycled raw materials can be included in 35% of EU packaging.

## On November 21, the waste plastic door closed.

Measures in the same direction began two days ago. Since November 21, the EU has banned the export of plastic waste generated in member countries to non-OECD countries under the Waste Transport Regulation (Regulation (EU) 2024/1157). At least until May 21, 2029. According to the Commission, the EU produces about 40 million tons of plastic waste every year and exports 1 million to 1.5 million tons, and half of the exports in 2025 went to non-OECD countries. This was followed by Turkmenistan with 510,000 tons, Malaysia with 276,000 tons, Indonesia with 215,000 tons, and Vietnam with 137,000 tons.

Exports to OECD countries will continue to be permitted, but subject to monitoring. The Commission published the sustainability assessment of Turkiye exports on September 18, and independent audits of facilities receiving exports will be required from May 21, 2027. The direct impact of this ban on Korea is not specified solely through public data. However, if EU raw materials used by Southeast Asian recycling companies are concentrated in the OECD region, the raw material procurement structure for recycled pellets may be shaken.

## 82.5% is still in the first stage

The report released on October 27 by the International Trade Research Institute of the Korea International Trade Association, which surveyed 610 EU export companies from August 21 to September 2, is sobering. 82.5% of respondents said they did not know PPWR at all or only knew roughly, and 16.7% of companies had completed or were in the process of diagnosing the application of their own products. 45.2% of companies did not have a diagnosis plan.

The gap in evidence is larger. Among the 356 companies using plastic packaging materials, the proportion that did not have basic information was 19.7-22.8%, but the proportion that did not have proof of recycled raw material supplier, recyclability evaluation, and producer responsibility recycling (EPR) reporting data was 50.6-53.4%. The scale of the cost is unknown. 49.3% of companies were unable to calculate one-time costs, and 54.1% were unable to calculate recurring costs. Of the 577 companies that expected additional costs, 81.6% responded that it would be difficult to reflect them in the transaction price at all or that only 25% of them could be reflected.

The government also moved. The Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment held a joint briefing session with related ministries on April 29 and operated a cross-ministerial working group, and the Ministry of SMEs and Startups held a meeting of small and medium-sized businesses in beauty, food and packaging materials on October 20. From November 16th to 25th, training and consultation sessions will be held in five regions across the country, and 50-70% of testing and certification costs (up to 100 million won per company) will be supported as strategic support for overseas standard certification acquisition support projects. The application deadline is November 30th.

## Two bills

The EU’s cause is confirmed by numbers. According to Eurostat, EU packaging waste in 2023 is 79.7 million tons, or 177.8 kg per person. Plastic packaging waste is 35.3 kg per person, but only 14.8 kg (42.1%) is recycled. This means that there is no basis for lifting regulations.

The bill on the other side also exists. Composite packaging, such as ramen bags, is disadvantageous in recyclability evaluation, and as the Korea Economic Daily reported on September 2, CJ CheilJedang and Pulmuone were required to submit declarations of conformity to EU customers even before implementation. A survey showing that 81.6% of small and medium-sized businesses are unable to add costs to prices shows that this regulation can actually operate as a non-tariff barrier.

Speed ​​control within the EU is also in progress. Omnibus VIII, which suspends EPR proxy obligations until 2035, was passed by the European Parliament by a vote of 616 to 9 on October 20 and by the Council on October 21, but negotiations have not yet begun. However, there is no law to postpone the application date of PPWR. There are two things that have not been confirmed. These are the total compliance costs for Korean companies and whether domestic recycled raw materials are recognized as EU performance. Both depend on documents coming out after December 31.

title: 15-20% and 25.5% — three numbers set by the government bill for the Framework Act on Digital Assets on the 24th
deck: The Financial Services Commission will hold a virtual asset committee meeting on the 24th to disclose the main contents of the government bill for the Framework Act on Digital Assets. The exchange's major shareholders' stake is capped at 15-20%, the bank's stake in the Korean won stablecoin consortium is 50%+1 share, and the Monetary Policy Committee's base interest rate in the same week is 3.00%. We divided each of the three numbers into confirmed records to see what has changed and what has not yet been determined.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: The Financial Services Commission will hold a virtual asset committee meeting on November 24, 2026 and disclose the main contents of the government plan for the Framework Act on Digital Assets (Virtual Asset Stage 2). The government bill was proposed as legislation by lawmakers under the name of Chairman of the Political Affairs Committee Yoo Dong-soo and undergoes a combined review by the Political Affairs Committee. The announcement on the 24th is not a final law, but a draft release.

A cap of 15-20% for major shareholders of exchanges, postponement of implementation, or restrictions on voting rights are discussed. As reported by Metro Newspaper on November 9, 2026, the shareholding ratio of the largest shareholders in domestic exchanges ranges from 25.5% for Upbit to 97% for DigitalX. A 50% bank stake + 1 share consortium is likely to be the Korean won stablecoin, but due to the 15% stake limit for non-financial companies under the Banking Act, at least 4 banks are needed to fill the majority.

The Bank of Korea Monetary Policy Committee meeting will be held on the 26th of the same week. The base interest rate is 3.00% per year, and the market prefers a 3.25% increase (Maeil Business Newspaper confirmed with four experts from the Bank of Korea on the 22nd). The share cap number, grace period, and implementation timing have not yet been confirmed, and the Financial Services Commission maintains its position that ‘no major details have been confirmed.’
body:
On the 24th, the Financial Services Commission opens the Virtual Asset Committee, a statutory advisory body. Immediately after the meeting, the main contents of the government's bill for the Framework Act on Digital Assets (Second Stage Legislation for Virtual Assets) will be revealed. This is the schedule reported side by side by Money Today, Digital Times, and Korea Economic Daily on the 22nd. Prior to the announcement, we will meet with representatives of the five major Korean won exchanges, including Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone, DigitalX, and Gopax, early this week to collect on-site opinions for the final time.

What the market is paying attention to in this government plan is not the number of condolences, but three numbers. The upper limit on the shares of major shareholders of the exchange is 15-20%, the share that banks must have in the won-denominated stablecoin issuance consortium is 50% + 1 share, and the base interest rate of the Bank of Korea Monetary Policy Committee held in the same week is 3.00%. The first two numbers change the rules of the market, and the last number changes the value of the fund.

## 1. What will be released on the 24th — it is not a law, but a draft

The government bill is proposed as legislation by lawmakers in the name of Chairman Yoo Dong-soo of the National Assembly’s Political Affairs Committee. Afterwards, the Political Affairs Committee undergoes a merge review with the existing ruling and opposition party's bills, and then moves on to the Legislation and Judiciary Committee's review of the system and structure, and then to the plenary session. In other words, the announcement on the 24th is not a final law, but a draft.

The framework of the government plan is divided into three parts. First, the regulations that were divided into the Specific Financial Information Act (Special Financial Information Act) and the Virtual Asset User Protection Act are combined into one business law. Second, by subdividing the work of virtual asset business operators (VASP), storage and management work is separated into a separate 'trust business', and the bulk reporting system is differentiated into an authorization system and registration system depending on the nature of the work. Third, it contains a plan to hold business operators liable for no-fault damages in the event of hacking or computer failure. Interest in this government's plan is whether to legislate the standards for transaction support (listing) and termination of transaction support (delisting), and to what extent the so-called "separation of gold and price" principle, which has prevented traditional financial companies from entering the virtual asset business, will be relaxed.

## 2. First number — 15-20%, 25.5%, and 97%

The biggest issue is regulation of shares held by major stockholders in exchanges. Under the Capital Markets Act, a plan is being discussed to place an equity cap of 15-20%, which is the level of alternative stock exchanges (ATS), and to grant a grace period of 1-2 years (or 3 years) to existing exchanges. To avoid controversy over unconstitutionality, an alternative that only restricts the exercise of voting rights instead of the shareholding ratio is also being reviewed.

The reason this number is problematic is the actual share structure of domestic exchanges. According to a report in Metro News on November 9, 2026, the largest shareholder's share of domestic virtual asset exchanges ranges from 25.5% in Upbit to 97% in Digital X. If the upper limit is set at 15%, even the country's No. 1 exchange will have to liquidate its shares within the grace period if it is set at 20%.

All that remains is to find a place to organize. There are criticisms in the industry that if regulations on the separation of finance and industry (separation of financial capital and industrial capital) are not eased, it will be difficult for acquisition candidates such as banks to step forward. It is the gap that remains between the direction of regulation and the possibility of actual implementation.

## 3. Second number — 50%+1 share, arithmetic created by banking law 15%

The Korean won stablecoin was weighted toward the bank-centered consortium advocated by the Bank of Korea. When asked about the issuer during the audit of the National Assembly's Finance and Economic Planning Committee on October 12, 2026, Bank of Korea Governor Shin Hyun-song answered, "As agreed, it is a bank-led consortium," and "The bank is 50% + 1." He then explained that this plan is “a government plan and an agreement with the government.”

Once the number is determined, arithmetic follows. Current banking law restricts banks from holding more than 15% of shares in non-financial companies. If this provision is left in place, at least four banks are needed to fill the majority of the consortium with bank shares alone. The structure of Hana Financial Group, which formed a consortium through a multilateral agreement with BNK Financial Group, iM Financial Group, SC First Bank, and OK Savings Bank in January 2026, fits this arithmetic (Green Economy Newspaper, November 17, 2026). The minimum equity capital requirement for the issuer is said to be around 5 billion won.

The counterargument is also clear. If the issuing entity is limited to banks, the pace of fintech experimentation will slow down. The Bank of Korea maintains its position that bank-centered issuance is “not the best option, but a compromise to reduce the risk of being abused as a means of avoiding regulation,” and that issuance qualifications can be expanded after the consistency of technology and regulations is confirmed.

## 4. Third number — 3.00% and 3.25%

On Thursday (26th) of the same week, the Bank of Korea's Monetary Policy Committee will hold the last monetary policy direction meeting of the year. The current base interest rate is 3.00% per annum, and the market prefers a 3.25% increase. Maeil Business Newspaper asked four experts from the Bank of Korea on the 22nd, and all four predicted a 0.25% point increase. This is because the consumer price inflation rate in October was 2.8% and the core inflation rate was 2.8%, exceeding the Bank of Korea's target (2.0%), and the growth forecast is expected to be raised due to strong semiconductor exports. Nomura Securities also predicted a 25bp increase on the 20th.

When interest rates and regulations move in the same week, two forces act on risky assets simultaneously. Interest rates change the discount rate, and regulations change the rules of the market. Bitcoin fell to $55,326 during intraday trading on the 21st, hitting the lowest level since September 2024, and then recovered to the $60,000 level on the evening of the 22nd. As of 19:30 on the 22nd, it is $60,815, 1.2% higher than 24 hours ago, Upbit won price is 82.6 million won, and kimchi premium is -0.02%. Although there has been a rebound, it is still down around 5% on a weekly basis.

## 5. To what extent has each issue been confirmed?

|Issues|Current|What is discussed in the government|Confirmed or not|
|---|---|---|---|
|Major shareholders’ shares of the exchange|No upper limit on shareholding (reporting system, major shareholder eligibility screening)|15-20% cap + moratorium on implementation, or restrictions on voting rights|Not confirmed|
|Issuance of KRW stablecoin|No legal basis|Bank-centered consortium, 50% of bank shares + 1 share|Direction likely, number unconfirmed|
|Storage/Management (Consignment)|One of the five VASP tasks|Separate ‘consignment business’, differentiated authorization and registration|Expected to include draft|
|Responsibility for hacking and computer failures|Compensation for damages under the User Protection Act|Business operator’s no-fault liability|Expected to include draft|
|Standards for listing and delisting|Exchange’s own standards + DAXA autonomous guide|Whether legally binding common standards are in place?|Review Phase|

## 6. Confirmed and unconfirmed

What has been confirmed is the schedule and direction. Multiple media reports confirm that the Financial Services Commission will unveil the government plan at the Virtual Asset Committee on the 24th, that stablecoin issuance is leaning toward a bank-centered consortium, and that major shareholder regulations are being reviewed in two ways, including a cap on shareholding and a limit on voting rights. The same goes for the procedure in which a government bill is proposed in the form of legislation by lawmakers and undergoes a combined review by the Political Affairs Committee.

There are many more that have not been confirmed. It has not been determined whether the stake cap will be 15% or 20%, and whether the grace period will be 1-2 years or 3 years. The Financial Services Commission has repeatedly stated that “no major details have been confirmed.” It has not been determined to what extent fintechs and exchanges can participate in stablecoin issuance and whether the minimum equity capital requirements for issuers will be included in the draft. The numbers may change during National Assembly review, and the timing of implementation has not been determined.

## 7. Point connected to February 2027

This government plan is in line with the token securities system. The amendments to the Electronic Securities Act and the Capital Markets Act passed the plenary session of the National Assembly on January 15, 2026, and are scheduled to go into effect on February 4, 2027. In the first stage, tokenization of private MMFs exclusively for institutional investors, privately placed bonds, unlisted stocks using the trust method, and publicly offered piece investment securities will begin. The Financial Services Commission's policy briefing left 'on-chain payment', where securities and payments are settled at once with stablecoins, as the final task.

Therefore, the issuer and timing of the Korean won stablecoin become variables that determine the speed of the payment infrastructure. If issuance is held late, centered on banks, the first stage of token securities will run first on existing bank accounts and the Korea Securities Depository ledger.

## 8. Three things for readers to check

First, you only need to look at the three numbers in the announcement on the 24th. These are the upper limit and grace period for major shareholders' shares, the bank consortium's share requirements (whether 50% + 1 share remains the same), and the scope of separation of the trustee business (whether the exchange can continue to handle the trusteeship).

Second, this is the result of the Monetary Policy Committee meeting on the 26th. If it rises to 3.25%, the costs of floating rate loans and leverage also rise.

Third, where are my assets stored? Even if the law is implemented, the storage structure of individuals does not automatically change. Items to check include who stores exchange deposits and virtual assets and whether there is a separate custodian.

title: It was not this month’s pension that was shaken by the plunge, but the calculation for 2069 — a breakwater worth 1,684 trillion won.
deck: On November 20, KOSPI closed at 4,869.96. The equity value of 287 listed companies in which the National Pension Service holds more than 5% decreased from 515.9 trillion won at the end of June to 333.5 trillion won on October 15. However, this month’s pension payment is not reduced. The reasons and the point at which losses turn into actual burdens were divided into disclosures, laws, and financial estimates.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: The latest official announcement from the National Pension Fund Management Headquarters is as of the end of August (posted on October 30). Reserves: KRW 1,684.4 trillion, rate of return since the beginning of the year: 14.77% (provisional), profits: KRW 218.3 trillion. Domestic stocks accounted for 25.8%, or 433.8 trillion won. The slump since September has not yet been reflected in any public announcements.

Pension already received is not reduced by the fund rate of return. Benefits are determined by subscription period and income and are adjusted annually to keep in line with prices. Article 3-2 of the National Pension Act, which came into effect in January 2026, stipulated the state's obligation to guarantee payment. The 10% insurance premium rate in 2027 is also a schedule already confirmed by law, regardless of the plunge.

Where losses become a real burden is in financial estimates. The National Assembly Budget Office predicted a deficit in 2050 and exhaustion in 2069, assuming a long-term rate of return of 4.6%. If the rate of return rises by 1 percentage point, exhaustion will be delayed by 13 years to 2082. The results of the 6th financial calculation will be released in March 2028.
body:
On the afternoon of the 20th, KOSPI closed at 4,869.96, down 267.93 points (5.21%) from the previous trading day. KOSDAQ also closed at 645.68, down 39.13 points (5.71%), and a selling sidecar was applied to both markets. This is a loss of 46.6% from the all-time high closing price on June 22 (9,114.55). Compared to 5,730.74 at the end of October, it lost 860.78 points (15.0%) in three weeks.

If you place the national pension number next to this number, you can see both at the same time. One is that the fund has actually decreased, and the other is that this month's pension payment amount remains the same. Both are true. This is because the same event is viewed in different time units.

## November not yet announced

The latest official announcement from the National Pension Fund Management Headquarters is as of the end of August. The 'Portfolio Management Status and Returns by Asset Class (August 2026)' posted on October 30 is the last, and the September version has not yet been posted. The last confirmed figures currently available are from August 31.

- Reserves **1,684.4 trillion won**. It is calculated by subtracting KRW 471.6 trillion in salaries (pension benefits, KRW 457.6 trillion + management and operating expenses, KRW 14.0 trillion) from the KRW 2,156.1 trillion created since 1988 (KRW 968.4 trillion in pension insurance premiums + KRW 1,187.7 trillion in operating income).
- Rate of return since the beginning of the year **14.77%** (provisional), profit KRW 218.3 trillion. It fell from 27.22% at the end of June to 14.84% at the end of July, and then fell 0.07 percentage points further in August.
- The asset composition is foreign stocks 619.3 trillion (36.8%), domestic stocks 433.8 trillion (25.8%), domestic bonds 282.2 trillion (16.8%), alternative investments 240.4 trillion (14.3%), and foreign bonds 98.5 trillion (5.8%).

These August numbers do not include the slump since September. However, the direction is already clear. The reserves, which were 1,865.6 trillion won at the end of June, decreased by 181.4 trillion won in July alone (domestic stocks 543.2 trillion → 418.6 trillion won), and only increased by 267 billion won in August. Since the end of June, the stock valuation of 287 listed companies in which the National Pension Service holds a 5% or more stake has decreased by KRW 182.3963 trillion (35.3%) from KRW 515.9293 trillion (at the end of June) to KRW 333.533 trillion (October 15), according to FnGuide. 71.8% of the decrease, or KRW 131.0971 trillion, came from two stocks: SK Hynix (-74.2261 trillion KRW) and Samsung Electronics (-56.871 trillion KRW).

This tally does not represent a total loss for the fund. This is an estimate targeting only stocks held by more than 5%, and since the KOSPI fell 15.0% again between the end of October and November 20, the actual valuation will be lower than that. The exact amount will be confirmed only when the September portion is announced.

## 1,684 trillion won is 30 times the annual salary

Let’s change the unit for measuring the size of the plunge. This year, the number of national pension recipients is approximately 8.28 million, and the benefits to be paid are expected to be around 56 trillion won (National Pension Research Institute Mid-Term Fiscal Outlook 2026-2030, August 2026). Simply dividing the accumulated savings of 1,684.4 trillion won at the end of August is 30 times the annual salary.

This ratio is only a rough indicator of how well the fund is holding up. This does not mean that the fund will run out after 30 years, as it earns management profits and receives insurance premiums in the meantime. Rather, in 2025, pension insurance income of 63.8803 trillion won was more than salary expenditure of 49.6605 trillion won. The money coming in is a bigger step than the money going out. The transition to deficit is expected to occur in 2050, and exhaustion is expected to occur in 2069 (National Assembly Budget Office, revised forecast for June 2026, assuming a long-term rate of return of 4.6%). The number ‘30 years’ worth’ is enough to mean that your salary will not be blocked tomorrow, but it is not enough to mean that it will be okay even 30 years from now.

![The dam blocking the reservoir water and the lights of the village below. The fund is not an individual bank account, but a joint reserve fund. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/nps-fund-crash-safety-2026.jpg)

## Why is the pension already received not reduced?

The national pension benefit amount is not determined by the fund rate of return. It is determined by the subscription period and income during subscription (standard monthly income). The basic amount is calculated by multiplying the average income of all subscribers (value A) and the average income of the member during the subscription period by a legal constant, and 5% is added for each year of the subscription period exceeding 20 years. The income replacement rate of 43% will be applied to new subscription periods starting in 2026. The pension you start receiving is adjusted each year according to the national consumer price fluctuation rate. Although there is an upward direction, there is no structure in which prices are lowered due to stock prices.

Looking at the scale, you can see how widespread this salary is. As of the end of July 2026, there were 7,863,299 beneficiaries, and the payment amount that month was 4,547.7 billion won, or an average of 650,515 won per person per month. There are 6,727,607 old-age pension recipients. As of June 2026, the average old-age pension benefit is 706,150 won per month, 1,173,493 won for subscribers with 20 years or more, and 451,966 won for subscribers with 10 to 19 years of experience.

In other words, even if the fund decreases by 200 trillion won, this month's 650,000 won will not become 570,000 won. The reason why this sentence holds true is because the fund is a ‘joint reserve fund’ rather than an ‘individual bank account’. Instead, the cost lies elsewhere.

## What the payment guarantee guarantees

Article 3-2 of the revised National Pension Act, which came into effect on January 1, 2026, stipulates that “the state shall ensure stable and continuous payment of pension benefits under this Act.” The provision before the revision was, ‘Policies necessary for stable and continuous payment must be established and implemented.’ The obligation to pay is put directly into the sentence.

We must distinguish between what this provision means and what it does not mean. It is true that there is a legal basis for saying that the state cannot give up and say, “I cannot provide funds because I do not have the funds.” However, it is not a device that guarantees individual amounts separately like depositor protection, and it does not even set a method of financing such as filling the shortfall with general accounting or paying a specific tax. Although the obligation to pay has become clear, how to divide the cost among insurance premiums, finances, and supply conditions is still the responsibility of financial calculations and legislation.

‘Exhaustion of funds’ is not the same thing as ‘suspension of payments’. Exhaustion is the point when the reserve balance becomes 0, and even then, premium income continues to come in. After exhaustion, it approaches the charging method of paying that year's salary with that year's insurance premium, and the shortfall must be made up with other financial resources.

## Where losses become a real burden — the reckoning for 2069

A financial forecast is not just one number. Even with the same revised law, the results vary depending on the long-term operating rate of return. The Ministry of Health and Welfare proposed 2071 at a rate of return of 5.5% and 2064 at 4.5%, and the National Assembly Budget Office calculated a return to deficit in 2050 and exhaustion in 2069, assuming 4.6% in the revised outlook in June 2026.

The sensitivity of the rate of return is as follows. According to the same analysis by the Office of Budget and Policy, if the long-term rate of return is increased by 1 percentage point, the transition to deficit will be delayed by 13 years to 2060, and the exhaustion will be delayed to 2082. If you raise it by 2 percentage points, the surplus will be maintained until 2120 and the fund will not be depleted. Conversely, when investing government funds, timing is more important than size. If you add 1% of GDP every year from 2026, the depletion will be delayed by 31 years to 2100, but if you start adding it only in 2069, when the fund runs out, the effect will only be one year.

From this structure, the meaning of this crash becomes clear. One year's valuation loss does not in itself advance the exhaustion point by several years. The key is how much the long-term average rate of return moves. By the end of August, the return since the beginning of the year was 14.77%, significantly exceeding the 4.6% assumption. The problem is after September. When September's disclosure is released, we will be able to know where this year's rate of return stands, and that number will be the starting point for the 6th financial calculation to be released in March 2028. Financial calculations will begin in earnest from 2027.

Let’s add one more number. At the National Assembly Planning and Finance Committee, Representative Yoon Young-seok said on October 6, “Even if the operating rate of return is set at 4.5%, there is an unfunded debt of 1,447 trillion won.” This means that the present value of the money accumulated in the fund and the money to be given in the future are different. The 1,684 trillion won fund is not a number that erases this debt, but a number that buys time.

## January 2027, 0.25% point in bank account

Regardless of the crash, changes that have already been decided are a month away. From January 1, 2027, the national pension contribution rate will increase from 9.5% to 10.0%. The supplementary provisions of the National Pension Act (Law No. 20903) promulgated on April 2, 2025 set the rate at 9.5% in 2026, 10.0% in 2027, and 10.5% in 2028, and will increase by 0.5 percentage points each year until 13% in 2033.

Because the employee subscriber divides the plan in half, the out-of-pocket rate increases from 4.75% to 5.0%, and the employer's share also increases by the same amount. If the standard monthly income is 3 million won, the out-of-pocket burden increases by 7,500 won, from 142,500 won to 150,000 won per month. Local subscribers and voluntary subscribers pay the entire amount themselves, so it ranges from 9.5% to 10.0%. The upper limit of the standard monthly income is 6.59 million won and the lower limit is 410,000 won (applied from July 2026 to June 2027).

This increase is not a measure linked to the stock market. Even if there was no plunge, it was scheduled to rise, and it was not postponed because of the collapse. The 43% increase in income replacement rate is already being applied from the 2026 subscription period.

## Why has the ‘safety valve’ become smaller?

The reason the National Pension Service failed to make purchases in a sharp decline is not because the fund dried up. This is the result of changing the rules. On January 26, the Fund Management Committee postponed rebalancing until the end of June to prevent mechanical selling even if the proportion of domestic stocks exceeds the allowable range of strategic asset allocation (SAA), and on May 28, it raised the target proportion of domestic stocks this year from 14.9% to 20.8% and expanded the allowable range from ±3 percentage points to ±6 percentage points (maximum 28.8%). As a result, the proportion of domestic stocks rose to 29.1% at the end of June, and in the plunge in July, 124.6 trillion won in domestic stock valuation disappeared in one month.

The purchasing power in a falling market also decreased. On November 6, when foreigners sold KRW 2.6892 trillion, net purchases by pension funds were KRW 287.4 billion (10.7%), and on October 15, when foreigners sold KRW 3.768 trillion, net purchases by pension funds were KRW 35 billion. This is in contrast to the net purchase of 8.35 trillion won by pension funds from December 4, 2024, to April of last year. Daishin Securities estimates that the proportion of domestic stocks in the National Pension Service, reflecting the sharp decline, is about 20.5%, and that if the allowable upper limit is applied, there is room for purchase of about 50 trillion won.

Minister of Health and Welfare Jeong Eun-kyeong said at the Fund Management Committee on October 20, "I am well aware that the public has great concerns about long-term financial stability due to the volatility of domestic stocks," but added, "There is a need to evaluate the rate of return of all assets in a long-term and comprehensive manner." The ruling and opposition parties fought over the decisions made in January and May during the National Assembly audit, and related meeting minutes will be made public in 2030. The core of this controversy is not ‘whether one can receive a pension’ but ‘who bears how much of the downside risk?’ The risk ultimately belongs to the fund, and the fund belongs to the subscriber.

## Three things to check now

1. **My Expected Pension** — You can see the subscription period and expected receipt amount in ‘Learn about my pension’ on the National Pension Service website and app. This number is more important to me than the fund return table.
2. **Premium premium for January 2027** — From 4.75% to 5.0% for employed subscribers. The national pension deduction amount on pay stubs will increase by 0.25 percentage points.
3. **Age for starting benefits** — Age 65 for those born after 1969. In principle, the subscription period for the old-age pension must be at least 10 years.

## Limitations of this article

- Fund returns and reserves have not been disclosed since September. The extent of November's losses has not yet been confirmed by any official figures.
- The 182 trillion won decrease in 287 listed companies is calculated by F&Guide and is not a total loss of the fund.
- 2050, 2064, 2069, and 2071 are all projections based on assumptions. There is no confirmed exhaustion year until the results of the 6th financial calculation are released in March 2028.

factCheck.title: Fact check & sources
factCheck.note: The fund figures were based on the National Pension Service Fund Management Headquarters announcement (as of the end of August, published on October 30), and the figures for June and July were compared with the press release for the first half of the year and the monthly announcement from the same organization. The index, beneficiaries, and financial outlook were based on data from the Korea Exchange, Bank of Korea ECOS, National Pension Service statistics, and National Assembly Budget Office, and were cross-checked with multiple reports citing them. '30 times the annual salary' is a simple calculation dividing the accumulated reserves of 1,684.4 trillion won at the end of August by the 2026 salary forecast of 56 trillion won and is not the actual duration of the fund. The decrease of 182 trillion won in 287 listed companies is not the total loss of the fund as calculated by FnGuide, and does not include additional declines after October 15th. The amount of losses in November, the rate of return since September, and the financial calculation results for 2028 were not confirmed at the time of writing this article, so forecasts and facts are presented separately.

title: 0.14% for rent vs. 0.03% for sale — 4-fold gap created by Seoul’s ‘moving-in cliff’
deck: In the third week of November, apartment rental prices in Seoul rose 0.14%, and sales rose 0.03%. In the same week, the number of move-ins in the metropolitan area decreased by half compared to the previous month. The structure in which only rent prices rise where house prices have stopped has been decomposed into three axes: indicators, government announcements, and loan interest rates.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: According to the Korea Real Estate Agency's weekly statistics (as of 2026-11-16), the sale price of apartments in Seoul increased by 0.03% and the jeonse price by 0.14% compared to the previous week. This year's cumulative increase rate was 9.43% for jeonse, exceeding 8.91% for sales.

According to Zigbang's tally, the number of apartments moving in nationwide in November was 11,559 households, down 30% from the previous month and 49% from the same month last year, and in the metropolitan area it was cut in half to 4,031 households. There are 488 households in Seoul and 0 households in Incheon.

In a briefing on November 13, the government announced that 16,000 units will be occupied in the metropolitan area in November and December and 28,000 units will be occupied in the first quarter of next year. It has not yet been confirmed whether the plan leads to actual occupancy or whether the forecast of 13,212 households in 2028 is maintained.
body:
Write the conclusion first. In the third week of November 2026, the Seoul apartment market entered the section where 'house prices stopped and only rent prices rose'. In the same week, the sale price rose 0.03% and the jeonse price rose 0.14%. The gap between the two numbers is more than four times. The force that created this gap is supply, not demand. The main channel for renting out new apartments has decreased by half in the metropolitan area in just one month.

This article is checked in three ways. First, how much the indicator has actually risen. Second, how much has the occupancy volume decreased and how different is it from the government plan? Third, how lending interest rates amplify this structure. And at the end, write down what was confirmed and what was not confirmed.

## 1. Same week, sale 0.03%, lease 0.14%

The starting point is the weekly apartment price trend for the third week of November (as of November 16) announced by the Korea Real Estate Agency on November 20. Apartment sales prices in Seoul rose 0.03% compared to the previous week. It is half of the previous week's increase rate of 0.07%, and is the lowest increase in 91 weeks based on the published week since the second week of February 2025 (0.02%). The record of rising for 93 consecutive weeks continued, but the pace was virtually flat.

In the same week, the jeonse price increased by 0.14%. Since the second week of March 2026, the weekly increase rate has exceeded 0.1% for 37 consecutive weeks. When viewed cumulatively, the direction is clearer. This year, the rental price of apartments in Seoul rose 9.43%, exceeding the cumulative sales increase rate of 8.91%. Last year, during the same period, the rate of increase in jeonse rent was 2.77%, so the rate of increase was more than three times faster.

Even if you look at each region, the directions are different. Sales prices in the 3 Gangnam districts fell for 11 consecutive weeks at -0.30% in Gangnam-gu, -0.31% in Seocho-gu, and -0.42% in Songpa-gu. In the same week, jeonse prices rose by 0.22% in Gangnam-gu, 0.09% in Songpa-gu, and 0.01% in Seocho-gu. This means that even in areas where sales prices are falling, jeonse prices are rising. The rate of increase in jeonse prices in the metropolitan area was 0.14%, which was more than four times that of the provinces (0.03%), and nationwide it was 0.08%.

|Metrics|Buy and Sell|Charter|
|---|---|---|
|Weekly increase rate for the third week of November (Seoul)|0.03%|0.14%|
|Cumulative growth rate in 2026 (Seoul)|8.91%|9.43%|
|Cumulative for the same period in 2025 (Seoul)|—|2.77%|
|Third week of November in Gangnam-gu|-0.30%|0.22%|

Source: Korea Real Estate Agency weekly apartment price trends (as of 2026-11-16), cross-checking media reports.

This has already been reflected in consumer prices. Consumer prices for monthly rent in October rose 1.4% from a year ago, the largest increase since December 2022. Monthly rent rose 1.5%, the highest since December 2013, and Seoul's monthly rent inflation rate has been in the 2% range for two months. Since jeonse and monthly rent prices reflect both existing and new contracts, the increase in prices concluded in the market now will remain in the index for several more months.

## 2. Cliff of occupancy — 4,031 households in the metropolitan area in November

The biggest way for leased properties to be released into the market is through new construction. The passage narrowed. According to Zigbang's tally, the number of apartments moving in nationwide in November was 11,559 households in 21 complexes. It decreased by 30% from the previous month (16,567 households) and by 49% from the same month last year (22,551 households).

The decline was concentrated in the metropolitan area. The number of households moving into the metropolitan area was 4,031, a decrease of 49% from the previous month, and the decrease rate in regional areas during the same period was 13%. In Seoul, there are only 488 households in three complexes. All three complexes are redevelopment complexes with less than 300 households, so there are not many rental properties released upon move-in. Incheon does not have any units scheduled to move in in November. Of the 3,543 households in Gyeonggi, 3,136 households, or 89%, are concentrated in Pyeongtaek (1,604 households) and Icheon (1,532 households). In areas bordering Seoul, new supply has virtually stopped.

On an annual basis, the gap is longer. According to Real Estate R114, the number of apartments in Seoul in 2026 will be 17,698 households, which is the lowest in 13 years since 2013 (16,321 households). It decreased by 45% from 2025 (32,370 households). In 2027, the number will increase slightly to 18,329 households, but in 2028, it will drop to 13,212 households. This is the lowest volume since R114 began counting in 1990.

Supply and demand indicators also point in the same direction. The Seoul rent supply and demand index fell slightly from 120.2 in the second week of November to 119.4 in the third week, but has remained above 100 for 78 consecutive weeks since the third week of May 2025 (100.2). This index is based on 100, and the closer it is to 200, the more people are looking to purchase the product. The Gyeonggi jeonse supply and demand index is also at 110.6, maintaining the highest level since August 2021.

As jeonse became scarce, conditions for occupancy in new complexes actually improved. According to the Housing Industry Research Institute, the Seoul apartment occupancy rate in October 2025 was 87.6%, up 2.8 percentage points from the previous month (84.8%). This is interpreted as a result of the lack of rental properties pushing up new construction.

## 3. Government sees other signals — increased listings and 28,000 homes in the first quarter

The government’s diagnosis is different from market indicators. The Office for Government Policy Coordination and the Financial Services Commission announced at the 3rd regular housing supply briefing on November 13 that the Seoul market's downward stabilization indicators are expanding. There are three numbers provided as evidence. As of November 11, the number of apartments for sale in Seoul exceeded 80,000, an increase of more than 40% since the beginning of the year, and over the past three weeks, jeonse and monthly rent properties increased by 5.0% and 10.6%, respectively, so the combined sales and monthly rent exceeded 123,000. From January to September, housing permits in Seoul increased by 33% compared to the same period last year, of which 38,000 apartments were approved, which is 1.5 times the average for the past 10 years.

A supply schedule was also presented. Approximately 16,000 units will begin moving in in the metropolitan area between November and December 2026, and approximately 28,000 units will begin moving in in the first quarter of 2027. The number of units moving into Seoul in the first quarter was approximately 6,000, of which approximately 4,000 units were in the Mapo, Seocho, and Yongsan areas. The government announced that more than half of the move-ins in the metropolitan area in the first quarter were large complexes with more than 1,000 households, so it is expected that rental properties will be put up for sale along with move-ins.

The two observations are not contradictory. Market indicators refer to the current execution price and supply and demand, and government announcements refer to the supply plan for the next few months. The problem is the time difference between them. The number of households moving in in November calculated by Zigbang is 11,559, and the number of households moving in in the metropolitan area between November and December according to the government is 16,000. Although it is difficult to make a simple comparison because the counting criteria (completed move-in/expected move-in, metropolitan area/nationwide) are different, there is always a gap between plan and reality.

## 4. Interest rate – double burden created by 4.57% jeonse loan

The rise in rent prices doubles the burden on tenants when combined with the rise in loan interest. According to the Bank of Korea's monetary and financial statistics, the deposit bank's deposit loan interest rate (based on new transaction amount) is 4.57% per annum as of September 2026. It rose 0.22 percentage points from 4.35% in August and is 0.87 percentage points higher compared to 3.70% in May 2025.

If you apply it to the same principal, you can see the difference. When borrowing 100 million won, the monthly interest increases from 308,300 won to 380,800 won. With a simple calculation assuming that the principal remains the same, it costs 72,500 won more per month or 870,000 won per year. Tenants who have to borrow more deposits due to rising rental prices are in a zone where both the loan amount and interest rate rise simultaneously.

The cumulative burden at the household level is also large. According to the National Data Agency's Household Financial Welfare Survey microdata, the average deposit for jeonse households in 2025 is 217.97 million won, a 34.9% increase from 2019 (161.62 million won). Financial debt for the purpose of securing a deposit increased by 53.0% over the same period to an average of 46.39 million won per household. The proportion of loans compared to deposits increased from 18.8% to 21.3%.

The direction of interest rates has not yet been determined. The market expects the Bank of Korea's Monetary Policy Committee to raise the base interest rate from 3.00% to 3.25% on November 26. In the United States, the October Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index is scheduled for November 25, and the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) is scheduled for December 8-9. The U.S. base interest rate is currently 3.75-4.00% per annum, and the market is effectively reflecting the December increase as the base scenario.

## 5. Confirmed and unconfirmed

What has been identified are indicators and published plans. The Korea Real Estate Board's weekly index, Zigbang and Real Estate R114's occupancy volume statistics, Bank of Korea interest rate statistics, and the National Data Agency's Household Financial Welfare Survey are raw data published by each organization. The contents of the government's briefing on November 13 are also confirmed in the published announcement.

There are four things that have not been confirmed.

First, whether occupancy in December and the first quarter of 2027 proceeds as planned. The government plan is based on expected occupancy, and the actual occupancy rate was 87.6% as of October 2025 in Seoul. Plans and reality may differ.

Second, how much the increase in rental price is reflected in the renewal contract. There is a time difference in the monthly rent consumer price as it reflects the existing contract. Even if the price of a new contract rises, the burden on existing tenants changes at the time of renewal.

Third, the sustainability of the forecast of 13,212 households in 2028. This figure is an estimate that reflects the current permit and construction start plan, and will vary depending on the speed of future project approval and construction start.

Fourth, interest rates. The results of the Monetary Policy Committee meeting on November 26 and the FOMC meeting in December have not been released. Market expectations are not the result.

## 6. Next gate — three numbers, three dates

There are three numbers that are meaningful to both tenants and buyers. Seoul apartment sales are 0.03% vs. jeonse at 0.14%, 4,031 households moved into the metropolitan area in November (-49% compared to the previous month), and the jeonse loan interest rate is 4.57%.

There are also three dates. The US October PCE (10:30 p.m. Korean time) on November 25, the Bank of Korea Monetary Policy Committee meeting on November 26, and the FOMC on December 8-9. After three schedules, the direction of interest rates and jeonse loan interest rates are sorted out.

The last thing to check is your contract, not the market average. Number of months remaining until renewal, current deposit and loan balance, and monthly housing costs you can afford under your next contract. These three lines must be present for the indicator to become the basis for judgment.

The strong jeonse price will subside only when interest rates and supply are released simultaneously. Interest rates are on the rise, and the quantity of occupancy is set to decrease until 2028. The first variable that will shake up this structure is whether the 28,000 units will actually begin moving in in the first quarter of 2027.
