title: Naphtha is −9.5%, but PC is −0.9% — Playback PC is Shinjae’s 6-discount weekly
deck: While naphtha fell 9.5% in one week, PC fell only 0.9%, and PP·PE fell by around 6%, reflecting the decline in raw materials. Recycled PC regrind costs $1,200, the two regulatory axes that have already come into effect in 2026, and the cost per kg for a 20-ton shipment are summarized on one page.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: Raw material costs plummeted, but PCs held on. In the week when naphtha (CFR Japan) fell 9.53% from $890.75 to $805.88, PC fell only 0.94%, while PP -6.20% and LDPE -5.59% almost directly reflected the decline in raw materials. The spread of PC compounders has improved, and general-purpose PP/PE processing is experiencing raw material inventory valuation losses.

Playback PC is still below 60% of Shinjae’s. PC regrind CFR Korea's USD 1,200/ton (as of 11/5) is KRW 1,603 per kg, which is 57% of the KRW 2,818 per kg converted to Chinese PC spot at the same exchange rate on the same day. Even within the same playing PC, there is a $400 to $500 gap between regular regrind and high-quality PCR ($1,600 to $1,700).

Regulations have already begun in 2026. The EU PPWR went into general application on August 12, 2026, and in Korea, the mandatory use of 10% recycled PET bottle raw materials has been in effect since January. The 15% increase plan for 2027 is in the state of administrative notice (2026-09-07), and the 2027 cost will be different for companies that currently set the quality, quantity, and verification conditions of raw material supply contracts and those that do not.
body:
Write the conclusion first. In the 4th week of November (11/16 - 11/20), the petrochemical raw material market moved in one direction, **only polycarbonate (PC) deviated from that direction.** While naphtha fell 9.5% in a week, PC fell only 0.94%, and PP and PE fell 5-6%, almost directly reflecting the decline in raw materials. The three branches of the same raw material chain that gave different answers are the focus of this week.

This article is the first issue of the raw material market situation brief written every Friday based on notices. All values ​​listed are announced and evaluated prices confirmed from free and public sources, and no estimates were included. The base date and unit were written for each item, and the tariff rate and customs clearance costs used in the calculation example were indicated as assumptions. There are no notices on weekends, so the values ​​from 11/20 (Fri) are the most recent.

## Naphtha −9.5%, PC −0.9%, PP −6.2%

Write down this week’s five key points one by one.

- **Polycarbonate (PC)** — China spot general grade **14,116.67 yuan/ton**. −0.94% for the week, −0.59% for the previous day.
- **ABS Resin** — China spot general grade **11,583.33 yuan/ton**. −2.93% for the week, −0.86% for the previous day.
- **Polypropylene (PP)** — L5E89 (raffia) **10,083.33 yuan/ton**. −6.20% for the week, −0.66% for the previous day.
- **Naphtha (MOPJ)** — CFR Japan valuation **$805.88/ton**. -9.53% from $890.75 the previous week, -0.74% the previous day.
- **Won·Dollar** — Seoul foreign exchange market closing price at 15:30 **1,336.20 won**. 1,336.70 won the previous week, -0.04%, and -0.50 won the previous day.

PC, ABS, and PP are SunSirs China spot prices, naphtha is CommodityScope CFR Japan valuation price, and the exchange rate is the Bank of Korea Seoul Foreign Exchange Market weekly trading closing price (11/20). The previous week's value was calculated from the weekly fluctuation rate and standard value announced by the relevant source.

> Yuan/ton value is China's domestic spot price (VAT included), and differs from Korean import negotiators depending on grade, volume, freight, and payment conditions. Use direction as an indicator and not as an actual estimate.

### Raw Material Chain and Freight — Supporting Indicators

- **Basic fraction** — Ethylene (C2) 9,900.00 yuan/ton unchanged · Propylene (C3) 10,244.33 yuan/ton (previous day −0.16%) · Benzene 7,536.67 yuan/ton (−6.22%) · Styrene monomer (SM) 9,804.00 yuan/ton (+0.14%).
- **General purpose resin** — LDPE (2426H) 10,983.33 yuan/ton (−5.59%) · HDPE (5000S) 10,400.00 yuan/ton (−2.92%).
- **Engineering** — PMMA 14,733.33 yuan/ton. It is unchanged from the previous day (0.00%), but +1.84% compared to the beginning of the month.
- **Shipping/Crude Oil** — BDI 2,898 points (−2.75%) · Baltic Panamax (BPI) 2,140 points (+1.04%) · WTI $83.98/barrel (−5.17%).

There are three points to read. First, **C2·C3 barely moved, but PP·PE fell by 5-6%.** This means that this is a week in which demand and inventory factors, not raw materials, have driven down prices, and if raw materials rebound next week, processing margins will be squeezed first. Second, **PMMA is flat, but PC is down.** A compounder who handles two items together must look at the point where the directions diverge. Third, **BDI is -2.75%, but Panamax alone is +1.04%**, the highest since October 22nd. Companies that import raw materials in bulk rather than small containers must confirm that the directions of Cape (−4.6%) and Panamax are different.

![Petrochemical plants and recycled plastic raw materials, raw material price flow — Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/pcr-recycled-resin-weekly-brief-01.jpg)

## Playback PC is still below 60% of Shinjae’s

Recycled raw materials do not have a single published price like new materials. The values ​​below have **different sources and reference dates**, so compare them only within the same line, and do not directly subtract the values ​​between lines.

- **PC Regrind (CFR Korea)** — $1,200/ton, 2026-11-05, Polymer in Stock public selling price.
- **rPC Natural (Asia)** — $1,300~1,450/ton, 2026-09-11, Fukutomi Recycling Weekly Report Korean translation.
- **High-quality PCR PC (Asia)** — $1,600-1,700/ton, 2026-09-11, same report.
- **PC new material (China spot)** — 14,116.67 yuan/ton, 2026-11-20, SunSirs.
- **Domestic recycled pellets** — ABS 1,423.3 won/kg, PE 981.2 won/kg, PP 793.7 won/kg. 2026-09-10 Survey, Korea Environment Corporation recyclable resource price survey.

Three things to read from rPC this week.

1. **1,200 dollars/ton (CFR Korea) is 1,603 won per kg.** This is the value applied at the exchange rate of 1,336.20 won. On the same day, Chinese PC spot price of 14,116.67 yuan/ton is equivalent to 2,818 won per kg at the yuan-won exchange rate of 199.65 won. Although it is not an exact multiplier due to differences in whether spot, VAT, and freight charges are included, the direction is clear that remanufactured PCs are below 60% of new ones.
2. **The grade gap within the same reproduction PC is $400 to $500.** A high-quality PCR PC is $1,600 to $1,700, which is 33 to 42% more expensive than a regular regrind. Demand for “verified renewable raw materials”, such as EU PPWR or mandatory domestic use, pays for this top. Here, the presence or absence of GRS·ISCC PLUS certificate is added.
3. **The domestic recycled pellet notice (September) only increased for ABS.** It was 1,423.3 won/kg, up 19.5 won from the previous month, and PE and PP fell by 8.7 won and 2.2 won, respectively. Considering that new PP fell 6.2% this week, domestic recycled PP pellets are also under downward pressure in October and November. However, the October and November notices require confirmation after announcement.

## Regulations have already begun in 2026

### EU packaging and packaging waste regulations (PPWR, Regulation (EU) 2025/40)

- **General application 2026-08-12.** It is applied directly throughout the EU without member state legislation, and is subject to conformity assessment, technical documentation, declaration and identification.
- **Minimum content of recycled raw materials 2030-01-01.** Contact sensitive PET is 30%, other contact sensitive materials are 10%, disposable beverage bottles are 30%, and other plastic packaging is 35%. On 2040-01-01, it increases to 50%, 25%, 65%, and 65%.
- ** Recognition of recycled raw materials from third countries 2027-11-21. ** Until then, only recycling within the EU and EEA regions is recognized as performance, and thereafter, third countries that meet requirements such as OECD are also recognized.
- **Recycling design grade.** 2030-01-01 Grades A to C are assigned and the release of non-assigned packaging is prohibited, and from 2038-01-01, the release of grade C is also prohibited.
- **Calculation and Verification Implementation Act.** The Commission plans to establish a method for calculating and verifying the content of recycled raw materials by 2026-12-31.

There are three things that change in practice. First, from 2027, customers who send packaging materials and finished products to the EU will ask “where the recycled raw materials were recycled.” Second, since only recycling within the EU is recognized before 2027-11-21, **conditions for selling Korean rPC·rPP to EU buyers will open after 2028.** Before that, it is necessary to check the procurement within the EU or the method of calculating chemical recycling performance. Third, on the contrary, domestic and Asian customers try to secure suppliers in advance that meet EU standards.

### Obligation to use domestic plastic recycled raw materials

- **Basis** — Article 33-3 of the Act on the Promotion of Saving and Recycling of Resources (newly established on 2023-03-28, effective on 2025-03-25), Ministry of Environment Notice No. 2025-165 (enforced on 2025-10-01).
- **Target** — Businesses that manufacture drinking spring water and non-alcoholic beverages using more than 5,000 tons of plastic bottles per year.
- **Mandatory rate** — A revision to increase the rate to 10% in 2026 (effective 2026-01-01) and 15% in 2027 was administratively announced (2026-09-07, opinion collection 9/30). If confirmed, it will take effect in 2027.
- **Mid- to long-term** — By 2030, the target will be expanded to more than 1,000 tons per year and the duty rate will be raised to 30%.

> This system currently only applies to plastic bottles. Since PC, ABS, and PP are not yet mandatory, sales statements like “PC is also mandatory” are not true. What is actually effective for PC/ABS demand is the demands of global customers following the EU PPWR, certification requirements such as EPEAT, REACH, and RoHS, and cost reduction.

## Cost of a shipment of 20 tons — KRW 1,767 and KRW 1,663 per kg

It is a calculation framework used when deciding whether to “buy a new talent or a rebirth” in the same week. The three points below are assumptions, and actual estimates and tariffs vary depending on product classification, negotiated tax rates, and customs clearance conditions.

- Assumption 1 — Quantity 20 tons, price $1,200/ton CFR Korea (based on 11/5 public sale price).
- Assumption 2 — Exchange rate 1,336.20 won (11/20 Seoul foreign exchange market closing price).
- Assumption 3 — Tariff rate of 6.5% (general tax rate) or 0% (agreed tax rate), customs clearance and inland transportation KRW 1.2 million.

The calculation result is as follows.

- **Goods price** — $24,000 = 32,068,800 won (regardless of tariff assumptions).
- **Tariff** — KRW 2,084,472 assuming 6.5%, KRW 0 assuming 0%.
- **Customs clearance/inland transportation (assumed)** — KRW 1,200,000.
- **Total cost** — Assuming 6.5% **35,353,272 won (KRW 1,767.7 per kg)**, assuming 0% **33,268,800 won (KRW 1,663.4 per kg)**.
- **Note: Value added tax (input tax amount, subject to refund/deduction)** — KRW 3,415,327 / KRW 3,206,880.

This is how much the cost per kg moves when conditions fluctuate. If the exchange rate rises by 10 won, it is 12.0 won, if the tariff rate rises by 1% point, it is 16.0 won, if inland transportation increases by 1 million won, it is 50.0 won, and if pre-shipment inspection and samples cost 2 million won, it is 100.0 won.

**Interpretation** — In a shipment of 20 tons, 100 won per kg is 2 million won. When using a recycled PC as a replacement for a new one, if there is a difference of 300 to 500 won per kg, it becomes a problem of 6 to 10 million won per shipment. In other words, if you try to save 2 million won in inspection, sample, and reshipment costs but encounter a quality accident with 20 tons of volume, the loss will be 10 times higher. This is the reason for purchasing a separate inspection agency.

## See you next week

- **11/23 (Monday)** — Oil price, exchange rate, and LME announcements will resume after the weekend break. Let's see if this week's decline is reversed.
- **11/29 (Sat)** — OPEC+ meeting. The next variable in the direction of crude oil and naphtha.
- **End of December** — EU Commission adopts the Act on Implementation of Recycled Raw Material Content Calculation and Verification (until 2026-12-31).
- **Within the year** — Whether the revision of the notice on the obligation to use domestic recycled raw materials will be confirmed (15% in 2027).
- **Around the 10th of every month** — Korea Environment Corporation recyclable resource price survey. Check the October and November volumes.

## Principles of this brief

- Only values confirmed from public sources are included. Values ​​that cannot be confirmed are written as “unconfirmed.”
- Write the unit and base date for each item. Do not mix yuan/ton and dollar/ton, spot and futures, VAT included and separate.
- The original text (law, notice, regulation number) and date of announcement are included in the policy. Anything that is not confirmed is written as “in progress.”

title: Like a one-man company — The cost and profit structure of a one-person business changed by AI agents
deck: 1.16 million one-person creative businesses, an increase of 15.4% in one year. What automation reduces is execution, and what remains is judgment and responsibility.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: According to a survey by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, the number of domestic one-person creative businesses increased by 15.4% in one year to 1,162,529 at the end of 2023. The average sales per company is about 266.4 million won and net profit is about 36.2 million won.

According to the U.S. payment company Stripe, the proportion of new startups with one founder increased from 23.7% in 2019 to 36.3% in 2025. The number of one-person businesses with annual sales of $1 million or more has doubled over the past three years.

The cost structure in the domestic case is an AI subscription fee of 1 to 2 million won per month. On the other hand, a one-person AI agency in the United States disclosed examples such as $5,000 per customer per month, $40,000 in monthly sales, and $750 in cost. The figures have not been verified by my own announcement.
body:
AI agents shifted the bottleneck of one-person businesses from ‘number of people’ to ‘judgment speed’. Statistics and examples from 2026 show that this change has already changed the cost structure of the business.

## The spread of one-person businesses in numbers

According to the ‘2025 One-person Creative Enterprise Survey’ conducted by the Ministry of SMEs and Startups, the number of domestic one-person creative enterprises increased by 15.4% in one year to 1,162,529 at the end of 2023. The speed has changed compared to the previous survey increase rate of 2.0%. The industries are e-commerce at 27.9%, manufacturing at 21.2%, and education services at 17.1%. The average sales per company was about 266.4 million won and net profit was about 36.2 million won, an increase from the previous year.

The quality is still different. The average age of the representative is 55.1 years old, and the average work experience before starting the business is 16.3 years. It is closer to a means of re-entry for middle-aged people with expertise gained at work. This is a different phenomenon from the path of youth entrepreneurship.

![A worker moves between multiple AI agent screens in a one-person office — Image · AI Illustration](/assets/img/articles/agent-ai-solo-business-workflow.jpg)

The same direction is taking place overseas. According to the U.S. payment company Stripe, the proportion of new startups with one founder increased from 23.7% in 2019 to 36.3% in 2025. The number of one-person businesses with annual sales of more than $1 million has doubled in the past three years, and the number of one-person businesses with annual sales of more than $10 million has nearly tripled. It is reported that the number of one-person companies (OPCs) in China exceeds 16 million.

## What is automated, what remains

Most repetitive tasks are skipped over. Representative examples include marketing copy, blog and newsletter drafts, customer inquiry classification and first response, quotation draft, invoice sending, and schedule coordination. American automation consultant Nick Sarajev sold a product that reduces customer inquiry response time from an average of 4 hours to 15 minutes, and disclosed that he earns $20,000 to $40,000 a month by managing 6 to 8 retainers. The cost of the tool is said to be around $300 to $500 per month. Since this is a figure that was revealed by the person, it has not been verified with accounting data.

What remains is judgment and responsibility. It falls to humans to define the customer's problem, check whether the draft produced by AI is correct, and take responsibility when something goes wrong. The standards frequently used by solo operators when designing automation are also aligned with this. Is there repeatability, is the result reversible, and is there primary data to confirm the correct answer? Automation is done only when all three are ‘yes’, and outgoing tasks such as blog publishing, email sending, and payment are approved by humans.

## How do costs change?

In domestic cases, AI costs range from 1 million to 2 million won per month. Kim Tae-ho, CEO of healthcare startup TapZero, said he is entrusting app development and maintenance, taxation, accounting, and sales to AI for about 2 million won per month. The explanation is that if the same work had been done by people, 7 to 8 developers would have been needed.

There are also cases where lower costs are claimed. A founder who runs a content and marketing agency alone revealed that he generates $40,000 in monthly sales with a monthly operating cost of $750 (about 970,000 won). It is a ‘model roster’ approach where low-cost models handle the bulk of the work and people focus on strategy and customer relationships. This figure was confirmed only through secondary reporting because the original article was a paid post.

The domestic service market also formed a price range. Small projects range from KRW 100,000 to KRW 500,000, medium-sized projects range from KRW 500,000 to KRW 2 million, monthly retainers range from KRW 500,000 to KRW 3 million, and automation system design and operation range from KRW 5 to 10 million. This price range is a compilation of estimates and cases from industry insiders and is not an official statistic.

## The profit structure is three-pronged.

Project units are easy to start, but they run the risk of increasing scope. Monthly retainers generate recurring sales, but are vulnerable to customer churn. Performance-based contracts are easy to contract, but it is difficult to agree on performance measures and the initial income may be zero. What is important for a one-person business is the distribution of the number of customers rather than the size of sales. This is why the advice to maintain 6 to 10 retainers is repeated.

The limitations of the Korean market are also clear. Many of the one-person startups are concentrated in livelihood services such as wholesale/retail, lodging, and restaurants, and the proportion of high-value startups targeting the global market with AI is low. As AI tools lower the barrier to entry, the intensity of competition has also increased. As the number of people using the same tool increases, the difference ultimately comes down to domain knowledge and customer access.

## What Automation Doesn't Create

AI agents reduce execution but do not create trust. Customers buy the quality of the results and responsibility. If an agent determines several steps on its own, it is difficult to track what went wrong at which step when an accident occurs. The same problem is the gap in responsibility distribution and damage relief pointed out by the National Assembly Research Service in November 2026.

What has not been confirmed is the universality of the ‘one-person unicorn’. Success stories usually rely on the sales and costs disclosed by the person, and failure cases are not counted. What is certain now is that the cost of tools has dropped to one-tenth of the cost of labor, and the scope of work that can be done alone has expanded accordingly.

title: The search is over and the citations have begun — New rules for Naver UGC and Google AI overview
deck: When the AI ​​overview appeared, external clicks decreased by 39.8%. Naver fills 70% of citations with its own UGC. Where is the value of content determined?
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: When the Google AI overview is displayed, clicks on external websites are 0.37 times per search, which is 39.8% less than when it is not displayed (0.62 times). The percentage of people completing searches without clicking increased from 54% to 73%.

The AI ​​overview exposure rate increased from 5.93% in September 2024 to 61.43% in August 2026. On the other hand, about 70% of the content cited by Naver's AI briefing is Naver's own UGC, including Naver's blog, cafe, and Knowledge iN.

On November 5, 2026, Naver introduced the 'Experience UGC Block', which groups experiences and reviews by topic, and on October 8, Google unveiled the 'UGC Fresh Data Program', which allows the community to directly send the latest posts and reaction data.
body:
The purpose of search has changed from ‘sending to good pages’ to ‘directly showing good answers.’ As a result, the value of content began to be measured by citations rather than clicks.

## Clicks decreased, citations increased

There is an experiment measuring the effectiveness of Google's AI overview. Researchers in the U.S. and India divided U.S. desktop Chrome users into a group that displayed AI overview and a group that did not display AI outlines and compared them for two weeks between January and February 2026. In searches with the AI ​​overview displayed, external site clicks were 0.37 times per search, and searches without the AI ​​outline were 0.62 times per search. The difference is 39.8%. The percentage of people completing a search without clicking on an external site jumped from 54% to 73%.

Exposure increased rapidly. According to Data for SEO, the percentage of AI overviews displayed in Google searches increased from 5.93% in September 2024 to 61.43% in August 2026. During the same period, the top highlighted snippet rate decreased from 8.96% to 0.44%. Liz Reed, head of Google search, countered that total outgoing natural search clicks were relatively stable compared to the previous year after the introduction of AI features, but did not disclose specific figures.

The citations and rankings are also inconsistent. According to SEO analysis company Areps, the percentage of pages cited in the AI ​​overview that also appeared in the top 10 results for the same search term was about 38% in March 2026. Being exposed at the top and being cited have become two different games.

![AI summary above search results and list of cited articles below — Images · AI Illustrations](/assets/img/articles/search-to-ai-ugc-selection.jpg)

## Naver found the answer in its own ecosystem

Naver’s choice is in the opposite direction. According to Naver, as of January 2026, the proportion of its UGC among the content cited by the AI ​​briefing was 70%. This means that blogs, cafes, knowledge iN, and premium content are the source of the answer. Naver announced that it will block external AI crawling of its UGC by default starting in 2025 and will invest 1 trillion won in the content ecosystem over the next five years. ‘Naver Mate’, which selects creators frequently cited in AI briefings and provides them with activity fees, is also part of this.

On November 5, 2026, the 'Experience UGC Block' was introduced. When you search for 'Fukuoka travel', detailed topics such as 'Day trip around Fukuoka' are grouped into subheadings, and relevant sections of related blog and cafe posts are displayed. Subheadings, comments, and experience tags are given priority instead of the entire text.

There are also changes that emerged from the performance announcement. CEO Soo-yeon Choi said in an earnings presentation on February 6, 2026, that search terms longer than 15 characters have more than doubled since the launch of the AI ​​briefing, and clicks on follow-up questions within the briefing have increased more than six times.

## Google pulls in data from outside

Since Google does not have its own ecosystem, it joined hands with an external community. On October 8, 2026, the 'UGC Fresh Data Program' was released, allowing online communities and social media to transmit the latest posts and user reaction data. Rather than being scraped by a search robot, the approved platform sends it directly to a dedicated system. This is an extension of the data cooperation signed with Reddit in 2024.

## So what is cited?

There are five content creation principles that Naver revealed in May 2026. First-hand knowledge, consistent topic, authenticity without lies, easy-to-read structure, and up-to-date. On the other hand, it was revealed that repetitive keyword listings, fraudulent documents, pieces with unclear sources, and articles mechanically generated and summarized by AI are likely to be filtered out. There is no disadvantage just because an AI tool was used, but the condition is that the creator's actual experience and review must be included.

Measurement tools are still asymmetric. Google has a generative AI performance report in Search Console and also provides settings to exclude only AI functions. Naver did not disclose a report indicating the status of AI briefing citations on an external website. The number of citations is displayed only in search results and profiles of creators selected as mates. Site operators have no choice but to create a set of questions and directly check for citations once or twice a month while logged out.

## Calculation of content providers

What has changed is the distribution channel. Even if search traffic decreases, the brand is exposed when cited in AI answers, and there is analysis that users who click even after seeing the summary have clear purchase intentions. Conversely, if you are not cited, your traffic and brand will disappear. Therefore, the focus of recent practice is not ‘top exposure’ but ‘citable structure’. Information that changes, such as prices and policies, should leave an update date, and key information in the image should also be written in text.

What has not been confirmed is how much Naver AI Briefing has reduced the inflow of external sites. Naver did not disclose related statistics. Google's 39.8% is also an experiment with American desktop users, so it cannot be applied to all searches. What is certain now is that the total number of clicks has decreased and competition for citations has begun.

title: The bottleneck in AI data centers is not chips, but power and memory values.
deck: Data center demand in 2027 is 27GW, with 22GW available for NVIDIA. HBM is sold out, and 93% of power system reviews are data centers.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: Hana Securities estimated the new data center demand for hyperscaler, neocloud, and sovereign AI in 2027 to be about 27GW. The scale that can be handled with NVIDIA GPUs is less than 22GW, and AMD is about 3GW.

HBM shipments in 2027 are estimated at a total of 4.9 billion GB, including 2 billion GB from Samsung Electronics, 2.3 billion GB from SK Hynix, and 600 million GB from Micron. DRAM demand increases by 27%, but supply only increases by 25%.

According to Korea Electric Power Corporation, data centers account for 62.8GW (93%) of the 67.4GW of power system impact assessment applications from August 2024 to June 2026. The volume that has completed the main review is only 7GW.
body:
The next bottleneck for AI data centers is not GPUs, but power and memory prices. Securities company, government, and industry data released in November 2026 say the same conclusion with different numbers.

## Demand is 27GW, available computing power is 22GW

In a report dated November 12, 2026, Hana Securities estimated the size of new data centers needed by major hyperscalers, NeoCloud, and Sovereign AI in 2027 to be approximately 27GW. The scale that can be handled with NVIDIA GPUs is less than 22GW, and AMD is about 3GW. The rest must be made up by Google TPU and self-developed AI chips. In 2027, NVIDIA data center GPU shipments are expected to exceed 8.96 million units, Google TPUs will exceed 8.8 million units, and hyperscaler chips will exceed 4 million units.

Memory is tighter. HBM shipments in 2027 total 4.9 billion GB, including 2 billion GB from Samsung Electronics, 2.3 billion GB from SK Hynix, and 600 million GB from Micron. As HBM's expansion encroaches on general DRAM production capacity, the DRAM supply growth rate is limited to 25%. The demand growth rate is 27%. By 2027, server shipments will increase by 15% to 27 million units, and servers will account for more than 50% of DRAM demand. On the other hand, smartphone and PC shipments will decrease by 7% and 8%, respectively. The structure is such that AI takes away the memory of general IT.

![Image depicting an AI data center connected by power lines and HBM stacked chips — Image · AI Illustration](/assets/img/articles/ai-datacenter-power-hbm-bottleneck.jpg)

## Memory values eat up capex

Big Tech’s investment scale is the largest ever. The total facility investment for 2026 announced by the five major U.S. big tech companies is $730 billion. Morgan Stanley predicted that Big Tech will invest $3 trillion in data centers between 2025 and 2028. The problem is memory's share of that money. According to Trend Force, the share of memory in cloud service providers' AI infrastructure spending will jump from about 47% in 2026 to 68% in 2027. JP Morgan sees memory's share of value in CSP capex as 31% in 2026 and 49% in 2027, up from less than 10% before AI.

Prices have already soared. Micron's average DRAM sales price in the third quarter of its fiscal year rose more than 260% compared to the same period last year, but shipments increased only in the low 20% range on a bit basis. The average DRAM sales price growth rate in 2026 is estimated to be 235%. JP Morgan predicted that the price of HBM in 2027 will rise 42% compared to the previous year. Customers survive by reducing payload. NVIDIA is testing a plan to lower the HBM load of Rubin Ultra, and server manufacturers are increasing the proportion of 32 and 64GB modules instead of 96 and 128GB DRAM. Memory Capex sees this as a problem of distribution of limited capital, not simply a response to a supply shortage.

## Power is the second wall

The power consumption of one AI server is up to 100kW. DigiTimes Research estimated that after the first GW-class data centers appear in 2026, 30% of the world's data centers will use more than 1GW by 2035.

The bottleneck in Korea remains the number in the screening queue. According to Korea Electric Power Corporation (KEPCO), the amount applied until June 2026 after the implementation of the power system impact assessment in August 2024 is 67.4GW. Among these, data centers account for 93%, or 62.8GW. The quantity that was judged ‘capable of supply’ in the first screening was 39.9GW, but the quantity that completed the main screening was only 7GW. Approximately 33GW remains between the first and main reviews.

The government chose to reduce procedures. On November 20, 2026, the Ministry of Science and ICT and the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment announced the enactment of the AIDC Special Act Enforcement Decree and Enforcement Rules. Data centers with a contracted power of 50 MW or less in non-metropolitan areas are exempt from power system impact assessment, and within AIDC special zones, non-technical assessments are omitted regardless of size. GW-level mega projects and projects requiring batch processing of licenses are evaluated first. The enforcement date of the special law is March 10, 2027.

The industry welcomed it, but was disappointed with the standards. Large data centers of hundreds of MW still need to be evaluated, and even if the evaluation period is shortened, securing transmission and substation networks is a separate task. The enforcement ordinance requires the construction start date to be reported within one year from the report date in order to prevent 'stupidity' of reporting construction but not starting construction.

## Where is Korea’s place?

Korea stands on both sides of this bottleneck. Those selling HBM and server DRAM benefit from price increases. At the same time, those who want to build an AI data center are blocked in power, licensing, and parts procurement. One 100MW hyperscale data center contains approximately 40,000 GPUs, approximately 330,000 HBMs, approximately 170,000 FC-BGAs, approximately 330 million MLCCs, and approximately 80 cooling distribution devices. If one part is late, trillions of servers will be idle.

What is not confirmed is whether this demand will continue beyond 2028. Equipment will be installed at Samsung Electronics P5, SK Hynix Yongin Y1, and Micron Idaho factories in 2027, but actual supply will occur after 2028. In the meantime, if memory prices rise further, demand may decline first. The way to resolve the bottleneck may be to adjust demand rather than expand supply.

title: It can be prevented even without selling chips — controlling US-China AI that has spread to the cloud
deck: The United States now looks at the end users of the computation rather than the destination of the chips. In that gap, the Korean and Japanese sub-directors are tied up again.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: On November 16, 2026, the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security announced an interim final rule regulating remote use of advanced AI semiconductors through third-country data centers. If a customer's total processing capacity exceeds 12 million, permission is required, and existing contracts must also receive permission within 90 days.

Export of cutting-edge chips to five countries, including Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil, requires prior permission. Although Korea is not on this list, domestic data centers can also be subject to approval if they provide calculations that exceed the standard to customers of the Chinese ultimate parent company.

Korea and Japan became closer again at Sobujang. Samsung Electronics invested 40 billion yen over five years into an advanced packaging research base in Yokohama, and SK Hynix shared its technology roadmap with about 20 Japanese partners. Japan accounts for 48% of the semiconductor materials market and 31% of the equipment market.
body:
The United States changed the standard for controlling semiconductors from ‘where the chips go’ to ‘who uses the calculations’. The interim final rule announced by the U.S. Department of Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) on November 16, 2026 (local time) is the turning point.

## What has changed?

Existing controls targeted the overseas transfer of semiconductors and equipment. The service-type GPU, which rents a graphics processing unit (GPU) from a third country data center over the Internet, was a blind spot. In order to prevent this route, BIS requires permission if the customer's headquarters or ultimate parent company is located in a country with security concerns, such as China or Macau, and the total processing capacity (TPP) provided exceeds 12 million. When multiple data centers are bundled together for service, computing power is added up. Businesses that have already provided services must obtain permission within 90 days from the effective date to continue the contract.

The chip import step was also tightened. Prior permission is required when exporting or transferring regulated chips to five countries, including Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil. Korea was not among these five countries. However, domestic data centers may also be subject to approval if they provide calculations that exceed the standard to customers whose ultimate parent company is in China. Shin Won-gyu, head of the global economy team at the Korea Economic Research Institute, said, “Domestic AI data centers and foundries may also be required to establish a management system that verifies the ultimate parent company and purpose of use of the customer.”

![Image depicting data center server racks and a semiconductor supply chain crossing the ocean — Image · AI Illustration](/assets/img/articles/us-china-ai-chip-supply-chain.jpg)

## Why now?

The trigger was the measure taken by BIS in January 2026 to restrict cloud services to Chinese users when exporting the H200 class. It only applied to semiconductors exported with U.S. permission, so it did not block other channels. Added to this was the scandal that led to the resignation of former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. There are suspicions that at least $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia chips were supplied indirectly through Singaporean company Megaspeed. Even U.S. intelligence officials have not been able to conclude whether there is a connection to Chinese intelligence agencies.

Congress also moves. The 'Remote Access Security Act (RASA)', which regulates remote access through the cloud, passed the House of Representatives with a vote of 369 to 22 in January and is pending in the Senate. The House plan narrows the target of regulation to foreigners in general, while the Senate plan narrows it to users related to countries of concern, such as China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. If the House of Representatives bill is adopted, Korean companies that use US-made GPUs overseas may also be subject to approval.

China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs objected on November 17, saying it was an "abuse of export controls." U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Besant said on CNBC on November 20 that there will be no change in the policy to allow H200 to be sold to the public. The baseline is H200, meaning lower grades are still allowed.

## The market has already priced in

The Korean stock market read this regulation as a result of its performance. On November 20, KOSPI plunged 5.21% to 4,869.96, hitting its lowest point in 10 months. Samsung Electronics -7.01%, SK Hynix -5.92%. The Financial Times reported on November 19 that Samsung Electronics and TSMC stopped shipping some chips to Chinese customers. Confirmation of the two companies was not made public.

Korea’s AI business is deeply intertwined with NVIDIA. SK Group signed a letter of intent worth more than $500 billion with NVIDIA in July 2026, and Naver received $1 billion and acquired a 4.13% stake. As a significant portion of HBM's sales are concentrated in NVIDIA, strengthening controls is a two-way risk. As we lose Chinese customers, due diligence demands from American customers increase.

## In that gap, the Korean and Japanese prosecutors are tied up again.

As the difficulty of HBM and advanced packaging increases, the precision of materials and equipment determines the yield. According to Japan's Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, Japanese companies account for about 48% of the global semiconductor materials market and about 31% of the manufacturing equipment market. Tokyo Electron holds more than 90% of the photoresist coating and development equipment market, and the three Japanese companies hold 97% of the EUV photoresist market.

Samsung Electronics opened its Advanced Packaging Research Base (APL) in Yokohama on September 8, 2026. 40 billion yen (about 350 billion won) will be invested over five years from 2024, and the Japanese government and Yokohama City will provide up to 22.5 billion yen. It is 56% of the total investment amount. SK Hynix held its first Partners Day in Chiba Prefecture on October 29 and shared its mid- to long-term roadmap with about 20 companies, including Shin-Etsu Chemical, Sumco, JSR, Tokyo Electron, and Disco.

Cooperation does not respect borders. Samsung Electro-Mechanics established a glass substrate materials joint venture worth 480 billion won with Dongwoo Fine-Chem in July. However, in an analysis by the Korea Institute for International Economic Policy, the share of Japanese products in hydrogen fluoride imports from January 2024 to August 2025 was 46.8%, which was higher than that of Chinese products (27.5%). Dependence, which had decreased since 2019, has increased again.

## Remaining Questions

What has been confirmed is the text and schedule of the rules and the company's investment. What is not known is how much this regulation will actually reduce China's computing power. Since regulations are aimed at ownership and use of servers, not their location, they must be pursued whenever a detour occurs. Korean companies are left with customer due diligence costs and loss of sales in China.

title: China's PC has become an exporter — prices rising from naphtha to renewable raw materials
deck: China ethylene 62.9 million tons, PC world 53%. Domestic petrochemical company's operating loss in the third quarter was 269.1 billion won. The prices of virgin and recycled raw materials fluctuate together.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: China's ethylene production capacity increased by 80% from 34.9 million tons in 2020 to 62.9 million tons in 2025, and the PE import ratio fell from 63% to 21% in the first half of 2026. In the second half of 2026, China's new olefin and aromatics capacity will exceed 34 million tons.

China's PC production capacity is 4.32 million tons in 2025, which is more than 53% of the world's. In May 2026, monthly PC exports exceeded imports for the first time, making Korea a net exporter. China's PC imports from Korea amounted to $361.49 million in 2025, down 13.8% from the previous year.

The combined operating loss of 10 domestic petrochemical companies in the third quarter was 269.1 billion won. The ethylene spread ranged from $315 per ton in April to $69 per ton in July and $170 in October, below the break-even point ($250-$300). A remanufactured PC costs around $1,300 to $1,450, and a high-quality PCR costs around $1,600 to $1,700.
body:
China has gone from a country that bought cheap plastic to a country that sells it. The change is pushing in the same direction, starting with naphtha and ethylene, and extending to polycarbonate (PC) and recycled raw material prices.

## The landscape of raw materials has changed

China's ethylene production capacity increased by 80% from 34.9 million tons in 2020 to 62.9 million tons in 2025. Polyethylene (PE) increased by 75% from 23.4 million tons to 41.1 million tons. This is a figure from a report released by the U.S. Rhodium Group on November 2, 2026. China maintained ethylene production while reducing crude oil imports by 4 to 5 million barrels per day. This is the result of using stockpiled crude oil, naphtha, and raw materials based on coal and natural gas.

Import dependence decreased rapidly. China's PE production-to-import ratio decreased from 63% in 2020 to 21% in the first half of 2026. Eugene Investment & Securities estimated that China's new olefin and aromatics production capacity will exceed 34 million tons in the second half of 2026. It is about 8 times the 4.35 million tons in the first half of the year. 6 million tons of ethylene, 5 million tons of PE, 6.96 million tons of propylene, 4.7 million tons of PP, and 2.77 million tons of PX are concentrated in the second half of the year.

## PC has already become a net exporter

China's PC production capacity increased by an average of 15.5% annually from 1.66 million tons in 2019 to 3.81 million tons in 2024, and accounted for more than 53% of the world's total to 4.32 million tons in 2025 (KOTRA Nanjing Trade Center). The operating rate is expected to rise to around 85% in 2026, and industry profits have also recovered.

The decisive event is May 2026. China's monthly PC exports exceeded imports for the first time and turned into net exports. The industry advanced the original estimate of 2028 by two years. Korea is still China's largest importer of PCs, but the amount is decreasing. In 2025, China's PC imports from Korea amounted to $361.49 million, a 13.83% decrease from the previous year. Thailand (-6.43%), Taiwan (-16.86%), and Japan (-10.48%) also decreased.

Prices are depressed. According to Hong Kong's Fukutomi Recycling weekly market situation, Chinese PC prices on November 13 were 11,850 yuan per ton, down 2.9% from the previous week. In the same week, ABS fell 7.0%, PE fell 7.2%, and PP fell 7.5%. PMMA alone remained flat at 15,100 yuan.

![Naphtha cracking equipment and plastic raw material granules, export containers at Chinese ports — Image · AI Illustration](/assets/img/articles/china-petchem-glut-naphtha-resin.jpg)

## Domestic performance is already in deficit

As a result of the Korea Economic Daily's compilation of the third quarter performance of 10 companies, including Lotte Chemical, LG Chemical, Kumho Petrochemical, and Hanwha Solution, the combined operating loss was 269.1 billion won. The operating profit in the second quarter was 1.5078 trillion won, which was overturned in one quarter. Lotte Chemical - KRW 281.4 billion, LG Chemical's petrochemical division - KRW 176 billion, and Kumho Petrochemical - KRW 20.8 billion. Kumho Petrochemical's quarterly deficit is the first in 11 years since the fourth quarter of 2015.

The cause is twofold. Although profits were made in the second quarter from naphtha purchased cheaply at the beginning of the Middle East war, expensive raw materials were used in the third quarter (reverse lagging). Naphtha prices fell 28% from $1,064 per ton in April to $770 in early June, and product prices collapsed even sooner. The ethylene spread ranged from $315 in April to $69 in July and $170 in October, far below the break-even point ($250-$300).

The structure is also bad. Shinhan Investment & Securities predicted that China's ethylene capacity will increase by 15.3 million tons between 2026 and 2028, while Asian facility closures will only amount to more than 5.3 million tons. In Korea, the Daesan facility and Yeocheon NCC are scheduled to be shut down in 2027, but the expansion of the S-Oil Shaheen project offsets this. An LG Chem official predicted continued oversupply in the third quarter conference call, saying, "8 million tons are expected to be shut down in Northeast Asia by 2031, but new capacity will be 29 million tons."

## Waves coming to the renewable raw materials market

As the price of virgin resin falls, the premium of recycled raw materials also comes under pressure. As of September 2026, Asian recycled PC (rPC, natural color) was traded at $1,300 to $1,450 per ton, and high-quality PCR was traded at $1,600 to $1,700. It should be taken into account that the price varies depending on the quantity and grade of raw material recovery, and that it is a regional benchmark rather than a confirmed contract price.

As China's PC self-sufficiency has increased, price competition for general-purpose recycled raw materials may become more intense. Conversely, demand for high-quality PCR remains in fields with high requirements for physical properties, such as automobiles, electronics, and optics. Chinese companies are also moving from general purpose to high added value, so if domestic importers and distributors do not differentiate by grade and use, they will face a drop in virgin prices.

## Confirmed and not confirmed

What has been confirmed is China's capacity expansion, net export shift, and domestic deficit. What has not been confirmed is the timing of the rebound after 2027. China's Longzhong Information said that there are no confirmed plans for new introduction and operation of large PCs in 2026, but there are also observations that a new expansion cycle may begin in the second half of 2027. International oil prices, the situation in the Middle East, and exchange rates are variables. What is certain now is that the number of suppliers has increased, not the cost of raw materials.

title: Dividends are at an all-time high, but why is there so little left in the bank account?
deck: Shareholder returns have increased due to separate taxation, cancellation of treasury stocks, and revision of the Commercial Act. However, taxes and supply and demand filter personal cash flow again.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: With the implementation of separate taxation of dividend income on January 1, 2026, shareholders of high-dividend companies can now be subject to a tax rate of 14-30% instead of the maximum 49.5%. As of the 2025 fiscal year, there are 629 listed companies with high dividends.

Quarterly and interim dividends in the third quarter were KRW 62.3526 trillion, 3.5 times the amount a year ago (KRW 17.5877 trillion). Samsung Electronics 4,601 won (about 30 trillion won) and SK Hynix 20,000 won (about 14 trillion won) accounted for the majority.

The cancellation of treasury stocks became mandatory on March 6, 2026, and the cancellation amount in 2025 was 21.4 trillion won. However, since minority shareholders are only taxed on dividends and not on the acquisition or cancellation of treasury stock, controversy over equity remains.
body:
Although shareholder returns have increased, cash entering personal bank accounts goes through taxes and supply once more. The numbers confirmed in the domestic stock market in 2026 show that the size of the return and the investor's share are not the same thing.

## How much has the dividend increased?

The third quarter dividend is symbolic. As a result of Electronic Newspaper's analysis of Korea Exchange dividend decision announcements, the number of listed companies that decided on quarterly and interim dividends from April to November 10, 2026 was 190, an increase of 39 from a year ago (151). The total amount increased 3.5 times from 17.5877 trillion won to 62.3526 trillion won. The effect of Samsung Electronics' decision of 4,601 won (approximately 30 trillion won) per share on October 29 and SK Hynix's decision of 20,000 won (approximately 14 trillion won) per share the day before was significant. Even excluding the two companies, it increased by 35% from 9.456 trillion won to 12.7978 trillion won.

Annually, it is in the same direction. The number of listed companies paying dividends in 2025 was 1,246, an increase of 56 from a year ago, and the total dividend amount was 37.7519 trillion won, an increase of 16.9%. The 2025 cash dividend of securities market corporations settled in December was KRW 52.8 trillion, the highest ever (National Assembly Research Service).

## How have taxes changed?

As the Restriction of Special Taxation Act, revised on December 23, 2025, came into effect on January 1, 2026, separate taxation was applied to the dividend income of high-dividend listed companies. The requirement is for a company to have a dividend payout ratio of 40% or more without reducing cash dividends from the previous year, or a company that has a dividend payout ratio of 25% or more and increased dividends by more than 10% compared to the previous year. The shareholder can pay dividend income at a tax rate of 14-30% without adding it to other income. The difference is large compared to the highest comprehensive tax rate for financial income of 49.5%.

As of the 2025 fiscal year, there are 629 listed companies with high dividends (283 in securities, 346 in KOSDAQ).

## Buy and eliminate treasury stock

As a result of the amendment to the Commercial Act that took effect on March 6, 2026, newly acquired treasury stocks must, in principle, be retired within one year, and any shares held before enforcement must be disposed of by September 5, 2027. Exceptions include shareholder distribution, executive and employee compensation, organizational reorganization, and management purposes specified in the Articles of Incorporation, which require approval at a general shareholders' meeting.

The market moved before the law. The acquisition amount of listed companies' treasury stocks increased from KRW 4.8 trillion in 2021 to KRW 20.1 trillion in 2025, and the cancellation amount increased from KRW 2.5 trillion to KRW 21.4 trillion during the same period. Samsung Electronics decided to burn 82.5% (87 million shares) of its treasury stocks, and SK Hynix will burn all of its purchases worth 40 trillion won in October.

![Image of dividend notice, treasury stock being canceled, and cash flow from personal account overlaid — Image · AI Illustration](/assets/img/articles/korea-shareholder-return-cashflow.jpg)

## But why is the bank account the same?

First, taxes vary depending on the method of reduction. According to a report published by the National Assembly Research Service on October 13, minority shareholders of listed companies bear dividend income tax on cash dividends, but do not incur a tax burden on stock repurchase on the market or reserve reduction dividends. Depending on the method of majority shareholder ownership, it is taxed as dividend income or capital gain and the tax rate varies. Even if you share the same profits, the amount you receive varies depending on how you receive it.

Second, if the cancellation of treasury stocks increases, the company may fall out of the high dividend requirement. The dividend payout ratio and dividend growth rate, which are special requirements, are calculated only from cash dividends. Among the 629 companies, 58 (9.2%) acquired their own shares between January 2025 and June 2026, and among the 126 companies with a dividend payout ratio of 25% or more, 20 (15.9%). If they increase incineration, their capacity for cash dividends will decrease and they may be excluded from special treatment. The investigation office proposed to consider a plan to reflect the incineration requirements within the legal deadline.

Third, stock prices and supply and demand remain. KOSPI plunged 5.21% to 4,869.96 on November 20, hitting its lowest point in 10 months, and its market capitalization decreased to 3,991 trillion won. On the same day, individuals net purchased 1.5955 trillion won, but as of the 19th, investor deposits amounted to 81.5669 trillion won, a decrease of 10.6678 trillion won in one week. The credit transaction loan balance is 26.0832 trillion won. From November 9th to 13th, counter sales against KOSPI receivables amounted to KRW 133 billion, which was 3.3 times the previous week (KRW 40.2 billion). The structure is such that the cash received as dividends cannot offset the decline in stock prices and forced liquidation.

## The quality of reduction is still a work in progress.

What is confirmed is that the system has changed and companies have responded. What is not confirmed is whether this return leads to long-term holding by individual investors. In October, net purchases of U.S. stocks by domestic investors amounted to $5.42 billion, the highest this year on a monthly basis, and foreigners net sold domestic stocks worth $19.31 billion. It is also observed that the refinancing resources do not stay within the country but go abroad.

As a mid- to long-term task, the National Assembly Research Service proposed the introduction of Japanese-style ‘distributable profits under tax law’ and full separate taxation of dividend income. This is because the current special case is limited in scope and period, making it difficult to support a stable corporate return policy. Increased dividends and wealthier shareholders are still two different things.

title: The illusion that 1,330 won is ‘stability’ — three bills left behind by the fixed exchange rate
deck: It fell 9% from a year ago, but has been stuck in the 1,330 won range since September. I divided the bill by import price, shopping cart, and dollar demand.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: The won/dollar exchange rate closed at 1,336.2 won on November 20. It went from an average of 1,527.30 won in June to the 1,330 won range in September and stayed in the 1,330-1,340 won range for over two months. The average in October 2026 is 1,337.66 won.

Import prices in October fell 1.8% from the previous month, but are 13.5% higher than the same month last year. In the same month, consumer prices rose 2.8%, processed foods rose 2.9%, dining out 2.9%, and petroleum rose 14.9%. The drop in exchange rates did not reach the shopping cart.

The current account surplus from January to September was $340.66 billion, more than four times that of the same period last year. However, foreign stock funds had a net outflow of $19.31 billion in October, and net purchases of U.S. stocks by domestic investors were $5.42 billion. Demand for dollars is supporting the lower exchange rate.
body:
The 1,330 won range is not a ‘strong won’ but a ‘fixed exchange rate’. The won/dollar exchange rate, which reached 1,527 won in June 2026, fell to the 1,330 won range in September and has remained in the 1,330-1,340 won range for more than two months.

## How much did it fall and where is it stuck?

The closing price of the Seoul foreign exchange market on November 20 was 1,336.2 won, up 6.2 won from the previous trading day. It went down to 1,330.0 won on the 19th and 1,323.10 won on October 26th. The monthly average in October 2026 is 1,337.66 won. Compared to November 20th a year ago (1,467.90 won), it is 9.0% lower.

The amount of depression is decreasing. The average monthly exchange rate peaked at 1,527.30 won in June and fell for four consecutive months to 1,488.9 won in July, 1,404.4 won in August, 1,359.0 won in September, and 1,337.66 won in October, but the rate of decline narrowed from -5.7% in August to -3.2% in September and -1.6% in October. In November, it rose to 1,356.6 won on the 6th. The direction does not seem to have stopped, but seems to be blocked on both sides.

![Exchange rate graph staying in the 1,330 won range and dollar trading in the Seoul foreign exchange market — Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/sticky-won-dollar-1330-cost.jpg)

## Why isn’t it going down — even though dollars are coming in?

The first reason is the current account balance. According to the Bank of Korea, the current account surplus from January to September 2026 was $340.66 billion, more than four times the same period the previous year ($83.89 billion). Dollars created by semiconductor exports were released into the foreign exchange market.

There is a place that takes those dollars back. According to the Bank of Korea, foreigners' net outflow of domestic stock investment funds was $19.31 billion in October. The range increased from a net inflow of $40 million in August to a net outflow of $14.16 billion in September. Net purchases of U.S. stocks by domestic investors reached $5.42 billion in October, the highest monthly figure this year.

The figure calculated by Herald Economy using data from the Korea Exchange and Korea Securities Depository condenses this. Over the 52 trading days from September to November 17, foreigners sold a net worth of 54.4 trillion won in the domestic stock market, which, assuming they were converted to dollars, is an average of 780 million dollars per day. It is 2.4 times the amount from July to August (USD 330 million). Adding to this the purchases of foreign stocks by domestic investors ($188 million per day), $970 million per day moved toward the dollar.

US interest rates are also under upward pressure. Based on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange (CME) Fed Watch, the possibility that the U.S. Federal Reserve will raise the benchmark interest rate in December was reflected as 100% in mid-November. The probability of a 0.25 percentage point increase is 92.1%.

## First Bill — Company Costs and Margins

When the exchange rate falls, the cost of imports decreases. The import price index in October was 156.86 (2020 = 100), down 1.8% from the previous month. However, based on contract currency, the decline was only 0.2%. The remaining 1.6% points are an illusion created by the rise in the value of the won. Compared to the same month last year, import prices are still 13.5% higher.

The opposite direction is true for exporting companies. Export prices in October rose 0.7% from the previous month and 36.7% from the same month last year due to the rise in semiconductor prices. The strength of the won has a diminishing effect when money received in dollars is exchanged for won. In its explanation of its third quarter performance, LG Chem said that rising transportation costs and the strong won had put a strain on profitability. This is an area where the pros and cons of companies that buy raw materials and those that sell finished products are different.

## Second Bill — Time Differences in Shopping Cart

Consumer prices in October rose 2.8% compared to the same month last year. Although it is 0.1% lower than September (2.9%), it has been in the upper 2% range for two months. By item, processed foods rose 2.9%, instant foods 12.4%, bread and biscuits 5.9%, eating out 2.9%, and petroleum 14.9%.

The 13.5% increase in import prices in one year is the result of being passed on to prices over time. At the price situation review meeting on November 3, the Bank of Korea said, “We are alert to the transfer of accumulated cost pressure and increased demand-side pressure.” President Shin Hyeon-song also said, “There is a connection between the price transfer of costs and demand due to improved income conditions.” Even if the price of a new import contract falls, the passing on of already accumulated costs does not immediately stop.

## Third bill—cost for households to buy dollars

Households are now also parties to the exchange rate. Sell ​​won and buy dollars to finance overseas stocks, travel, and study abroad. Spreads and commissions attached when exchanging currency do not disappear even if the exchange rate fluctuates sideways. The company's foreign exchange hedging costs are ultimately shared by consumers.

## The next gate is November 26th

The Bank of Korea's Monetary Policy Committee determines the base interest rate on November 26. If the Bank of Korea raises interest rates while the U.S. has announced a hike in December, the interest rate gap between Korea and the U.S. will narrow, putting downward pressure on the exchange rate. Conversely, if it is frozen, the dollar will continue to strengthen.

What has not been confirmed are predictions such as ‘collapse of 1,300 won’ or ‘re-entry of 1,400 won.’ What is confirmed now is that 1,323.10 won (October 26th) is the lowest closing price in a year, and exporter negotiation volume and foreign selling are competing in the 1,330 won range. Saying that the exchange rate has stabilized and saying that prices have stabilized are two different sentences.

title: European Welfare Bill — Three Numbers from France
deck: Social protection spending 23%, France 31.9%, public spending 57.2%. We estimated the fiscal burden and growth stagnation of the welfare model using official figures from the OECD, EU, and IMF.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: OECD/EU average social protection spending is 23% of GDP in 2024. Social insurance benefits in the EU-27 are 27.3%, and in France at 31.9%, the second highest after Finland (32.5%). 77% of expenditures are focused on old age, survivors, and medical care.

French public spending is 57.2% of GDP in 2025, 7.7 percentage points higher than the EU average. The fiscal deficit is expected to expand again from 5.1% (2025) to 5.7% in 2027, and government debt will increase from 115.5% in 2025 to 120.9% in 2027.

The 2023 pension reform was postponed from December 2025 to January 2028. The IMF called for spending curbs and pension and unemployment benefit reforms in May 2026, and the Eurozone's growth rate is 1.1% in 2026, which is half that of the United States (2.3%).
body:
The problem with the European welfare model is not that there is a lot of welfare, but the structure of passing the bill to the future. Official figures from the OECD, EU and IMF for 2026 show how this structure works in one country: France.

## What percentage of GDP does Europe spend on welfare?

OECD and EU average social protection spending is 23% of GDP in 2024. Old-age benefits account for the majority at an average of 9.1% in the OECD and 9.8% in the EU, and medical/disability benefits account for the majority at 9.2% in the OECD and 8.5% in the EU (OECD, September 2026).

According to data comparing 27 European countries by DREES, a research institute under the French National Statistical Office, social insurance benefit spending in 2024 is 27.3% of the EU-27 average GDP, or 12,190 euros per person (purchasing power parity). France is second at 31.9%, following Finland (32.5%). It is followed by Italy at 28.3% and Spain at 25.1%. 77% of all EU spending is focused on the elderly, survivors, and medical care, and 89% is paid without an income test. The structure is such that most of the welfare goes to ‘those who have reached the appropriate age’ rather than ‘those who need it’.

## France's bill is summarized in three lines:

The first line is the amount of expenditure. French public spending is 57.2% of GDP in 2025, 7.7 percentage points higher than the EU average. It is the second highest spending country in the EU. Pension spending alone is 14.6% of GDP in 2023. The actual retirement age in 2022 is 62.2 years, which is significantly lower than Germany (66 years and 2 months) and the Netherlands (67 years).

The second line is deficit and debt. France's fiscal deficit was 5.8% in 2024 and 5.1% in 2025. The European Commission expects it to worsen again to 5.1% in 2026 and 5.7% in 2027. OECD predicts that government debt will increase from 115.5% in 2025 to 118.8% in 2026 and 120.9% in 2027. The EU launched the transitional deficit procedure (EDP) in France in July 2024. In June 2026, the Commission suspended the process to evaluate the implementation of the reform, but the debt did not decrease.

The third line is growth. In the IMF's October 2026 forecast, the Eurozone's growth rate is 1.1% and the United States' growth rate is 2.3%. France 0.4%, Italy 0.8%, Germany 1.3%. The OECD announced that in the second quarter of 2026, real household income per capita in France decreased by 0.6% and in Italy by 1.0% compared to the previous quarter. When growth stops, it is difficult to maintain the same welfare with the same taxes.

![Image depicting a European budget chart with welfare spending and fiscal deficit overlapping — Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/europe-welfare-fiscal-burden.jpg)

## Why did pension reform stop?

In December 2025, the French government postponed key measures of the 2023 pension reform in the 2026 Social Security Finance Act from September 2026 to January 2028. The reform was to raise the retirement age to 64 by 2030 and increase the contribution period required to receive a full pension to 43 years. This is the result of the cabinet, which did not secure a majority of seats, accept the opposition party's demands to avoid a rejection of the budget bill and a vote of no confidence.

Costs emerged in several places. International credit rating agency S&P downgraded France's credit rating from AA- to A+. According to data from the Korea Institute for Health and Social Affairs cited by the National Assembly Research Service, the additional interest costs that French citizens will bear due to the rise in government bond interest rates due to a decline in credit rating is estimated at 6 to 7.5 billion euros. In May 2026, the IMF called for "a multi-year plan that combines spending restraint, pension system reform, reduction of unemployment benefits, and efficiency in health and education spending."

## Welfare is not bad, financial resources are the problem

Balance is also needed. The OECD estimates that France's taxes and transfer spending lower the Gini coefficient by about 43% and the poverty rate based on 60% of median income by nearly 30 percentage points. The achievements of European welfare in reducing the income gap between classes are real. The problem is who will pay the costs of maintaining that performance and when.

The method Europe has chosen now is to postpone taxes and interest. In the 2026 budget, France raised tax revenues of 0.5% of GDP through special contributions for large corporations, increased taxes on high incomes, and increases in social security contributions for financial income. Of these, 0.3% are temporary. In 2027, this temporary measure will disappear and the deficit will increase again.

The implications for Korea are not ‘reduce welfare.’ This means that the speed of aging, financial capacity, and distribution of burden between generations must first be determined and the system designed. France is paying the price for delaying the order in terms of interest rates and growth rates. However, the figures after 2027 are projections and may vary depending on world oil prices and interest rates.
