title: ‘4 criminal records’ was in the judgment, and AI cheating was not confirmed — three questions left by the Lit perfect scorer case
deck: The history of criminal punishment confirmed in the ruling and the suspicion of AI cheating, with only traces of test papers remaining, are not the same incident. What remains after a person dies is not a question of individual morality, but a question of which door and what books, entrance exams, and qualifications check.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: What is confirmed by the judgment is the history of criminal punishment. It was reported that he was sentenced to 8 months in prison with 2 years of probation and 6 months in prison for intentional traffic accident blackmail in 2021-2022, a fine of 7 million won for assaulting a police officer in 2024, and a fine of 300,000 won for a summary order for intimidation. However, this is not official confirmation from the police that the person in the ruling is himself.

What has not been confirmed is AI fraud. There were traces of modifications to the test answers and name modifications on the report card (acknowledged by the applicant), but there was no direct evidence of cheating. When the person involved died on November 19, the investigation, cancellation of admission, and compensation for damages virtually stopped, and the suspicions remained without a conclusion.

What remains is the institutional question. The sanctions for cheating on the College Scholastic Ability Test are 1 year, up to 4 years for LIT, and 3 times for national qualifications, and there is no criminal background screening for law school admission, and there is no entity that verifies the author's history of self-published bestsellers.
body:
Write the conclusion first. Among the content that YouTube channel Ttang TV concluded in “The person with perfect Lit score, turns out to have 4 criminal records” **What is confirmed by the verdict is his past criminal punishment history, and what is not confirmed is the core suspicion that he cheated on the test.** These are not the same case. One is a final decision made by the court, and the other is a suspicion that no agency has yet reached a conclusion on.

And on November 19, Mr. Lee, the person involved in the suspicion, was found dead at a lodging establishment in Gangdong-gu, Seoul. An autopsy conducted by the National Institute of Forensic Science the next day did not reveal any evidence of homicide, and the death was pronounced on the 21st. The bereaved family declined to be interviewed at the funeral. This article does not include real names, faces, or personal details in consideration of the deceased and the bereaved family. Instead, we compare the claims made in the video one by one, and see what each of the remaining **three doors** — book, entrance exam, and qualification — confirms and does not confirm.

## What was confirmed and what was not confirmed?

**Criminal punishment history is cross-checked with judgments and summary orders obtained by various media outlets. On the other hand, none of the AI misconduct, detention center motive testimony, or medical student stalking revelations have been officially confirmed.**

What is confirmed by the ruling is as follows.

- Road in front of Arts Center Station in Namdong-gu, Incheon, November 9, 2021. After intentionally hitting the front bumper of a taxi that was turning right while riding a bicycle, he received 1 million won in cash by saying, "As you know well, the driver is at a disadvantage if you turn right when the crosswalk signal is blue. I won't have a problem if you reimburse me for the damage." About 30 minutes later, the same method was used against another taxi at the same location, but the police arrived and it ended in an attempt. The Incheon District Court sentenced him to eight months in prison and two years of probation for extortion and attempted extortion in January 2022, and it was confirmed without appeal.
- Post office intersection in Manan-gu, Anyang-si, Gyeonggi-do from March 19 to 21, 2022. He drove his bicycle toward a car that was turning right and demanded compensation, saying, "It's against you because the accident occurred at a crosswalk." He received a total of 2.42 million won from five drivers over the course of three days. There was also one attempt. Anyang Branch of the Suwon District Court sentenced him to six months in prison in September 2022 and wrote, “He reoffended about two months after the suspended sentence,” and “The spirit of the war is weak.”
- Yongsan-gu, Seoul in the early morning of April 19, 2024. When the taxi driver asked him to get off due to battery issues, he cursed, kicked his side, and hit his face (the prosecution was dismissed for this part because the victim did not want to be punished). He hit the arm of a police officer who responded to the report several times and pushed his back with his body. The Seoul Western District Court sentenced him to a fine of 7 million won for assault and obstruction of official duties in December 2024.
- In May 2024, the prosecution requested a summary order of a fine of 300,000 won for threatening him by sending a KakaoTalk message in March 2024 over a refund of 60,000 won for a joint cheering ticket at Korea University.
- The ruling also mentions the previous history of fines for similar methods.

If you put it this way, “4 criminal records” is not a legal term, but a number counted by the media by comparing sentences. This is why, depending on the media, the notation is different as '3 criminal records of the same type' and '4 criminal records'. However, the police have not officially confirmed that the person written in the verdict is Lee himself. The basis for media verification is a match between name, date of birth, and name before change. The Korea Economic Daily wrote, “It has not been finally confirmed that the person listed in the judgment is Mr. Lee himself.” This article doesn't cross that line either.

There are many more that have not been confirmed.

**AI cheating** was never confirmed. There were traces of corrected answers in questions 25 to 29 of the released Lit test papers, and the erased answers matched the correct answers to the immediately preceding questions (numbers 24 to 28) several times. This is where the suspicion arose that the answers received from outside were written down one by one and then corrected. However, nothing was detected by the proctor at the time of the test, and no direct evidence that AI or communication devices were used was disclosed. He denied it until the end, explaining, “I lost concentration in the second half and made more mistakes.” Noh Hyeong-seok, an instructor at Mega Law School who received a perfect score in Lit language comprehension in 2016, also drew the line, saying, “This is a part that requires explanation in the flow of the solution,” but “That alone does not prove misconduct.”

**Revision of report card name** is a fact acknowledged by the person. They claim that they changed the name because they did not want their name revealed before the name change, and that they did not change the scores and elective subjects. The Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation stated that even if the name is changed, the name at the time of application will appear on the transcript.

**Testimony of the detention center** is an exclusive report from JTBC, which states that a person who was also imprisoned said, “He said he was attending the math department at Sungkyunkwan University,” and, “He said his goal was to raise money through fraud and create learning materials.” This is a one-person statement and no additional verification has been done.

**Medical Student Stalking and Threats Exposure** is a one-person revelation posted on an online community. The recording and message were made public, and the reporter said that after receiving police counseling, the investigation was closed due to the cost and mental burden. The person concerned denied it, saying, “Rather, I am the victim.” Neither side has been legally judged.

Some of the expressions in the video are different from the facts. The video said 'Seoul National University Dental Center', but the place he attended was **Seoul National University Department of Dentistry (undergraduate)**. The history revealed by the person is that he received the 1st grade in all subjects (1 question incorrectly answered in Life Science II) in the 2026 CSAT and entered the university. 'The first perfect score in Lit's history' is not a confirmed official record, but is at the level of "known." The video says it has been "confirmed" by combining the confirmation of the verdict, testimony, and speculation in one flow, but the boundary confirmed by the coverage is narrower than that.

![Gavel, answer sheet, book. It symbolically contains the three doors through which this incident passed. AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/leet-top-scorer-criminal-record-gap.jpg)

## Where do the remaining procedures stop after death?

**Criminal procedures are halted due to the absence of the right to public prosecution, administrative procedures are halted due to the disappearance of the target, and civil procedures are halted due to inheritance issues.** There is a simultaneous risk that unconfirmed suspicions will become solidified as if they were confirmed, and there is a risk that what should have been confirmed will never be confirmed.

The police announced that they would continue the investigation despite the death. The Financial Crimes Investigation Unit of the Metropolitan Investigation Division of the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency is looking into complaints filed on charges of obstruction of business, obstruction of official duties, fraud, etc., and has requested the Seoul Metropolitan Office of Education to preserve evidence of last year's college entrance exam questions and answers to be stored at the relevant schools. However, if the suspect is dead, it is difficult to obtain a search and seizure warrant. Cell phones and laptops can only be secured with the cooperation of the bereaved family. Attorney Jung Joon-young said, “Because the suspect is dead, there is no right to prosecute, so there is a high possibility that the court will not issue a search and seizure warrant.”

‘No right to prosecute’ means neither innocence nor guilt. It is only a formal judgment that the object of punishment has disappeared, and is not a conclusion as to whether misconduct occurred. The final variable is how far the police can confirm with the remaining data.

Universities and test-hosting organizations are also unable to move. It appears that Seoul National University will handle death expulsion according to school regulations. The position is that it is difficult to cancel admission. As college entrance exam scores are the core of the selection process in regular recruitment, the Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation must first invalidate grades before cancellation of admission can be considered. However, if a person becomes deceased, the process also stops. Korea University said it had no issues under review, saying, “We can discuss related measures only when actual misconduct is revealed through a police investigation.” The Law School Council, which organized the exam, said on the 17th, "There were no unusual issues during the exam and we have no plans to investigate separately," but changed its position two days later, saying, "We will actively cooperate with the investigation and prepare supplementary measures."

The book has already been taken off the market. Yes24 stopped selling “Brain Accel” on the 20th, and Kyobo Book Center and Aladdin are discussing whether to continue selling it. The lawsuit for damages that the buyers had anticipated was canceled immediately after the death was reported. The education company Sidae Talent terminated the contract on the 18th, eight days after signing the contract.

This case was overturned within three days. On the 17th, an online disclosure was made, the verdict was reported on the 18th, and the person involved died on the 19th. Meanwhile, reporters visited the home, and the bereaved family declined to cover the funeral. The speed at which unconfirmed suspicions can be handled is not the same as the speed at which one person can handle them.

## Why did the book become a bestseller without any resistance?

**This is because there was no subject anywhere to verify the narrative.** The book was published on September 2nd at the regular price of 22,000 won by 'Bright Brain Research Institute', a publishing company founded by the deceased. According to Yes24's tally for the fourth week of August, it ranked first in the self-development category and 18th overall, and 62.9% of buyers were in their 20s and 30s. The core product of the book was the story of going from a 7th grade on the CSAT to entering the Department of Dentistry at Seoul National University and earning a perfect score in LIT.

There is no place that has confirmed its history. The publisher was a company founded by the author himself, and the online bookstore does not review the content of the book or the author's academic background. The bestseller ranking is a tally that counts sales volume. The same goes for the entrance exam academy contract. Sida Talent signed a contract for learning content on November 10 and terminated it eight days later, saying, “Considering the seriousness of the issues related to test fairness, verification of the facts is necessary.”

If the suspicions are confirmed to be true, it is pointed out that this could be an advertisement that deceived consumers. However, it was not confirmed, and the person involved died. In principle, the liability for compensation is inherited, but inheritance waiver and limited approval are possible, and the plaintiff must directly prove the wrongdoing. This is why the legal community says, “The realistic threshold is high.”

There is a separate structural question. **Who checks the ‘grades’ of test books and self-help books?** There are no regulations to verify the author’s resume before selling. The point at which readers have grounds for suspicion is always after an incident occurs. In a market where popularity and trust are synonymous, validation arrives only after the fact.

## If the scores become invalid, will admission be cancelled?

**The principle is 'invalidation of grades → cancellation of admission', but the first step is death.** If cheating on the CSAT is confirmed, the test is invalidated in accordance with the Higher Education Act and the College Scholastic Ability Test Management Regulations, and application is restricted for one year following the year of enforcement. In the National Assembly, lawmakers from both the ruling and opposition parties have proposed amendments to the Higher Education Act that would extend this period to 5 years and require disciplinary action by notifying the affiliated university if the cheater is enrolled or on leave of absence from the university (November 17). Some reports also discussed extending the period to up to 10 years. Neither has yet been passed.

The weight of the sanctions is different for each test. In case of minor misconduct, the grade will be cancelled, if it is serious, the applicant will be restricted from taking the exam for 1 year from the next year. If it is serious, the applicant will be subject to civil and criminal action and will be restricted from taking the exam for 4 years from the next year. The national qualification test is limited to taking the exam three times, and the civil service appointment test lasts for five years. Even for the same 'cheating', the time lost can range from 1 to 5 years depending on which exam center you pass through.

This gap was revealed in numbers in this year’s CSAT. The Ministry of Education announced that it had detected 98 cheaters related to electronic devices in the 2027 CSAT. There were 49 people due to 3 emergency disaster text messages, 44 people due to signal detection and possession crackdown, and there were 5 cases of actually using smart devices during the test (1 smart glasses, 1 small camera/wireless earphone, 1 photo shoot for question paper, 2 bathroom smartphones). This is the result of increasing the number of supervisors and deploying Wi-Fi and Bluetooth detection.

The spark was the tax accountant exam. The person who passed the 63rd tax accountant exam surrendered to the police on November 15, confessing that he had taken pictures of questions with a tiny camera, sent them to generative AI, and checked the answers with his smartphone. There was even a statement that a camera was attached to correction tape and a calculator was converted into a transceiver. He said he used the same method in the first exam for certified public accountants. There were 5 cases of cheating using smart glasses in this year's national qualification exam, and 19 cases of AI cheating were confirmed in regular university exams from January 2020 to August of this year.

A gap in relief also remains. Even if the scores are invalidated, the rules for automatically passing the next applicant are different for each university, and there is little practical benefit in a lawsuit contesting the decision to fail the previous entrance exam. An applicant who was rejected as the first candidate in the 2024 class of Korea University's Department of Political Science and Diplomacy posted a post saying, "Ask me to pay the re-examination fee," but experts say, "A separate procedure from the school or the Ministry of Education is necessary."

## Through which door are criminal records filtered out?

**The only question of qualification is the sentence 'imprisonment or worse'. Therefore, fines cannot close any door, and repeated property crimes pass through the door.** Article 5 of the Attorney Act and Article 6 of the Attorney Examination Act disqualify those who were sentenced to imprisonment or heavier imprisonment and less than 5 years have passed since the end of the sentence, those less than 2 years since the probation period has passed, and those who are in the probation period of sentencing. Article 8 of the Medical Service Act will also be revised in 2023 to apply the same sentencing standards regardless of the crime. If the sentence is imprisonment or more, it will be 5 years. If the sentence is suspended, it will be 2 years after the probation period. If the sentence is suspended, you cannot become a medical professional or take the national exam during that period.

If calculated according to the legal provisions, a person sentenced to prison in 2022 will have to wait 5 years from the date of execution to become a lawyer or medical professional. Dentists are held to the same standard. But there is no door in the previous step. Article 22 of the Law School Act stipulates that admission qualifications are limited to those with a bachelor's degree. The National Human Rights Commission recommended that the criminal punishment section be deleted from the 2020 law school application, citing the fact that "even those who are disqualified are eligible for admission and may not be disqualified when they graduate."

To summarize, it is as follows. At the admission and registration stage, no one asks about criminal records, and the qualification gate only functions as a sentence at the national examination stage. A fine does not prevent a person from entering law school or obtaining a medical license. Conversely, trust as an 'exam star' is created independently of these questions. Books, lectures, and broadcasts are not subject to qualification verification.

## What oversees exams in the AI era?

**Currently, the director is focused on ‘what did he bring in with him?’, and there is no procedure to confirm ‘what he did with it’ after the fact.** The CSAT prohibits the bringing in of electronic devices in principle, and possession of them is determined through disaster text and signal detection. You cannot bring in mobile phones, smartwatches, wireless earphones, or memo pads; only analog watches are allowed.

However, it is difficult to prove cheating with just the test paper and answer sheet. Unusually high scores or traces of answer revisions may be clues, but they are not conclusive evidence. A lawyer said, “Not only must the circumstances of purchasing a camera or smart glasses be proven, but also the fact that they were used in an actual test.” Conversely, if the supervising agency says, “Nothing has been detected, so there is nothing to investigate,” the suspicion returns to the individual.

The suspicions that returned in this case took the form of public verification. About 400,000 viewers flocked to the plan to show off one's skills by solving the Korean language exam questions live, but the person involved never showed up. Since the system did not verify, individuals were put on the stage, and the stage became a place for spectacle rather than a place for verification.

## So what should you check?

**The remaining question is which door does not check what, not the individual's criminal record or death.** There are five things to check.

1. Does the test organization have procedures in place to move from ‘detection’-focused supervision to ‘post-verification of abnormal signs’? For both LITT and CSAT, if the proctor doesn't catch you, it's over.
2. How open is the window for test takers and universities to report and check forgery and falsification of transcripts and certificates? The problem this time was also the modification of the report card name.
3. How does the publishing and lecture market deal with the author’s academic background and grades? Is there at least a sign that it is an ‘unverified self-report’?
4. When the person involved dies, how long can investigation records and test data be preserved and what can be verified? This time it was blocked at the warrant stage.
5. How to provide relief to the next applicant when grades are confirmed invalid.

This incident cannot be viewed solely as a ‘witch hunt by an unjust genius.’ Traces of corrections to the answer sheet and name corrections to the report card were parts that actually required explanation, and there are clearly victims left in the ruling. Conversely, the story that ‘the cheater was discovered’ does not hold up. Nothing was discovered during the test, direct evidence was never disclosed, and the person involved died in denial.

Turning a person's life into a summary of a three-day verdict is not reporting. Writing confirmed things as confirmed and unconfirmed things as unconfirmed — nothing more, nothing less — is the minimum that reporting can do in this case. Judgment on the deceased, the bereaved family, and the victims whose names were left in the judgment is left to judicial procedures and time.

title: Receive subsidies and disappear leaving behind waste — records do not indicate nationality
deck: The practice of piling up waste and hiding in leased factories and the failure to recover subsidies has been confirmed in practice. However, the subjects of large-scale cases confirmed in reports, rulings, and administrative data from 2016 to 2026 were domestic organized crime gangs, waste brokers, and barge owners. Separately read what is confirmed and what is not confirmed.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: The method of piling up waste and hiding it in a rented factory has actually been confirmed. From August 2021 to August 2026, a national budget of 19.324 billion won was spent on processing 202,806 tons of abandoned waste, and the money recovered from the cause was 25 million won.

If the corporation that received the subsidy goes out of business, the recovery stops. Of the 33 non-payment of local government subsidies, 23 were closed corporations, and the unpaid amount of 4.5873 billion won (85.3%) was concentrated there.

However, the identity of the subject as a ‘Chinese factory’ was not confirmed. Official statistics do not distinguish between nationalities of actors, and the subjects of confirmed large-scale incidents were domestic gangsters and waste brokers. Rather, China is the ‘trigger’ that raised domestic treatment costs by suspending waste imports in 2018.
body:
Write the conclusion first. The story of "setting up a factory, receiving a subsidy, and disappearing without paying the waste disposal fee" **is true about the structure, but the subject has not been confirmed.** The method of piling up waste in a rented factory and then disappearing, the structure in which the cost is passed on to the building owner and local finances, and the problem of clawbacks stopping when the corporation that received the subsidy goes out of business are all recorded with dates and amounts attached. On the other hand, the part “the subject is Chinese” found no basis in any of the reports, rulings, or administrative data from 2016 to 2026 confirmed in this report. The statistics on abandoned waste do not distinguish between the nationalities of the actors, and the subjects of confirmed large-scale incidents were domestic gangsters, waste brokers, and the bosses they set up.

## How much is actually earned? 5 years, 19.3 billion won in taxes spent, 25 million won returned

The numbers are not small. According to data received from the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and released by Rep. Eogyu of the National Assembly's Climate, Energy, Environment and Labor Committee, 19.324 billion won in national funds was spent to process 202,806 tons of abandoned waste through administrative processing from 2021 to August 2026. The money recovered from the cause during this period is 20 million won in 2021 and 5 million won in 2022, for a total of 25 million won. It is 0.13% compared to input.

The burden on local governments is wider. According to the Kyunghyang Shinmun reported in September 2024 on data received by Rep. Lee Yong-woo from the Ministry of Environment, the cost of executing abandoned waste by local governments from 2020 to the first half of 2024 was 37.415 billion won. Iksan-si, Jeollabuk-do, spent 30 billion won to clean up the mountain of waste left behind by waste companies, Eumseong-gun, North Chungcheong Province spent 3 billion won, and Uiseong-gun, Gyeongbuk spent 28.2 billion won, a combination of national and provincial funds. During the same period, the amount paid directly by the landowner was 1.776 billion won, and the cost paid by LH, which expropriated the land where the waste was left, was 60 billion won.

The scale did not decrease. Since the Uiseong Garbage Mountain in 2019, there have been 493 garbage mountains confirmed nationwide by July 2024, which is more than double the tally from five years ago (235). Although 400 sites have been processed, 93 sites still remain, and 38 of them are in an unprocessed state. According to data compiled by the National Assembly Budget Office in July 2025, the cumulative illegal waste amounted to 1,911,000 tons by 2024, of which 83.6% has been disposed of. This means that the remaining 300,000 tons remain somewhere.

## Why is the building owner in trouble? The law looks at the ‘land owner’ first

Article 48 of the Waste Management Act determines the subjects to whom action orders can be issued for improperly disposed waste. Item 1 is the person who disposed of the waste, and Item 3 is “the owner of the land where the waste was dumped or reclaimed if he directly disposed of the waste or allowed others to use his own land.” A landlord is subject to an action order simply because he or she has lent the building. No intent or negligence is required. Suwon High Court's ruling 2022nu10265 wrote, "Since the landowner is not required to be intentional or negligent in disposing or bringing in waste, he or she is subject to an action order simply because he or she is the landowner." The Constitutional Court also did not consider this structure unconstitutional in its 2007Hunba53 decision in 2010.

The results are concrete. The owner of an 8,346㎡ factory site in Yeongcheon-si, Gyeongsangbuk-do lent the land to a tenant in 2017, but ended up taking on 16,939 tons of waste in 2019. After Yeongcheon City spent 3.69284 billion won and processed it through administrative proxy execution, the amount charged to the owner was 3.33251 billion won. The owner filed a lawsuit, saying, “The burden is greater than the rental income,” but the Daegu High Court, the appellate court, deemed the imposition legal in December 2022.

The numbers on the ground are better. In the case of Gimhae, Gyeongnam, reported by Yonhap News in March 2024, the waste accumulated in a 620 pyeong factory was 2,900 tons, and the disposal cost was 900 million won. The tenant started piling up waste two months after signing the contract and stopped contacting us. In 2017, in Yeoncheon, Gyeonggi Province, a landowner who was supposed to receive a rent of 3 million won per month was asked to pay 300 million won in disposal fees, and in Pohang, North Gyeongsang Province, a factory owner who rented for 10 million won per month had to pay 15,000 tons of waste and 3 billion won.

The system has changed little by little from 2024. In June 2024, the 'Land Owner Notification System' will be implemented, and local governments will notify land owners when they identify illegal waste. From March 26, 2026, the revised Waste Management Act (Law No. 20859) came into effect, creating a ranking of action orders, and landowners who made efforts to prevent waste management can receive up to 50% reduction in execution costs. The requirements for reduction are specific. Did they regularly visually inspect the land use status, or did they request cessation of use and disposal without delay after recognizing the waste? This means that the only means of defense left to the person renting the building are the contract and photos.

## Faces left on record — gangsters and barge bosses

The protagonists of these incidents were not Chinese. In May 2018, the Gyeonggi Southern Provincial Police Agency arrested 40 people who rented 18 mixed land and factory lands (105,600 m2) in the Gyeonggi area in the name of CEO Baji, dumped 45,000 tons of industrial waste, and pocketed 6.6 billion won. In November 2021, a group caught by the same Blue House Violent Crime Investigation Unit accumulated 46,000 tons in 11 empty factories across the country and pocketed 9.2 billion won. The police summarized their roles as "dump site operator, broker, bar manager, and gatekeeper."

The method was close to the manual. After signing a short-term contract by paying only a portion of the deposit and promising a high monthly rent, they put up a 4-6m high screen and pour water heavily at night, disappearing before the balance is due. They took over a licensed waste disposal company and registered only part of the waste in an electronic information processing program (Allbaro System) to pretend it was legal, and sent the rest to an illegal dump. The structure was to receive a processing contract for 2.25 to 2.45 million won per 25-ton vehicle, hand it over for 1.8 to 2 million won, and give 1 to 1.2 million won to the dump.

Local governments say the same thing. Asan City, South Chungcheong Province, determined that 18,000 tons of illegal waste was accumulated in 7 locations as of February 2023. At the time, an Asan city official said, "Waste companies rent factories or land and dump illegal waste for which they only paid a 10% down payment." The 'garbage mountain' in Uiseong, Gyeongsangbuk-do was 159,000 tons, more than 150 times the permitted storage amount of 1,020 tons. The company's former CEO and his wife were sentenced to five and three years in prison and a fine of 1.38 billion won. 30 billion won in Iksan and 3 billion won in Eumseong were also invoices left by domestic companies.

![Waste gunny bags and drums piled up in an empty rental factory, and a tightly locked iron door. This is usually the scene left behind by tenants who leave without paying the processing fee. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/factory-subsidy-waste-abandonment.jpg)

## How much is confirmed about the ‘Chinese factory’?

In this report, we checked reports, rulings, and local government data on about 20 cases of waste abandonment at rental factories reported since 2016, but did not find any cases that explicitly stated that the nationality of the perpetrator was Chinese. Official statistics don't answer that question either. The Ministry of Environment's illegal waste and abandoned waste data and local government execution settlements are announced by region, volume, and cost. The National Police Agency counts foreign suspects by nationality, but we have not been able to confirm public data that divides nationality separately for violations of the Waste Management Act.

There are separate points where foreigners appear in the records. Ulsan Dong-gu announced that of the 461 cases of illegal garbage dumping detected in 2024, 137 (29.7%) were foreigners. In 2020, it was 14 out of 180 (7.8%). However, this is the dumping of household waste in residential areas crowded with foreign workers at shipyards, and the reasons for Dong-gu's involvement are differences in separate disposal methods and language barriers. This is a different story from the case of renting and storing industrial waste from a factory.

Generalizing one case to a group is not a basis. In July 2025, there was a case in Gyeongju where a Chinese business owner was arrested on charges of non-payment of 13 million won in wages, but that was a violation of the labor law of a foreign-employed business and was not a waste or subsidy case. On the contrary, there are countless incidents of the same type committed by domestic companies.

So this article does not use the claim that “the Chinese factory is the culprit” as fact. Instead, write down where there are loopholes that could make that claim. The moment you place nationality as the cause, the prescription becomes wrong. Domestic companies and foreign investment companies use the same laws, same guarantee limits, and the same rental market.

## Who Really Receives the Subsidies — What Kind of Money Flows to Foreign Factories?

The situation is different on the subsidy side. This is where Chinese capital actually appears.

According to what Maeil Business Newspaper reported in March 2025 based on data submitted to the National Assembly by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, the cash subsidies paid by the government and local governments to foreign companies from 2020 to 2024 amounted to 495.2 billion won. American companies accounted for the largest proportion with 22 cases, and cases of Chinese companies began to appear from 2022. Chinese company A, which invested $37 million (approximately 53 billion won) in Jeonnam in 2021, received 5.88 billion won in national funding in the same year and 2.52 billion won in local government funding the following year. The government temporarily raised the cash subsidy limit to up to 75% in 2025.

The scale of investment was also large. In 2024, China's direct investment in Korea amounted to USD 5.79 billion, accounting for 19.7% of the total, and in 2025, it decreased by 38.0% to USD 3.59 billion. Total foreign direct investment was the highest ever at $36.05 billion in 2025, and the first place was the United States ($9.77 billion, 27.1%).

The outcome of the system is two-pronged. Mergers and acquisitions (M&A)-type investments screen six items, including defense industry, strategic materials, and national core technologies, but there is no same screening standard for new/expanded factories (greenfield)-type investments. An official from the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy told Maeil Business Newspaper, “It is difficult to come up with a plan to improve the system to control bypass exports from specific countries.” Instead, there is a local investment promotion subsidy to attract domestic investment. From 2004 to the first half of 2019, 1.328 trillion won in government funds went into 1,198 companies.

Here we need to clear up a common misunderstanding. The statement that “foreign factories take advantage of Korea’s employment subsidies” is difficult to establish in terms of the system. In principle, workers without Korean nationality are excluded from employment promotion incentives. The only exceptions are residence (F-2), permanent residence (F-5), and marriage immigration (F-6) visa holders. There is no structure in which employers receive subsidies just because they hire a lot of foreign workers.

## Why does the recovery stop? There is a law, but there is no collateral.

The law is rather strict. Article 20-4 of the Enforcement Decree of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act stipulates false or unfair applications, failure to fulfill obligations under the cash grant contract, and “cases where the business can no longer be carried out due to the bankruptcy or closure of the investment corporation or business during the contract period” as reasons for cancellation, withdrawal, reduction, or recovery. The 「Cash Support System Operation Guidelines」 provides for a business operation period of 5 years after the investment period ends, and requires investment and employment performance to be maintained during that period. It is specified that collateral such as mortgage, provisional registration, and guarantee must be secured before payment. With the revision on October 20, 2026, the national and local governments' refund payment deadline was unified to 30 days.

The problem is enforcement. If the corporation has no assets, the recovery stops. According to data received from 17 cities and provinces by Rep. Kim Sang-hoon of the National Assembly Planning and Finance Committee, there were 33 corporations that did not comply with the subsidy return order as of November 2023, and the unpaid amount was 5.37522 billion won. Of these, 23 were closed corporations, and the unpaid amount was 4,587.3 million won, accounting for 85.3% of the total. The average elapsed time for corporations that exceeded the return deadline was 1,087 days. A corporation in Incheon went out of business 5 days after receiving the last subsidy, and a corporation in Seoul was ordered to return 2,039.86 billion won and did not pay a penny for 1,983 days.

In some cases, water can be returned. Daejeon City received 1 billion won in local investment promotion subsidies and disposed of the real estate of corporations that closed down without meeting employment obligations through voluntary auction, collecting the entire principal and interest in November 2022. Ulsan City confirmed that 6 out of 12 companies that received local investment promotion subsidies did not fulfill the investment and employment requirements in a comprehensive survey in 2020, and recovered the entire amount. Sacheon City, South Gyeongsang Province, recovered 2.02 billion won from companies that fell short of their employment plan (50 people), and the court supported this. Conversely, Gyeongsangbuk-do announced in 2019 that it had not been able to recover 4.622 billion won in subsidies it was supposed to receive from bankrupt companies. The loss rate was 23%.

There are also large differences between systems. From 2022 to August 2026, 5,240 cases of illegal receipt of employment incentives worth 15.64 billion won were detected, but the actual recovery rate was 58.0% on average and 49.2% in 2025. During the same period, the number of illegal unemployment benefits received by foreign workers was 285 cases worth 240 million won in 2025, and the recovery rate was 85.9%. Even within the same employment insurance system, recovery results vary from system to system. The abandoned waste side is below that. I spent 19.3 billion won over 5 years and received 25 million won back.

## China was the trigger, not the culprit

There is one fact that changes the direction of the story. China's role in Korea's waste crisis was not that of 'throwaway' but 'non-receipt'.

China notified the World Trade Organization in July 2017 and suspended the import of 24 types of solid waste, including waste plastic, waste paper, and waste metal, from January 2018. By then, much of Korea's recyclables had gone to China. Of the 196,279 tons of recycled waste sold domestically and overseas in 2017, 127,917 tons (65.2%) were destined for China. After the ban, exports of waste plastic to China from January to February 2018 decreased by 92.0% from 22,097 tons to 1,774 tons, and waste paper decreased by 40.6%. The price of corrugated cardboard fell from 130 won to 90 won per kg, and in April 2018, recycling companies in the metropolitan area refused to collect waste vinyl, causing a 'garbage crisis'.

Processing costs moved in the opposite direction. In November 2017, an official from Yangju City told Yonhap News, "Due to the deterioration of relations with China, waste recycling has decreased, so the processing cost has risen from 100,000 won to 200,000 won per ton when incinerated, and from tens of thousands of won to 100,000 won when shredding." The number of places to dispose of it has decreased and the price has doubled. Local governments believe that the profits became an incentive for illegal speculation.

The story of the factory where waste remains is also consistent with this structure. As reported by the Jeonbuk Geumgang Ilbo in April 2026, about 8,000 tons were piled 7 to 8 meters high at the waste synthetic resin recycling plant in Seongdang-myeon, Iksan. In 2016, the license was revoked after being caught violating storage standards, and the subsequent business that inherited the rights through an auction also went bankrupt. Iksan City explained that this factory had been exporting waste to Hong Kong, Malaysia, Vietnam, and China, but its management collapsed as the export route was blocked. The city said, “We considered administrative execution, but the processing cost is over 1 billion won, so we are worried about recovery issues.”

In other words, China is the trigger, not the perpetrator, in this story. The decision to close the cheap processing route raised domestic processing costs, and it was domestic organizations and licensed companies that took advantage.

## So what should you check?

The question that remains is not nationality but design.

First, the guarantee limit. Waste disposal companies must guarantee twice the permitted storage amount (5 times the excess storage amount). However, the amount of neglect in Uiseong was 150 times the permitted amount. There is a double-digit multiplier gap between what a warranty can cover and how much is actually accumulated. The gap is left to the local government budget and the landowner.

Second, it is a lease. Damage was usually determined by how closely the contract stipulated the purpose, prohibition on bringing in waste, restoration obligations, and security deposits. In order to receive a reduction in execution costs through the 2026 revision, “periodic visual inspection” and “request for cessation of use without delay after recognition” must be made. Photos and proof of content once a month have become a profitable structure.

Third, there is collateral and follow-up management of subsidies. Cash support for foreign investors stipulates securing collateral, but if the collateral is real estate, it is pushed down in the auction rankings. The 2026 revision to unify the payment deadline to 30 days is a change that narrows the process. However, there is still no answer when a closed corporation has no assets.

There are also things readers can check for themselves. You can view the treatment history and reporting procedures at the Korea Environment Corporation's Allbaro System (allbaro.or.kr) and the Illegal Waste Dumping Reporting and Counseling Center, and you can check the traces of accumulation at a specific site in time series using aerial photos of the national land information map. Before renting a building, the minimum defense is to check whether the contracting company has a license and an abandoned waste disposal performance guarantee, and to include provisions prohibiting the introduction of waste and restoration to its original state in the contract.

Finally, we note the limitations of this article. The fact that we were unable to find a ruling or investigation record specifying nationality does not mean that there were none. Unless the local government announces nationality, answering this question requires coverage that follows the business registration, corporate registration, and immigration records of individual cases. If there is a report, we will check it through that channel.

title: Where regulation has won, what's left? — Claims from three cases of 'regulatory isolation'
deck: Basic laws on autonomous driving, non-face-to-face medical treatment, and AI. According to the published numbers, the cost of national isolation was not caused by the ‘ban’ but by the ‘amount of verification’ and ‘time of release’.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: The cumulative mileage of domestic self-driving cars is about 13 million km, which is less than 10% of the leading companies in the United States and China, which exceeded 160 million km for a single company. The technology gap in 2025 will be 13.6 months compared to the United States, narrowing it by only 1.1 months over two years.

Non-face-to-face medical treatment was institutionalized on December 2, 2025, 15 years after the first bill was submitted in 2010, and will be implemented on December 24, 2026. Although the industry's petition for restrictions on prescription and address city/province within 7 days of the first visit exceeded 50,000, the formula for the industry's estimate of '2 out of 3' was not made public.

The AI ​​Framework Act came into effect on January 22, 2026, but it was pointed out that the criteria for determining ‘provision’ and ‘high impact’ were unclear. The cumulative number of regulatory sandbox approvals is 2,787 (as of November 2026), but it is assessed that the responsible party for institutionalization after verification is unclear.
body:
What Korea lost due to regulation was not innovation itself, but the opportunity to verify innovation. The disclosed numbers in the three fields of autonomous driving, non-face-to-face medical treatment, and artificial intelligence (AI) refer to the same place. The technology is available domestically, but the equipment to roll it out on the roads and in the market was opened late.

## Are you unable to run because you do not have the skills, or are you unable to learn because there is no place to run?

Autonomous driving is the clearest. According to the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, as of July 2026, there are 72 organizations and 584 vehicles that have received temporary operation permits. Autonomous A2Z (A2Z), which has revealed the actual vehicles permitted to operate, has 91 vehicles as of the end of 2025. At the same time, there were about 3,000 Waymo units, 1,975 Pony AI units, and 1,800 WeRide units.

The driving data gap is even larger. The cumulative mileage of domestic self-driving cars is about 13 million km, which is less than 10% of the leading companies in the United States and China, which exceeded 160 million km for a single company. As of 2025, Korea's technological level was 13.6 months behind the United States. The gap narrowed over the two years since 2023 is 1.1 months.

The law has been substantially revised in 2025. However, completely unmanned operations are impossible due to the Road Traffic Act and the Passenger Transport Service Act, which require a person to sit in the driver's seat. On October 23, the government established a new 'autonomous driving service business operator' system and announced the launch of paid robotaxi in Gwangju by 2028.

Investment decreased. The autonomous driving research and development (R&D) budget decreased by 43% from KRW 156.8 billion in 2023 to KRW 89.5 billion in 2026. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport's budget for autonomous vehicle commercialization decreased by 78% from 42.9 billion won in 2024 to 9.4 billion won in 2025. Plans and budgets moved in opposite directions.

![Self-driving car and control screen accumulating empirical data on the road — Image · AI Illustration](/assets/img/articles/korea-regulatory-isolation-cost.jpg)

## A law that took 15 years, what remains before implementation

Non-face-to-face medical treatment is a case where regulations remain even after regulations are lifted. The institutionalization bill was first submitted to the 18th National Assembly in 2010, and passed the plenary session of the National Assembly on December 2, 2025. It’s been 15 years. The effective date is December 24, 2026.

The amendment to the enforcement rules announced by the Ministry of Health and Welfare limits prescriptions for first-time patients to within 7 days in principle, and allows up to 30 days as an exception only once. Medical institutions that can provide treatment were limited to clinics located in the same city/province as the patient's address. There was also a ban on dedicated institutions, a 30% treatment ratio, and a cap of 500 cases per month per doctor.

The numbers on the ground are different. Of the approximately 2.815 million non-face-to-face medical treatment claims in 2025, 98.6% and 6,891 of the 6,990 participating medical institutions were at the clinic level. In a survey commissioned by Korea Research by the Telemedicine Industry Council, the average number of prescription days for 2,066 experienced patients was 33.7 days, and 46.3% were more than 30 days. However, as the survey was commissioned by an industry group, the population and sample design were not disclosed.

The backlash led to a petition. On November 4, the number of signatures on the petition to guarantee the use of non-face-to-face medical treatment exceeded 50,000, and it entered the National Assembly review process. The industry claims, “It will become difficult for two out of three existing users to receive treatment as they are now,” but the formula for this estimate has not been made public. The medical community counters that safety measures are lacking.

## AI basic laws, if there are no standards, it is not regulation but homework

The AI Framework Act came into effect on January 22, 2026. If classified as high-impact AI, there is an obligation to explain risk management measures and judgment criteria, a human supervision system, and keep implementation documents for 5 years. The fine is less than 30 million won, and the government announced that there will be a guidance period of at least one year.

The problem is the judgment of applicability. The law defines the scope of business with the expression ‘provision’. Even if a financial company screens a loan using its own AI, it can be interpreted that it is not a business that provided AI because what it provides to customers is a loan. At the AI ​​Legal Policy Forum on November 16, attorney Jiwon Kang of the Pacific Law Firm pointed out that the scope and obligations of business operators should be clarified to prevent such interpretations.

Regulatory sandboxes present a different picture. According to the Science and Technology Policy Institute (STEPI), the cumulative number of approvals as of November 2026 is 2,787. However, it is unclear who will be responsible for changing the system after the verification is completed. There is a lot of approval, but the road to institutionalization is narrow.

## The bill for national isolation is not ‘prohibition’ but ‘time’

In Germany, Momenta and Uber began a supervised robotaxi pilot service in Munich on November 19, 2026. Momenta received national level 4 test approval from the German Federal Automobile Agency in July. In the same month, 19 level 3 taxis and 1 unmanned demonstration vehicle were in operation in Korea.

Of course, the cost of safety is real. Accidents in domestic pilot areas increased from 2 in 2022 to 37 in 2025, and 8 of the 66 cumulative accidents were caused by system errors. Therefore, experts call for an order to increase the scale of verification and feed accident records back into the system.

What has not been confirmed is the total cost of national isolation. I could not find any official figures from the government or research institutes that tally the costs of regulatory delays by industry. However, the number of demonstration units, mileage, budget, and release date have been confirmed. As those four things increase, so do your bills.

title: From $55,130 to $60,000 — What Happened in Bitcoin in Two Days
deck: After being pushed to the lowest price in two years, it rebounded by 9%. The size of forced liquidation, ETF fund flow, and conditions remaining in the US market on the 23rd were compared in the first report.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: Bitcoin was pushed from $55,130 (CoinDesk) to $55,251.60 (Reuters) during the intraday session on November 21, recording the lowest since September 2024, and then rebounded by more than 9% on the same day to recover to the $60,000 range. It is about 56% lower than the all-time high of $126,200 in October 2025.

The size of the 24-hour forced liquidation ranged from $1.8 billion (CoinDesk, Coinglass) to $2.67 billion (Bitcoin.com) depending on media statistics, and most of them were long positions. Glassnode analyzed that the long cluster in the $59,000 to $62,000 range was eliminated and the 'source of forced selling at the bottom of the market' was reduced.

It has not yet been confirmed whether a rebound is a trend. Blackrock IBIT's figures as of November 20 and the reaction to the opening of the US market on Monday the 23rd remain, and the FOMC's interest rate decision on December 8-9 is the next turning point.
body:
At 8:32 am on November 22, 2026, Bitcoin was 82,691,000 won in Upbit won. This is 1.92% higher than the previous day’s closing price. Twelve hours ago, this price had fallen to 76 million won. At the same time, the global average was $60,153 (24 hours +2.1%), which was about 2% higher than the domestic price converted to Korean won, which was 80.96 million won. The price is what I checked directly at the time of writing this article.

The sequence of what happened to this asset over the course of two days is clear. On November 20 (local time), $60,000 collapsed in the US market for the first time since July, and was pushed to the $55,000 range on Saturday Asian time. Reuters set the intraday low at $55,251.60, and CoinDesk set it at $55,130. Both media outlets wrote that it was the lowest since September 2024. On the afternoon of the same day, the price rebounded more than 9% from the low and regained $60,000.

## The starting point of the decline was not the coin

Reuters cited questions about the profitability of investments in artificial intelligence infrastructure, rising borrowing costs, increased regulatory uncertainty after the U.S. midterm elections, and the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang as the reasons behind this sale. On the 20th, Nasdaq fell by more than 4%, falling to its lowest level since April, and S&P 500 and Dow entered a correction phase. That same week, major U.S. indexes were on course to record their biggest weekly decline since the announcement of the 'Liberation Day' tariffs in April 2025.

CoinDesk pointed out the rise in inflation-linked government bond interest rates (real interest rates) as a key variable. As the real yield of government bonds, which are classified as safe assets, rises, the relative attractiveness of Bitcoin and gold, which do not bear interest, decreases. In fact, gold, copper, and Asian stocks were pushed along with technology stocks this week. The nature of Bitcoin moving in the same direction as stocks has been repeated this time.

Antropic's listing was recorded as an event that fostered this trend. The company was listed on Nasdaq at a public offering price of $83, and Reuters reported that the stock price's failure immediately after listing stimulated concerns about AI valuation. Investing.com wrote that on the first day, the stock price fell by more than 14%, below the public offering price. On the other hand, some trading platform announcements also record that the opening price was $111.50 (+34% compared to the public offering price). This appears to be due to large intraday fluctuations, but the closing price figures require further confirmation.

## Size of liquidation: 1.8 billion or 2.7 billion

The fuel for the rebound was not a new buying trend but forced liquidation. When the price was pushed down, the position with insufficient collateral was automatically closed, and the sale pushed the price again, creating a chain of closing the next position.

The problem is that the scale varies from medium to medium. The Coinglass tally cited by CoinDesk was $1.8 billion in 24 hours, of which $1.3 billion was long. An earlier article from the same outlet put it at $2.4 billion (more than $1 billion in Bitcoin futures and $545 million in Ethereum futures), while Bitcoin.com reported $2.67 billion. The difference arises due to differences in the timing of counting and the scope of exchanges included. EconomyBloc's calculation by HTX senior analyst Cloud was $1.893 billion, of which 91% were long.

The directions of the numbers are the same. Most of those who suffered losses in this decline were longs who had bet on a rise. CoinDesk reported that the single largest liquidation was a $51.71 million Bitcoin long position. This means that most market participants did not expect the price to fall below $60,000.

Glassnode analyzed that the cluster of leveraged longs that had been piled up in the $59,000 to $62,000 range for several months was eliminated through this sale, eliminating a 'large source of forced selling' at the bottom of the market. CryptoQuant's dark post, an on-chain analysis company, described this phase as 'extreme surrender', saying that the realized loss on the 7th was $11.3 billion, which is about 8 times the realized profit over the same period.

## On the other side are institutional funds

If liquidation has lifted the selling pressure, the ingredients that will continue the rebound have not yet been confirmed. Rather, institutional funds moved in the opposite direction.

IBIT, BlackRock's spot Bitcoin ETF, saw a net outflow of $541 million per day on November 19th. It is the highest ever on a single day. The entire U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF lost about $1.1 billion last week, and the cumulative net outflow in November was about $2.9 billion. CoinDesk reported that the daily outflow on November 19 exceeded $300 million, and that there was an outflow on 12 of the last 14 days. On November 17, Citigroup lowered its Bitcoin target price from $113,000 to $99,532 and Ethereum's target price from $3,028 to $2,838. The departure from the 200-day moving average and slowdown in ETF demand were presented as evidence.

The direction of the Federal Reserve is also a burden. In the October FOMC minutes, almost all attendees said that 'an additional interest rate increase is appropriate in the coming months.' There were two committee members who mentioned a 0.5% point increase (big step) in December. Director Christopher Waller left open the possibility of more aggressive measures, saying in a CNBC interview on November 17 that he was "very, very concerned" about inflation. The Fed's next meeting is December 8-9.

## Conditions for rebound

Singapore-based trading firm QCP Capital believes that Bitcoin's next meaningful rebound will require stabilizing technology stocks, reduced interest rate volatility, and evidence of institutional capital inflows. The explanation is that until the condition is met, it is difficult for the rebound due to short covering to lead to a sustained rise. Market maker Wintermute took the position that recovery can be convincingly said only when Bitcoin recovers to $68,000 and funds come back into spot ETFs, and pointed out that the recent rebound is not due to new buying demand but is in the nature of short covering.

Domestic market numbers also point in the same direction. Based on Upbit, the 52-week highest price was 143.05 million won on January 14, and the lowest price was 76.433 million won on November 21. The current price is 42% lower than the peak. At the same time, the top assets in market capitalization also rebounded, with Ethereum at 2.31 million won (+3.26%) and Solana at 96,450 won (+1.69%).

## Confirmed and unconfirmed

Confirmed facts include price, liquidation size, ETF outflow, Nasdaq plunge, and even Federal Reserve personnel remarks. Conversely, Daum has not been confirmed at the time of writing.

- Blackrock IBIT’s net outflow figures as of Friday, November 20th. It was not released over the weekend.
- Reaction to the opening of the US market on Monday, November 23rd. The stock market was closed on the weekend, so only Bitcoin moved first.
- December FOMC interest rate decision. The minutes suggested a further increase, but it was not confirmed.
- Is $55,130 the low point of this decline? The price, which returned 9% in just over two hours, does not tell us the nature of the bottom.

## Remaining schedule

The closest gateway is the reopening of the U.S. market on Monday, November 23. It is highly likely that the extent to which Nasdaq reverses its 4% decline will lead to the direction of Bitcoin. Next is ETF funds. The signal is whether the outflow is decreasing or whether funds are coming back from IBIT. The last is the FOMC on December 8-9 and the price and employment indicators released before then.

There is only one thing we can confirm now. This rebound is a rebound from the loss of debt, and it has not yet been confirmed whether money will come back in that place.

title: 24 years without a visa — Jeju visa-free, light and dark of 11,945 people
deck: We cross-checked statistics from the Ministry of Justice and the National Police Agency, press briefings from the Ministry of Justice, a survey of the Jeju Tourism Organization, and remarks from the Provincial Council. Illegal stays increased and tourist spending decreased. Between abolition and management, we distinguish between confirmed numbers and unverified claims.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: The number of illegal residents entering Jeju without a visa increased from 9,972 in 2021 to 11,945 in August 2026, of which 10,134 (84.8%) are Chinese. The number of foreign suspects arrested by the Jeju Police Agency also increased by 25.7% from 610 in 2024 to 767 in 2025.

The Ministry of Justice announced an intensive crackdown from October 7 to December 11 (232 people caught by October 28), 3,103 people denied entry from January to September, and a plan to introduce a 'departure pre-departure check system' for domestic flights from Jeju, but the timing and procedures for operating the system have not yet been determined.

Jeju tourism made up for the decrease in domestic tourists (-2.2%) with an increase in foreigners (+17.7%), but per capita spending on cruises decreased to $122.1 (2025), and spending by individual tourists from the Greater China region ($866.7) was the lowest among major regions. The abolition bill (11/13) and the theory of strengthening management (11/17) are competing.
body:
The visa-free system, which allows people to enter Jeju Island without a visa and stay for up to 30 days, began in 2002 with the creation of Jeju Free International City. 24 years later, this system became the subject of a bill to abolish it in the National Assembly and a rebuttal speech in the Provincial Assembly. The starting point is numbers. According to data submitted by the Ministry of Justice to the National Assembly, the number of illegal foreigners who entered Jeju without a visa increased to 9,972 in 2021, 10,826 in 2023, 11,426 in 2024, 11,581 in 2025, and 11,945 at the end of August 2026. Among them, 10,134 people were Chinese, or 84.8%.

## 10,000 people, accumulated number

This number is not the number of new arrivals each year, but rather the number of people confirmed to be illegally residing in Jeju at that time. The curve, which decreased from 9,972 in 2021 to 8,569 in 2022 and then increased again, reflects the suspension and recovery of entry during the COVID-19 period. Comparing the 11,581 people in 2025 to the 357,598 illegal aliens nationwide, it is 3.2%. This is the ratio suggested by Rep. Han Dong-soo, chairman of the Jeju Provincial Council's Culture, Tourism and Sports Committee, in a 5-minute free speech at the plenary session on November 17. Police statistics moved separately. The number of foreign criminal suspects arrested by the Jeju Police Agency increased by 25.7% from 610 in 2024 to 767 in 2025, of which 556 (72.5%) were Chinese. During the same period, the number of foreigners visiting Jeju increased by 17.7% from 1,907,945 to 2,244,169. It is also important to note that as the number of people staying increases, the number of cases may also increase.

## Ministry of Justice's prescription, three prongs

The government's response is divided into crackdown, entry screening, and movement management. The Ministry of Justice announced on October 30 that it conducted an intensive crackdown on foreigners who entered Jeju illegally without a visa from October 7 to December 11 and caught 232 people as of October 28. Illegal employment employers and brokers are also subject to crackdowns. At the entry stage, there were 3,103 foreigners who were denied entry to Jeju from January to September this year. The Ministry of Justice explained that it is using the Passenger Pre-Confirmation System (IPC) to prevent people wanted by Interpol and people with domestic criminal records from boarding aircraft. Movement management is still in the design phase. They said they would introduce a 'departure pre-confirmation system' to check whether foreign passengers can depart when issuing boarding passes for domestic flights departing from Jeju, but the operation time and confirmation procedure have not been determined as budget security and system construction remain. On November 19, a government-wide meeting was held at the Jeju Immigration Office.

## What the visa-free leaves behind in Jeju

The share of foreigners in Jeju’s economy is growing. The number of tourists visiting Jeju in 2025 was 13,846,961, an increase of 0.6% from a year ago, but the number of domestic tourists decreased by 2.2% to 11,602,792 and the number of foreigners increased by 17.7% to 2,244,169. Among foreigners, Chinese account for 70.2% (1,588,107 people). Representative Han Dong-soo said, “The number of domestic tourists decreased by about 240,000 last year, but the number of foreign tourists increased by about 340,000, offsetting the decrease.” The problem is the density of consumption. According to an analysis by the Bank of Korea's Jeju headquarters (as of 2023), the average spending per cruise tourist is $188, which is 27% of the individual tourists staying in Jeju ($693). The stay time is short, around 8 hours, and consumption is concentrated in large duty-free stores. Afterwards, expenditures decreased further. According to a survey of tourists visiting Jeju Island, spending per cruise tourist decreased to $157.1 in 2024 and $122.1 in 2025. Individual tourists who enter without a visa are no exception. In the Jeju Tourism Organization's 2024 survey, the proportion of individual travel among tourists from the Greater China region was the highest at 94.3%, but per capita spending was $866.7, the lowest among major regions. The average for all individual foreign travelers in the same year was $943.7.

![Jeju Port arrival hall and passenger ship. Visa exemption is a system that exempts people from visas, not a system that exempts them from immigration screening. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/jeju-visa-free-entry-tradeoff.jpg)

## Calculations surrounding ‘By Land’

Jeju Island announced that Governor Wi Gon Wi met with Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism Choi Hwi-young on July 18 and proposed allowing visa-free tourists to travel to other regions. The idea is to increase stays and consumption by using Jeju as an inbound gateway. Objections came from three directions. It has been reported that the Ministry of Justice has already responded to the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism in March with an opinion that it would be difficult to accept due to the continued prevention and crackdown on illegal stay. Even within the tourism industry, calculations are divided. Kang Dong-hoon, head of the Jeju Island Tourism Association, said, "If it is conditioned on staying for more than 2 nights and 3 days, it is welcome," but added, "If it is only a transit through Jeju, the shortage of airline seats will worsen and it will not be helpful to Jeju tourism." Yonhap News pointed out that if the itinerary of 4 nights in Jeju is changed to '1 night in Jeju and 3 nights in Seoul', the number of stays in Korea may increase but consumption in Jeju may decrease. At the October National Assembly audit, Rep. Jin Jong-oh questioned the circumstances of the proposal, and Governor Wi responded, “We stopped it because the Ministry of Justice said it was difficult,” and “We will abolish it.” At the same meeting, Governor Wi also said, “Foreigner crimes in the Jeju region account for less than 1% of all crimes.”

## Between abolition and management

On November 13, Rep. Song Eon-seok proposed a revision to the Jeju Special Act. This is a bill that eliminates the visa-free special provision itself. Representative Song stated the reason, saying, “The safety and peaceful daily life of the people are threatened due to the side effects of the system.” Four days later, on the 17th, Rep. Han Dong-soo gave a five-minute speech with the exact opposite logic. “Visa exemption is a system that exempts people from visas in accordance with the law, not a system that exempts them from immigration screening,” he said. “To abolish the system, accurate statistics and sufficient verification are required first.” The prescription was also different. If unauthorized movement to the mainland is a problem, departure confirmation and crackdown on brokers must be strengthened, and if illegal employment is a problem, crackdown on placement organizations and hiring employers must be strengthened. The head of Jeju Island's Tourism Exchange Bureau said, "Linking the visa-free system to an increase in the crime rate for foreigners is an oversimplification of the purpose of introducing the system and its impact on the tourism industry." What has been confirmed is statistics showing an increase in illegal stays and foreign suspects, survey results showing low spending by cruise ships and individual tourists from Greater China, and the fact that the government's response is still in the stage of crackdowns and system construction. Whether abolition will reduce the number or whether checking attendance and cracking down on employers will come first has not yet been proven by the results.
