title: Why are half of the super tankers passing through Hormuz ships made by Korean companies?
deck: In the community, '93 ships, 40%, net profit 63 times' were compared one by one with the primary report and ship tracking data. The numbers were generally correct, but the conclusions were slightly different.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: Oil tankers owned by Janggeum Merchant Marine (Sinoco) carried 105.6 million barrels (37%) of the 286.3 million barrels of crude oil that passed through Hormuz in September 2026. Lloyd's List calculated the number of VLCC traffic to be 47% in September and more than 50% from October 1 to 10.

Iran's Persian Gulf Straits Authority (PGSA) increased its sanctions list from 45 vessels on August 24 to 240 vessels on November 2, of which at least 46 vessels were related to the Janggeum Merchant Marine. On October 27, it was announced that legal action would be taken against the entire fleet starting November 1. This is the first case targeting an entire specific shipping company.

The community post's '63 times net profit' has not been confirmed. As an unlisted company, its 2026 performance has not been announced, and the last number officially confirmed is its consolidated net profit of 663.7 billion won in 2025. WTI rose 25.3% from $67.02 just before the war to $83.98 on November 20.
body:
At 00:32 on November 22, 2026, a post was posted on the MLBPARK bullpen saying, “Korean companies are playing a very big role in destroying Iran.” Before twelve hours had passed, there were 4,851 views, 11 recommendations, and 27 comments. The main character of the article is Janggeum Merchant Marine (English name: Sinokor), a mid-sized shipping company headquartered in Bukchang-dong, Seoul.

There are three numbers that the community is excited about. “Owned 93 oil tankers, including 150 rented ships”, “40% of Hormuz crude oil, more than 50% in October”, “63 times net profit”. Among these, we tried to guess in order which ones were confirmed as primary reports, which ones were exaggerations, and which invoices were left after the numbers.

## Why does this company owe half of Hormuz?

The answer is that the ship was purchased before the war broke out. Janggeum Merchant Marine was a company that focused on the Korea-China container route, and from the end of 2025, it began purchasing used very large crude carriers (VLCCs) with funds from the co-founder of MSC, the world's largest container shipping company.

According to Clarkson, a British shipping information company, Janggeum Merchant Marine's VLCC increased from 42 ships in December 2025 to 93 ships in August 2026, and 99 ships in early November. The total tanker fleet is the world's largest, with 162 vessels as of August. If you include ships borrowed from other shipping companies, it is estimated that the operating scale is 130 to 150 ships.

Money was also concentrated. According to shipping data company Besennautical, Janggeum spent about $6 billion to purchase 73 oil tankers as of August this year. It is an amount similar to the combined investment amount of the eight companies that were the second most purchased during the same period. The Wall Street Journal reported in July that Vice Chairman Jeong Ga-hyeon invested about $7 billion just before the war to build the world's largest VLCC fleet. At the time, Janggeum operated more than 160 oil tankers and accounted for about 17% of the global oil tanker market.

The war began with the U.S. and Israel's airstrikes on Iran in late February, and the situation changed in March when Iran began blocking the Strait of Hormuz. While other shipping companies pulled out, the company that left the ship behind remained. Since mid-April, Janggeum Merchant Marine has been in charge of transporting crude oil for ADNOC, the UAE's national oil company, from inside the strait to the Gulf of Oman.

## How does the shuttle work?

It is a method of dividing one voyage into two sections. The shuttle tanker carries 2 million barrels of crude oil from a terminal inside the Persian Gulf and passes only the most dangerous section of the Strait of Hormuz. The cargo is transferred and loaded onto an empty oil tanker waiting in the Gulf of Oman outside the strait (ship-to-ship transfer, STS), and then returned inside. Long-distance ships go to Asia without entering the risk zone.

The method of operation is not recorded. There are many so-called ‘dark sailings’ that turn off the Automatic Identification System (AIS) and pass by on the opposite coast of Iran at night. By July, about 3.5 million barrels per day were leaving the strait through these shuttles and transshipments. This is about one-third of the daily crude oil that passes through the strait (S&P Global Energy). Many of the ships were escorted by the US Navy, which even mobilized fighter jets.

The scale became larger. In August, more than 70% of the crude oil that crossed Hormuz changed ships in the waters off Fujairah and Sohar. Transshipment volume between ships in September was 2.5 million barrels per day, nearly double that of August (1.4 million barrels). Kpler, a shipping information company, estimates that the Gulf of Oman shuttle fleet is about 80 ships, and that Janggeum Merchant Marine controls about half of them. The transshipment base was Fujairah 54% and Sohar 45%.

![A very large oil tanker passing through the Strait of Hormuz and a vessel waiting outside the strait. Shuttle operations only repeatedly pass through dangerous sections and cargo is handed over at sea. — Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/sinokor-hormuz-shuttle-oil.jpg)

## Is it 37% or 50% — both are correct, the counting units are different

If counted in barrels, it is 37%, and if counted in number of passages, it is 47-50%. According to Bloomberg's analysis of ship tracking data from Vortexa, Equisys, and Signal Ocean, oil tankers owned by Janggeum Merchant Marine loaded 105.6 million barrels of crude oil through Hormuz in September 2026. It is 37% of the total 286.3 million barrels of crude oil that passed through the strait in the same month. The average is 3.52 million barrels per day.

There are numbers that can be compared. The Saudi National Shipping (Bahri), Kuwait Oil Tanker, and ADNOC shipping sectors, ranked 2nd to 4th, combined had 97.3 million barrels. This means that one company carried more cargo than the three Gulf state-owned fleets combined. However, this tally is based on ship ownership. Due to the nature of the oil tanker market where ship owners, charterers, and shippers are different, this does not mean that “Janggeum Merchant Marine directly operated the cargo.”

If you look at the number of passages, the proportion is higher. Lloyd's List reported that of the 292 VLCC passages that passed through Hormuz in September, 137 (47%) were vessels related to Janggeum Merchant Marine, and from October 1 to 10, the number exceeded 50%. The share for November has not yet been disclosed.

The “93 ships” in the community post matches the number of VLCCs owned by Clarkson in August, and the “150 ships” also does not deviate from the operational estimate (130-150 ships) including charters. “September 40%” is an expression for an increase of 37%.

## Why did Iran target the company and not the ship?

This is because it was judged that the company's traffic could not be reduced by penalizing each ship. Iran created the Persian Gulf Straits Authority (PGSA) in May to manage the Hormuz passage, and has been disclosing a list of vessels that have violated the passage procedures established by Iran. Starting with 45 ships (5 related to Janggeum Merchant Marine) on August 24, 77 ships were added in September, 122 ships on October 27, and 114 ships were added on November 2, bringing the number to 240 ships.

Among these, there are at least 46 vessels related to Janggeum Merchant Marine. This is about half of the VLCC fleet owned and managed. On October 27, PGSA posted to Warnings were also issued to shippers and insurance companies. This is the first case of openly targeting the entire fleet of a specific shipping company.

The details of the execution were not disclosed. The means that the PGSA has been referring to are fines, detention, and confiscation. However, Iran's independent list does not have the same legal status as the internationally approved sanctions list, and it was not confirmed that the ships on the list were actually detained or seized until early November.

The explanation of Janggeum Merchant Marine begins with the ownership structure. Based on confirmation from Janggeum Merchant Marine on October 28, the Korea Shipping Association said, “The ship identified as subject to sanctions is a re-chartered ship that Janggeum Maritime borrowed from a ship 100% owned by an overseas shipowner and then lent it back to an overseas oil company. Commercial operations are determined by the company that rented the ship again.” An example is the Mombasa B, which was hit on July 14th. ADNOC's shipping subsidiary ADNOC L&S announced that it would operate the ship on a term charter basis.

## Then, did they press down on the oil price — the direction was right, the formula was wrong

Without the shuttle, oil prices would have been higher. However, the decline in November cannot be explained by this one company.

Let’s start with the numbers. WTI was $67.02 per barrel on February 27, just before the war, and soared to $111.54 in early April. The spot price of Brent crude oil in October was an average of $124 per month, the highest since the war (U.S. Energy Information Administration). After that, it fell by more than $30 by November 18, and on November 20, WTI fell to $83.98 and Brent to $92.57, falling for three consecutive weeks. If we accurately calculate the increase rate that the community post said was “about 20%,” it is 25.3% (67.02 → 83.98). The direction is correct and the width is slightly larger.

The cause of the decline cannot be summarized in one line. According to Kpler, Middle East crude oil exports in November returned to 90% of pre-war levels at 15.3 million barrels per day. However, the proportion passing through Hormuz is 60%, lower than before the war (80%). The rest were diverted to pipelines. This means that major projects such as the UAE's Abu Dhabi-Fujairah oil pipeline and the Iraq-Türkiye (Ceyhan) oil pipeline have worked to that extent.

There are also remarks from the US side. Secretary of State Rubio said at the G7 meeting in Paris on November 9-10, “Some nights it is 80 to 85% of what it was before the war,” and “the reason it is not 100% is because Iranian crude oil is not going out.” The International Energy Agency (IEA) predicted that supply would exceed demand in the fourth quarter for the first time since the war.

To summarize, it is as follows. The shuttle is a key device that prevents Gulf crude oil from being blocked. In fact, in September, 3.5 million barrels per day passed through the strait in this way. However, the forces that have depressed oil prices include pipeline bypass, shuttles from other ship owners (Bahri, KOTC, ADNOC), US Navy escorts, the US maritime blockade that reduced Iranian crude oil exports to zero, and a slowdown in demand. “Almost number one contribution” in a community post is understandable as an expression referring to the size of contribution, but it is not a sentence that pins the blame on one company.

One more thing. Shuttles also create costs that push up oil prices. The insurance premium for moving Middle Eastern crude oil to East Asia jumped approximately 200 times between January and October, reaching $12.29 per barrel (OPEC). Freight and insurance fees are added to the arrival price of crude oil.

## Who pays the bills?

They are sailors. Combining IMO records and foreign media reports, 10 attacks on 9 vessels related to the Janggeum Merchant Marine have been confirmed since June (counted on November 12). Lloyd's List counted the attack on the Fujairah Energy ship on November 10 as the ninth attack on the company's VLCC since June.

- On July 14, Mombasa B was attacked by a cruise missile. WSJ and Yonhap News reported that one Indian sailor died. The number of injured varies depending on the media.
- On November 10, the Fujairah Energy was hit by a projectile while en route from Al-Ruwais to Dubai, injuring four of the 22 people on board.
- On November 11, the Dominican Prosperity's engine room was hit and caught fire off the coast of Ras Al Khaimah, and all 22 crew members were evacuated by the UAE Coast Guard. Reuters reported that this ship was operated by Janggeum Merchant Marine.

On November 12, International Maritime Organization (IMO) Director-General Arsenio Domínguez again urged “ship owners and operators to refrain from commercial activities in the strait that expose seafarers to unacceptable risks.” There are criticisms both inside and outside the company, asking, “Should we continue to sail with the lives of sailors as collateral?” (Chosun Biz, October 7).

How much money was there? In September, one VLCC was contracted for a charter fee of over $1 million per day, and spot operation revenue rose to $700,000 per day (13 times last year's average of $55,000). Bloomberg estimated that Janggeum Merchant Marine may have earned up to $120 million through ADNOC shuttle transportation in July. Hazard pay was also added. In July, the company decided to pay an additional six months' salary for a one-month round trip to Hormuz, and the additional allowance was in the range of $9,000 to $90,000 (Bloomberg).

As for the company's overall performance, the last official numbers are KRW 3.7249 trillion in consolidated sales, KRW 616.2 billion in operating profit, and KRW 663.7 billion in net profit in 2025. Because it is an unlisted company, its 2026 performance has not yet been announced.

## Community post, to what extent is it correct?

- “Has 93 tankers” — That’s right. As of August 2026, 93 VLCCs based on Clarkson. 99 ships in early November.
- “150 boats, including rented boats” — That is a correct estimate. 130 to 150 ships in operation, including charter.
- “September 40%” — Only half true. 37% based on barrels, 47% based on number of passages.
- “Over 50% in October” — That’s right. Lloyd's List's tally from October 1 to 10.
- “CNN's 80% pre-war recovery” — Close to the truth. However, this figure excludes Iranian crude oil, and K-Pler's tally for November is 90% of total exports and 60% of Hormuz diesel.
- “Iranian Shipping Authority” — Inaccurate. The Persian Gulf Straits Authority (PGSA) was created by Iran in May.
- “63 times earnings” — Not confirmed. As it is an unlisted company, its 2026 performance has not been announced. The last confirmed net profit is 663.7 billion won in 2025.
- “WTI rises 20%” — The direction is correct and the width is 25.3%.
- “Almost the number one contributor” — This is an exaggeration. The contributions were significant, but pipeline diversions, shuttles from other shipowners, and the U.S. blockade worked together.
- “It attacks, but the damage is light” — No. There have been cases of death and injury, engine room fires, and everyone evacuating.

## See you next

- Hormuz passage and shuttle proportion in November. When Lloyd's List Intelligence's monthly brief comes out, it will be possible to check whether the proportion that exceeded half in October has been maintained.
- Whether the PGSA is enforceable. It has not yet been confirmed whether the fleet-wide legal action announced on November 1 resulted in actual detention and fines.
- War risk insurance premiums and securing crew. As long as the insurance premium remains in the $12 per barrel range, the economic feasibility of the shuttle will remain, but as captains increasingly refuse passage, it will become difficult to operate the fleet itself.
- Joint screening between Janggeum Maritime and MSC. The two companies are pursuing a 50-50 joint venture, and competition authorities in Korea, Greece, and Cyprus are conducting an evaluation. Once the joint venture is completed, half of the fleet will be under a joint management system.

title: 4,869.96 left over — 563 trillion won loss estimate and calculation of ‘Black Monday’
deck: KOSPI sank to its lowest level in 10 months, and New York collapsed further over the weekend. We confirmed with public data the two voices of the community and the battle between the government and the opposition party to determine what assumptions Citi's estimate of 563 trillion won is based on.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: On November 20, KOSPI closed at 4,869.96, down 5.21%, and KOSDAQ closed at 645.68, down 5.71%. It is the lowest in 10 months, down 46.6% from the all-time high closing price on June 22, and selling sidecars were activated in both markets.

Citi estimated household stock capital losses in the second half of the year to be KRW 224 trillion in the third quarter and KRW 339 trillion in the fourth quarter, for a total of KRW 563 trillion. This is an estimate of valuation loss assuming that domestic and overseas stock returns follow KOSPI and NASDAQ, and is not a loss confirmed by actual selling.

The government advocates fundamentals and a three-month exemption from the obligation to maintain a 140% collateral ratio for credit loans, while the opposition party aims to postpone single-stock leveraged ETFs and national pension rebalancing. The NASDAQ fell an additional 5.28% over the weekend, so the opening on the 23rd is a variable.
body:
At 3:30 pm on the 20th, KOSPI closed at 4,869.96. It fell 267.93 points (5.21%) from the previous trading day. Based on the closing price, it is the lowest in 10 months since January 16 (4,840.74). KOSDAQ also ended at 645.68, down 39.13 points (5.71%). Selling sidecars were activated one after another in both markets. Compared to the all-time high closing price on June 22 (9,114.55), 46.6% disappeared in 5 months, and the market capitalization fell below 4,000 trillion won in 10 months to 3,991 trillion won. In the New York market on the 20th (local time), which was held after KOSPI closed, Nasdaq collapsed by a further 5.28%. After the weekend and ahead of the opening on Monday the 23rd, Friday's drop is being recalculated.

## The 5,000 mark collapsed in three days.

In this decline, the first closing price below the 5,000 line was on the 17th (4,968.48, 2.59%↓). Three days later, the index fell to 4,831.69 (-5.96%) during the day. At the center of the decline were large-cap semiconductor stocks. Samsung Electronics closed at 183,100 won, down 7.01%, and SK Hynix closed at 1,113,000 won, down 5.92%. Foreigners net sold KRW 1.142 trillion for 6 consecutive trading days (cumulative KRW 5.0965 trillion), and institutions also sold KRW 951 billion. Individuals bought 1.5955 trillion won. The reasons cited were the concentration of funds due to Antropic's largest-ever initial public offering ($107.3 billion raised), concerns about strengthening regulations on mass semiconductors in the United States, and the possibility of an interest rate hike by the Federal Reserve. On the same day, the Nikkei (-5.06%) and Taiwan's Jiquan Index (-6.23%) also plummeted.

## 563 trillion won is estimated as ‘valuation loss’

In a report on the 19th, Citibank Korea Chief Economist Kim Jin-wook estimated household stock capital losses in the second half of this year to be about 563 trillion won. This is the sum of KRW 224 trillion in the third quarter and KRW 339 trillion in the fourth quarter, which is almost exactly the return of the KRW 579 trillion earned in the first half of the year. This corresponds to approximately 19% of annual nominal GDP and approximately 37% of private consumption expenditure. Applying the Bank of Korea's marginal propensity to consume on stock assets (1.5%) could reduce private consumption by about 8.4 trillion won, and Citi believes that this effect is equivalent to raising the base interest rate by 0.50 to 0.75 percentage points. However, this is an estimate assuming that households' domestic and overseas stock returns followed KOSPI and NASDAQ, respectively. It is not a loss confirmed by actual sales, and the fourth quarter is not yet over. The temperature of the market appeared first in other indicators. As of the 19th, investor deposits were KRW 81.5669 trillion, the lowest of the year, and the average daily trading volume was 239 million shares, the lowest since May 2014. Of the 94 equity-linked securities (ELS) issued in June, 46 had no record of early redemption as of the 16th.

![Yeouido stock price and decline chart. On the 20th, KOSPI closed at 4,869.96, down 5.21%. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/kospi-4800-household-loss-563trillion.jpg)

## “Mondays are scary”, two voices from the community

33 comments were posted on ‘KOSPI’s estimated loss of 563 trillion won from 9,000 to 5,000’ posted on Clien on the morning of the 20th. “Most of the 563 trillion won must have been taken by foreigners,” and “It should be considered based on buying and selling, but it is easy to incite losses by using the highest score evaluation standard.” The next day, in 'Why this stock decline is fatal', the comment "Investors are responsible for investment losses, but the government is also not free from criticism for failing to fulfill its role despite overheating" received sympathy. On the 20th, 'Songsori are coming out little by little' wrote, "Some of the liquidated songs are starting to come out." In Bobae Dream's 'Money is Melting Through Stocks' (17th, 316 recommendations, 17,959 views), "Stocks are unconditionally your responsibility" and "There are many people who invested in the government and lost money" were recommended side by side. Articles titled ‘2008 financial crisis level’ were also posted on Pomppu (20th) and Inven (17th). On the 21st, it was reported on Blind that an account screen with a loss of 280 million won was posted along with the message, “280 million won already lost, Monday is scary.”

## Government responsibility theory and global coordination theory

On the 6th, the government held an emergency market situation review meeting chaired by Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hyeong-il and decided to exempt securities companies from the obligation to maintain the collateral ratio (140%) for credit loans for three months. It took effect from the 9th. At the meeting, “mid-3% growth, exports expected to exceed 1 trillion won, and corporate operating profit expected to exceed 900 trillion won” were presented as the basis. On the same day, the ruling party also held an emergency meeting, and President Lee Jae-myung said at the Korea Exchange on the 13th, "The higher the mountain, the deeper the valley." The opposition party aims at a different point. On the 20th, People Power Party representative Jang Dong-hyuk called for a 'special investigation into stock price manipulation', saying, "This is the result of stock price manipulation for local elections." On the 21st, Rep. Na Kyung-won called for an investigation into the introduction of a single-stock leveraged ETF and the postponement of national pension rebalancing, saying, "Take the people's money." The ruling party emphasizes external factors. Kim Min-seok, leader of the Democratic Party, said on the 6th, "The main reason is the growing concern about a decline in investment in AI data centers after the U.S. midterm elections," and floor leader Byeong-do Han countered, saying, "The fundamentals of our economy, supported by exports and corporate performance, are solid." Taiwan strengthened short-selling restrictions when the Jiquan Index fell below the 39,000 level on the 19th, and the Stability Fund approved the tenth fund mobilization on the 9th of this month. The Seoul Economic Daily pointed out, “On the other hand, there are no clear measures to stabilize the stock market in Korea.”

## Monday the 23rd, remaining variables

On the 20th (local time) in New York, NASDAQ fell 5.28%, S&P 500 fell 3.70%, and Dow fell 1.93%. NVIDIA plunged 14.01% due to reports of an accounting investigation by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and Antropic, which was on its second day of listing, also ended at a weak 8% level. The volatility index (VIX) rose 26.2% to 35.89. In Korea, as foreigners continue to be net sellers for seven consecutive months (accumulated approximately 166 trillion won), there are concerns that counter-selling volume may pour in at Monday's opening. Securities companies also see that the decline is already at a historic level. The largest drop of 46% from the peak is the third since 2000, following the dot-com bubble (55.7%) and the financial crisis (54.5%). Samsung Securities calculated that the 12-month average rate of return after the bottom of the past eight sharp declines was 59.9%. No one has determined when the bottom point was. What was confirmed before the opening on the 23rd was the index and supply and demand numbers, and what was not confirmed was the location of the bottom.

title: Map of ingredients for a bowl of Malatang — Between YouTuber’s warning and Ministry of Food and Drug Safety records
deck: The issue raised by Daeryangnam TV, the number of cases detected by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, and the hygiene records of Chinese tea brands that landed in Korea and Haidilao were cross-checked with public data. How to distinguish between confirmed facts and claims.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
tags: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety
summary: Daeryangnam TV raised the issue of additives and hygiene in Chinese tofu and malatang raw materials in a video, but this claim is based on local reporting and is not based on product-level hazard test data.

According to the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety records, 37 out of 63 Malatang businesses and raw material companies were detected in 2019, the number of pesticide residues detected in Chinese wood ear mushrooms was 5 to 238 times higher, and 552 cases (38.9%) of the 1,420 cases of import nonconformity in 2025 remain from China.

Cha Baekdo, Michele, Heiti, Charge, and Haidilao, which entered Korea, have a history of local store hygiene incidents and company actions, and domestic branches can be individually confirmed through hygiene grades and administrative disposition records.
body:
On April 30, the waiting time at the first store of Chinese milk tea brand Charge in Sinchon, Seoul was 188 minutes. There were 194 teams on standby at Haidilao Hongdae branch. Malatang became the most ordered menu among the top 10 food delivery apps, and four Chinese tea brands opened within 1km of Myeongdong. Behind trends is the movement of raw materials. The question is to what extent the movement is recorded.

## The YouTuber’s warning and the official record are different.

Daeryangnam TV [Clarktv] is a channel with 1.24 million subscribers and consistently uploads videos about the current state of food in China. “Foods containing various toxic substances… Please be careful if they are sold in Korea as well!” (560,000 views) deals with additives and low-cost frozen raw materials used in malatang broth, fish cakes, and meatballs, and shorts “You can’t even buy tofu in Korea anymore...?” and “The hidden truth about everyone’s favorite malatang...?” are also in the same category. In an April 2025 report, he said of Chinese tofu, "Chinese people are boycotting this product, but I heard that these ingredients are coming to Korea."

This is a broadcaster's claim based on local reporting, and is not data that proves the harmfulness of a specific product by testing it. Expressions such as “the risks of cigarettes are the same as those of cigarettes” are not based on epidemiological studies. Please refer to the direction of the warning, but check the basis separately.

## Numbers remaining in Ministry of Food and Drug Safety records

Official records are more specific and narrower. In July 2019, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety inspected 63 Malatang restaurants and raw material suppliers across the country, and 37 were found to have poor hygiene and no indication of manufacturing date or expiration date. In March 2023, 51 out of 3,000 Malatang delivery restaurants were caught for storing products beyond their expiration date, and according to a KBS report in October of the same year, there were 119 violations in 600 stores of 8 Malatang brands over the past five years.

This was repeated in raw materials as well. In February 2023, 2.38 mg/kg of carbendazim, which was 238 times the standard value (0.01 mg/kg), was detected and recalled in dried wood ear mushrooms from China, and in September of that year, 3,030 kg of chlormequat was detected in white wood ear mushrooms, which was 12 times the standard level (0.01 mg/kg). In September 2026, the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety recalled three cases of wood ear mushrooms and white wood ear mushrooms from China within 10 days, and the detected amounts were 5 to 24 times the standard. According to import statistics, of the 1,420 cases of nonconformity in 2025, Chinese products accounted for the most with 552 cases (38.9%), and 97 of them were violations of pesticide residue limits. However, the nonconformity ratio compared to total income is 0.16%.

![A bowl of malatang, imported raw materials, and inspection records. Of the 1,420 cases of import nonconformity in 2025, 552 were Chinese. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/maratang-ingredients-distribution.jpg)

## At what point in the chain does the information break?

Dried tofu, fish cake, marinara sauce, and dried mushrooms go from importers to restaurants through intermediary distributors. Although the product name is included in the customs clearance declaration, the raw material combination, manufacturing date, and lot number are often not provided to the restaurant. Of the 792,374 import declarations in 2023, only 13.3% were detailed inspections and 5.1% were random sample inspections. Most of the passed quantity is released into the market without additional inspection. What the consumer encounters is a bag of finished product, and the history remains further up the chain.

## The second trend, Chinese tea brands

After opening its first store in Korea in January 2024, Chabaekdo now operates about 50 stores, Michel, which opened in Heukseok-dong in 2022, has 16 stores, Hay Tea has 5 to 6 stores in major commercial districts, and 11 Charges opened simultaneously in Gangnam, Sinchon, and Yongsan on April 30. Cha Baekdo's 'Mango Pomelo Sago' large size is 6,900 won, delivery order is 8,400 won, and in China, it costs 10 to 20 yuan (2,000 to 4,000 won).

Hygiene records came from headquarters and local stores. In May 2021, Michelangelo's Zhengzhou store was found to have used expired ingredients and changed the opening date label, resulting in 35 corrective actions, 3 immediate closures, and 9 administrative penalties. In June 2024, a store in Beijing's Chaoyang District was closed and disinfected after a video showed an employee washing his feet in a beverage sink, and on March 14, 2025, a store in Yichang, Hubei, was booked for using precipitated lemons and oranges and infesting flies. In January 2026, when a video of an employee squeezing a lemon with his bare hands went viral at a Fujian store, Charge fired the employee and closed the store indefinitely. Each company responded with an apology, closure, and retraining, and the CEO of Charge Korea said, “We will apply strict standards to employee training, hygiene, and safety management.”

There is also a record on the raw materials side. The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety issued an inspection order for leachable tea made in China from June 30, 2023, mandating preliminary inspection of residual pesticides. When noncompliance was repeated, it was redesignated from June 2026 to June 2027. The issue is not nationality, but repeated nonconformity with pesticide residues and management at the store level.

## Haidilao, Confirmation and Clarification

In August 2017, China's Legislative Reporter reported, through four months of undercover coverage, about rats in the kitchens of two Beijing stores and scenes of sewers being dug with a ladle. Haidilao apologized and ordered hygiene inspections at all stores and overseas stores, and Beijing authorities ordered the kitchen to be opened to the public and report inspection results within a month. In February 2025, the pot urination incident at the Shanghai store was the act of a customer, and the company replaced all pots and dishes and provided refunds and 10 times compensation to 4,109 visitors over 13 days. The court ordered 2.2 million yuan in compensation to the offending student and his parents. When four members of a family complained of gastroenteritis at the Seletar Mall branch in Singapore in October 2025, no hygiene problems were found during an on-site inspection by the Singapore Food Authority, and the company paid all medical expenses. In Korea, in the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety's hygiene rating inquiry, Haidilao Daehakro branch was confirmed as a 'food safe establishment' (May 20, 2024 - May 19, 2026), with 0 administrative dispositions. However, this is a record of one branch and not a guarantee of all branches.

## What consumers can directly check

You can see the product name, manufacturer, reason for nonconformity, and date in ‘Imported Food Nonconformity’ on the Imported Food Information Maru (impfood.mfds.go.kr). In Food Safety Nara, you can check the hygiene grade and administrative disposition history of a business, and the country of origin is even displayed for the primary raw materials of processed foods. If there is anything wrong, report it to 1399.

The fact that Chinese raw materials are used is not illegal in itself. The problem is that lot records are lost in multi-level distribution, and store management cannot keep up with the brand's expansion speed. Even if the epidemic passes, inspection records and recall history remain.

title: If there are no parts, the warranty is also a piece of paper — Chinese car after-sales service, confirmed record
deck: BYD electric buses in the metropolitan area were stopped for a maximum of 315 days, and passenger car accident repairs took 3.1 days longer than the domestic average. The gap between sales and maintenance numbers was pointed out using confirmed data and the manufacturer's explanation.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: Electric buses made in China were confirmed to be out of operation for a long period of time due to delays in the supply of parts. One BYD bus in the metropolitan area has been stopped for 315 days, four buses in Gyeonggi Province have been stopped for more than a month, and two out of six buses in Gimpo cannot be operated because parts cannot be obtained.

For BYD passenger cars, the average repair time for 373 accidents in the first half of this year was 9.8 days, which was 3.1 days longer than the average for domestic electric passenger cars, and the average rental price was twice that of domestic cars (1,076,000 won). The property loss ratio was 168.4%, the highest among electric passenger vehicle brands.

Sales increased to 21,731 units from January to October, but there are only 5 accident repair bases, and the battery warranty in Korea is 8 years and 160,000 km, which is shorter than in Europe (8 years and 250,000 km). An amendment to increase the 8-year parts supply obligation to law is pending in the National Assembly.

body:
A BYD electric bus was parked in the garage of a bus transportation company in Incheon for nearly a year. It was a vehicle that was involved in a traffic accident in 2025. The waiting time for parts was longer than the accident itself. OBS Gyeongin TV exclusively reported on the 22nd of last month that the vehicle's suspension period is 315 days. The company representative said on the broadcast, "Since the company is from China, parts supply is not good, and we should not feel like we are victims by buying Chinese buses."

On the 28th of the same month, a different number came out at the Gimpo City Council. The answer was that among the six buses deployed to the Han River Joint Bus, two Chinese-made electric buses cannot be operated because parts could not be obtained, and the remaining one is stopped due to a fire. Kim Soon, head of the public transportation department, said, “We are unable to find a solution because we cannot obtain parts and it is difficult to replace them with other parts.”

Domestic sales of Chinese cars are fast. There were also criticisms that maintenance, parts, and warranties could not keep up with the speed. This article summarizes the gap with verified reports, government data, and the manufacturer's official position. The estimates and experiences spread in online communities were not conclusively confirmed as facts, but were separately marked as ‘raised cases’.

## Number sold and number repaired

BYD launched a domestic passenger car brand in January 2025. Based on registration with the Korea Automobile Importers and Distributors Association (KAIDA), sales from January to October this year amounted to 21,731 units, which is 3.6 times higher than last year's annual sales volume (6,107 units). Among imported car brands, it ranks 4th after Tesla, BMW, and Mercedes-Benz.

The maintenance base is also increasing. The number of service centers increased from 11 at the time of launch to 21 last month, and the goal is to have 26 by the end of the year. The company says that it has 94 workbays, which are maintenance work spaces, and can handle up to about 10,000 vehicles per month. As of the end of October, there were 72 technicians in charge of electric vehicle maintenance. The parts distribution center in Pyeongtaek, Gyeonggi Province, also grew from 300 pyeong in December 2024 to 2,000 pyeong last month.

The problem is accident repair. Among the 21 official service centers, there are only five that can do sheet metal and painting: Yangcheon in Seoul, Anyang and Suwon in Gyeonggi Province, Bupyeong in Incheon, and Sasang in Busan. If the cumulative domestic sales of 26,244 units are divided among these five locations, one base can handle 5,248 units. If an accident occurs in Jeonnam or Gwangju, the car must be moved to Busan or the metropolitan area. The starting line is different compared to Hyundai Motors and Kia, which have 1,967 official service centers across the country.

![Electric car and parts box on a lift. Among the 21 official service centers, there are 5 that provide sheet metal and painting services. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/china-auto-as-parts.jpg)

## Gap between time and money

Repair delays are identified numerically. As a result of the Insurance Development Institute's analysis of 373 BYD passenger car accidents for which compensation was completed in the first half of this year, the average repair period was 9.8 days. It is 3.1 days longer than the domestic electric passenger vehicle average (6.7 days). The period of using a replacement car or rental car was 2.7 days longer at 9.4 days, and the average rental fee was 1,076,000 won, which was close to twice the average for domestic cars (552,000 won).

Costs also remained in insurance statistics. In the first half of this year, BYD's electric passenger car's property loss ratio was 168.4%, the highest among electric passenger car brands. This means that while the insurance company received 100 won in insurance premiums, it paid 168 won in property compensation. An official from a non-life insurance company said, “If the loss ratio continues to trend at this level, insurance premiums are bound to rise.”

There was also an estimate called a ‘repair cost bomb’ in the car owner community. An estimate that set the labor cost as 2,827,500 won, which is greater than the parts price of 2,151,500 won, was made public, and a post spread that the repair cost exceeded 11 million won in an accident in which the bumper and fender were lightly damaged. These figures are based on estimates and postings made public by the parties, and the extent of damage and the entire work details have not been verified.

Electric buses are of different degrees. According to an OBS report, as of August, the rate of BYD stopping operation due to breakdowns and maintenance in Gyeonggi-do was 2.82%, which was about 1.7 times the average of other domestic and foreign manufacturers. In Gyeonggi-do alone, four BYD buses stood still for over a month due to delays in parts supply. A mechanic who drives an electric bus in Seoul said, “Electric bus parts made in China sometimes take a week to be delivered.”

The structure of commercial vehicles is more rigid. Core components such as battery management system (BMS), high-voltage system, and motor controller are difficult to inspect without manufacturer-specific diagnostic equipment and software. Because parts are not in domestic inventory and rely on the Chinese headquarters, procurement often takes more than a month.

## Company’s explanation and remaining questions

On September 1, BYD Korea refuted the claim by publishing a reference material called ‘Misunderstandings and truths about after-sales service services.’ The controversial accident was reported because only the exterior damage was exposed and internal processes such as correction of structural parts and attachment and detachment of parts were omitted. The quotation was calculated based on the international quotation program 'Audatex' used by 10 domestic non-life insurance companies and imported car brands, and the hourly labor price for general repairs was approximately 115,000 won (excluding VAT). Parts prices are disclosed on the website, and if they are out of stock, they are procured by air transport, and if repairs take a long time, a replacement service is provided.

The data released by the company thereafter also follows the same direction. The plan is to have 21 service centers, 94 workbays, maintenance capacity of 10,000 units per month, Pyeongtaek parts center of 2,000 pyeong, 72 technicians, and 26 locations by the end of the year. BYD Korea said, “Our core task is to stably handle maintenance demand resulting from increased sales and maintain service quality.”

However, the labor wage for each center varies from 110,000 to 115,000 won, and the structure of having 5 accident repair bases cannot be resolved even with company data. The operating method of entrusting maintenance personnel training to six dealers is also pointed out as a factor slowing down the pace of expansion.

At the National Assembly’s Land, Infrastructure and Transport Committee audit on the 23rd of last month, Democratic Party lawmaker Chung Il-young said, “Our people who bought Tesla or BYD are said to be repair refugees.” Hong Ji-seon, Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, expressed sympathy, saying, "I think we should provide citizens with the same service no matter what brand of car they buy."

This problem is not limited to Chinese brands. According to data submitted to the National Assembly by the Korea Consumer Agency, there were 52 applications for damage relief related to electric vehicles filed with Tesla Korea from 2023 to August of this year, which is more than Hyundai Motors (28 cases) and Kia Motors (22 cases) combined. However, BYD's sales in the first half of this year increased 11 times compared to the same period last year (1,066 units → 11,675 units), and the relatively slow expansion of its maintenance network widened the gap.

## Conditions stated in the warranty

Warranty is the most common point of dispute. According to the warranty information on the BYD Korea website, the driving battery (high voltage) is guaranteed to maintain SOH of 70% or more for 8 years or 160,000 km, whichever comes first. The lifespan for the driving gear is 8 years or 150,000km, all vehicle parts are 6 years or 150,000km, the multimedia system and shock absorbers are 3 years or 60,000km, and consumables such as brake pads and tires are 6 months or 10,000km.

Regional conditions for the same brand are not the same. According to a Business Post report, BYD announced on January 15th of this year that it would extend the Blade battery warranty to 8 years and 250,000 km in Europe, retroactively applying it to existing vehicles as well. The battery warranty for vehicles sold domestically is 8 years and 160,000 km. There was no answer from the company as to why the conditions were different only in Korea. It was also pointed out that the basic warranty was clearly stated on the website as 6 years and 150,000 km, which led to misunderstandings as the different conditions for each item were revealed later.

There is a separate minimum line set by law. Article 49-3 of the Enforcement Rules of the Automobile Management Act provides for free repairs for defects that occur within 3 years or 60,000 km from the date of sale for prime movers, power transmission devices, and high-power nuclear electric devices, and within 2 years or 40,000 km for other devices. Even if the manufacturer offers a shorter warranty, the legal standards still apply.

If software defects overlap, warranty processing becomes complicated. A case was reported in which the accumulated mileage of about 7,000km was reset to 0km after an over-the-air update (OTA) in the 2025 BYD Ato3, and the recurrence occurred even after service center inspection. Replacing the body control module (BCM) was discussed, but there were no parts in Korea, so it had to wait 3 to 4 weeks, and the method of manually entering the mileage with a diagnostic device was discussed, leading to a controversy over the reliability of historical data.

## If the importer disappears, the warranty also disappears.

What is more frequently seen in commercial vehicles is ‘ghost warranties’. According to the Kaizuyu Data Research Institute, there are 18 Chinese bus companies that entered the domestic market between 2017 and 2025, and 10 of them continued sales as of 2025. Evik, which sold 20 electric buses in 2017, has since had its supply cut off, and although it is time to replace the batteries, it is difficult to find an official domestic after-sales service counter. It is known that Nanjing Jinlong, Beijing Motors, Ankai, and Foton also virtually disappeared after discontinuing sales.

There are also precedents for passenger cars and small commercial vehicles. DFSK Korea (Arm Motors), which imported Dongpung Socon (DFSK) vehicles, filed for bankruptcy in 2018, and consumers were denied not only after-sales service but also insurance repairs. Shinwon CK Motors, which acquired the sales rights, also closed after three years. At the time, the damaged borrower complained, “There is no one, not the head office, branches, insurance companies, or the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, that will come forward to provide relief.”

The same thing is still happening in rural areas. Gangwon-do announced that as of January last year, 102 (60%) of the 168 electric buses in the province were Chinese manufacturers. A transportation company in Gangneung was unable to operate 12 electric buses made by a Chinese manufacturer for a while due to failure to repair them. An employee of a transportation company in Samcheok said, “The repair period for the vehicles introduced in 2020 is approaching, but I am worried about whether I will be able to receive parts because the domestic company is undergoing rehabilitation procedures.”

The sales base is also shaken. As a large number of Chinese-made electric buses were excluded from the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment's evaluation of the selection of electric vehicle distribution projects, the possibility of new sales being halted and withdrawal is being raised. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport's low-floor bus subsidy has also become difficult to receive if it does not pass the Ministry of Climate Change evaluation. The remaining issue is who will be responsible for supplying parts and maintaining cars that have already been sold.

## There is a law, but it cannot be reached.

Article 32-2, Paragraph 1, Subparagraph 3 of the Automobile Management Act stipulates that manufacturers and importers must provide technical guidance and education necessary for inspection and maintenance, as well as equipment and materials such as breakdown diagnosis devices and maintenance manuals, to registered automobile maintenance service providers.

The Asia Times report on the 12th of last month puts a question mark on the effectiveness of this obligation. The BYD Korea website states that it provides materials in accordance with this provision, but when a reporter inquired about the procedures for using training, diagnostic equipment, and manuals at general maintenance companies through the provided email, the department in charge responded, "It is difficult to participate in the training because it does not meet the conditions for opening technical training." The company released a statement saying, “We are providing it through a web-based system,” which was contradictory to the response from the department in charge. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport's Automobile Policy Department explained that if it is not implemented, an implementation order can be issued.

Compared to overseas, the difference is clear. BYD's German subsidiary operates about 220 local brand repair shops and plans to increase the number to more than 300, and in the UK, it joined hands with maintenance network company Vizion to launch a network of 138 certified repair shops. As of the company's announcement, the parts availability rate is approximately 95% and the average delivery period is one day. In Korea, only plans to expand the company's own service center were presented, and no plans for cooperation with independent maintenance companies were presented. The Korea Automobile Maintenance Business Association (KAPOS) is in the position that cooperation is possible.

The capabilities of the maintenance industry are also a variable. According to the Korea Federation of Small and Medium Business, among 3,180 automobile maintenance companies in Seoul, 364 (11.4%) are capable of maintaining electric vehicles. High-voltage systems that require expensive equipment and specialized personnel cannot be easily handled by general repair shops.

## Shapes of Conflict

There are 953 applications for damage relief related to automobile maintenance filed with the Korea Consumer Agency from 2022 to May 2025. It increased from 234 cases in 2022 to 355 cases in 2024. By type, 73.3% (699 cases) were 'maintenance defects' such as vehicle damage or recurrence of defects after maintenance, 18.2% (173 cases) were 'unreasonable claims' where repair costs, diagnosis fees, and estimate fees were charged without prior notice or excessive maintenance, and 'maintenance delays' due to parts supply problems, etc. were 4.5% (43 cases). Only 36.9% of cases were agreed upon for compensation, repair, or refund.

Delayed maintenance may seem small, but this item can be structurally large for brands that do not keep parts inventory domestically. The Consumer Agency recommends receiving an inspection/maintenance estimate when requesting maintenance and a statement after completion to compare work details and costs, and if any abnormalities are identified, request warranty repairs before the free warranty period expires.

## How far has the system come?

Under the current system, the obligation to supply parts is 8 years. Article 49-3, Paragraph 2 of the Enforcement Rules of the Automobile Management Act stipulates that parts necessary for maintenance must be supplied for more than 8 years from the date of last sale of the same type of vehicle, and if other similar parts are available, they are deemed to have been supplied. Paragraph 3 of the same article requires that parts price data be disclosed on the website.

An amendment has been proposed to increase this period into law. The partial amendment bill to the Automobile Management Act proposed on June 18, 2026 by 10 people, including Rep. Heo Seong-moo, stipulates the parts supply period in the law, not the enforcement regulations, and adds an obligation for manufacturers and importers to build and operate maintenance facilities and service systems during that period. The National Assembly's Land, Infrastructure and Transport Committee referred it on July 23 and submitted it to the general meeting on September 8. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport also announced amendments to the enforcement rules on September 23 and clarified that parts with a useful life of more than 8 years will be supplied beyond the useful life.

The gap between distribution policy and follow-up management was also pointed out in the government audit. The national and local expenses invested over the past five years to purchase BYD electric buses in the metropolitan area are approximately 59.6 billion won, but there are no guidelines for local governments to force maintenance. Rep. Jeong Il-young said that it must be managed “surely, even by revising the law if necessary.”

## The next turn has already been decided

Brands following BYD also face the same test. Geely Automobile's premium brand Zeeker began delivering the mid-sized electric SUV 7X (KRW 52.99 million to KRW 69.99 million) in October, with 129 units registered that month, and announced that it would build service centers in 11 locations across the country. Xiaofeng has appointed a representative for its Korean corporation and is preparing to launch it as early as the first quarter of next year, and Cherry Motors is planning to issue 108.1 billion won worth of convertible bonds to KG Mobility to secure a 16.22% stake and advance into the domestic market next year.

The after-sales service problem of Chinese cars is closer to a problem with the import structure rather than a mistake made by a specific brand. If direct import through a few dealers, consignment maintenance that is not directly operated by the head office, and parts procurement dependent on the head office without domestic inventory overlap, the waiting time increases as sales increase.

Brian Lee, a researcher at CLSA Securities Korea, said, "Right now, everyone is only focusing on the price of the vehicle," and added, "As time goes by and the prices of used cars, service accessibility, and maintenance costs become clear, the attractiveness of the vehicle may decrease."

## Check before buying

- How far is the center where I live for accident repairs (sheet metal, painting)? The total number of service centers and the number of accident repair bases are different.
- Period and distance criteria for each item of the warranty. The battery expires whichever comes first: period or mileage.
- Are the overseas warranty conditions and domestic conditions for the same car model different?
- Are parts prices disclosed on the website, and what is the actual inventory and procurement period?
- Is there a clause in the contract or warranty providing for a replacement or rental car when repairs take a long time?
- Receive an estimate and statement during maintenance, and leave photos before and after the work.
- In the case of commercial vehicles, the financial strength of the importer and the history of withdrawal or replacement of the importer in the past.

In a market where sales have increased simply because car prices are low, the next question ultimately comes back to ‘Who will fix this car and how quickly?’ Parts inventory and maintenance access have become items that must be confirmed through contract terms and records rather than advertising text.
disclaimer: This article was written based on publicly available press and government data and the company’s official position. The figures cited are as of the time of each source's announcement, and unconfirmed community claims are categorized as 'raised cases'.

title: Korea-Japan FTA resumes after 20 years — The remaining barriers are not tariffs but rules
deck: Negotiations that stopped in 2004 were brought back to the table in 2026. The card the government pulled out was CPTPP, not bilateral negotiations. The numbers followed the changed conditions due to the $20.6 billion deficit with Japan and dependence on the small and medium-sized department.
author: Insight Brief Editorial Room
summary: In 2025, exports to Japan were $28.3 billion and imports were $48.9 billion, resulting in a deficit of about $20.6 billion. The deficit, which had decreased from its peak of $36.1 billion in 2010, has increased again due to increased imports of semiconductor equipment.

The export competition between Korea and Japan is 46.8, the highest among major countries. However, the center of competition has shifted from finished products to materials, parts, equipment, and high-tech fields, and 83% of tariffs have already been eliminated through RCEP, so the practical benefits of further tariff reductions are limited.

In March 2026, discussions on Korea-Japan supply chain partnership and CPTPP membership became a practical window for cooperation. The issue is not tariff rates, but origin accumulation, binding force of crisis response provisions, protection of sensitive items, and profit distribution.
body:
FKI Tower, Yeouido, Seoul, October 23, 2026. At the 33rd Korea-Japan Business Meeting, Yoshinobu Tsutsui, Chairman of the Federation of Japanese Economic Organizations (Keidanren), said, “We actively look forward to Korea’s application to join the CPTPP.” Minister of Trade, Industry and Energy Kim Jeong-gwan, who appeared at the same event, responded that he would continue to communicate with stakeholders “so that domestic procedures can be completed and as soon as possible.” Discussions on the Korea-Japan Free Trade Agreement (FTA), which had stalled after the sixth round of negotiations in November 2004, are back on the table after 20 years. However, the card the government has drawn is not a resumption of bilateral negotiations, but an application to join the CPTPP. It is a detour that aims to do what a bilateral FTA could not do through a multilateral agreement in which Japan is effectively the gatekeeper.

However, the agenda for this table is different from 2004. It is not a question of how much tariffs will be lowered, but who will move first when the supply chain is interrupted and under what rules will it be restored. Japan's export restrictions on semiconductor materials in 2019, the shift in the trade balance with China to a deficit in 2023, and the expansion of the deficit with Japan caused by the semiconductor super cycle in 2025 changed the premise of the negotiation table 20 years ago.

## Negotiations that stopped 20 years ago are brought up again

Korea-Japan FTA negotiations began in December 2003 and were conducted six times until November 2004, but no conclusion was reached. The government cited the opening of Japan's agricultural and marine products market, resolution of non-tariff barriers, and opening of the government procurement market as issues at the time. Afterwards, there were four working-level council meetings in 2008 and 2009, two director-level council meetings in 2010 and 2011, and three manager-level council meetings in 2012, and negotiations were not resumed.

The document that lowered tariffs for the first time between Korea and Japan was not a bilateral FTA, but the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement (RCEP), which came into effect in February 2022. The two countries decided to eliminate 83% of tariffs based on the number of items, but sensitive items such as automobiles and machinery were excluded from the concessions, and the rate of elimination of agricultural products was only 46%. Only 41.4% of the items became tariff-free immediately after effect. It was an agreement in which the fact that it was the ‘first institutional connection between Korea and Japan’ was more important than the extent of the tariff reduction.

The waters of resumption burst one after another in 2026. On March 14, the Korea-Japan Industry and Trade Ministers' Meeting was held in Tokyo, and the ‘Korea-Japan Industry and Trade Policy Dialogue’, a regular consultative body, was established, and the ‘Korea-Japan Supply Chain Partnership (SCPA)’ was signed on the same day. On April 22, Yeo Han-gu, head of the Trade Negotiation Headquarters, mentioned the case where Korea and Japan tried to pursue an FTA 20 years ago but stopped at the Keidanren Hall in Tokyo, and said that there is a need to discuss a new trade and investment framework now that the strategic interests of the two countries are higher than ever. At the Andong Summit on May 19, a joint press release was issued by the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry, detailing cooperation on energy security and supply chain resilience.

The private sector moved further ahead. At the 26th Korea-Japan New Industry Trade Conference on March 16, Lee In-ho, vice president of the Korea International Trade Association, said that it is time to design the future trade order together through the CPTPP and the Korea-Japan FTA and connect the results to growth and stability. At the Choi Jonghyun Academy and East Asia Institute conference on November 12, a three-stage roadmap for 2026-2045 was presented. The first step is Korea's accession to the CPTPP, and the final step is the conclusion of the Korea-Japan Economic Community Agreement. Although this roadmap is an expert proposal rather than an intergovernmental agreement, it shows the coordinates of the discussion.

## Now in numbers: $20.6 billion deficit and 4.0%

In 2025, Korea's exports to Japan were $28.3 billion, down 4.4% from the previous year, and imports were $48.9 billion, up 2.8%. The deficit was about $20.6 billion, an increase of $2.6 billion from a year ago. The deficit with Japan peaked at $36.1 billion in 2010 and has been decreasing, but rebounded in 2025.

The reason becomes clear when you look at the items. The top export to Japan is petroleum products (USD 5.38 billion, -21.7%), followed by steel sheets (USD 2.12 billion). On the other hand, the top imports from Japan are semiconductors (USD 8.35 billion) and semiconductor manufacturing equipment (USD 6.34 billion, +20.9%). The structure is that the more Korea makes and sells finished memory products, the more equipment and materials needed for its production are purchased from Japan. The Japan External Trade Organization (JETRO) cited “increased domestic production due to the semiconductor super cycle” as the reason for the expansion of the deficit with Japan in 2025.

The weight of trade also decreased. Japan's share of total exports is 4.0%, and its import share is 7.7%. Korea's share of Japan's total exports is 6.3%. When discussing the Korea-Japan FTA in the early 2000s, the relationship was not the ‘largest trading partner’, but rather an ‘important but not the only’ partner for both sides.

Changes in public relations are faster. China's share of total exports fell to 19.7% in 2024 and 18.4% in 2025, and the trade balance with China returned to a deficit of $18.1 billion in 2023, followed by a deficit of $6.9 billion in 2024 and $11.2 billion in 2025. The report by the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry analyzed that the proportion of Chinese added value included in Korean exports is increasing, and conversely, China is reducing its dependence on Korea and Japan for added value. As it has become difficult to rely on one direction for both exports and imports to China, creating rules with neighbors who share the same supply chain risks has emerged as the next task.

There are also indicators that the nature of the relationship itself has changed. According to JETRO, Korea overtook Japan for the first time in per capita gross domestic product (GDP) in 2022, and in 2024, the gap widened to $36,239 in Korea and $32,487 in Japan. This is the result of a shift from a structure in which Japan unilaterally sold capital- and technology-intensive products and Korea sold labor-intensive products to a structure in which both countries buy and sell capital and technology-intensive products. The same goes for investing. Japan's direct investment in Korea reached an all-time high of $6.12 billion in 2024, ranking first among countries, and decreased by 28.1% to $4.4 billion in 2025. Conversely, Korean companies' investment in Japan exceeded the all-time high with 318 new corporations between January and September 2025.

![Busan Port container terminal and semiconductor clean room. The deficit with Japan in 2025 will be $20.6 billion, and the top import from Japan is semiconductors. Image · AI illustration](/assets/img/articles/korea-japan-fta-supply-chain.jpg)

## Competition did not decrease, only the center of gravity shifted.

The statement that ‘Korea and Japan are no longer competitors’ is only half true. The export competitiveness index (ESI) analyzed by the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA) from 2019 to the third quarter of 2024 was the highest in Japan at 46.8. Singapore (40.1), Germany (39.8), the United States (39.1), and China (38.5) followed. Among the 10 major export items, 9 overlapped with Japan. During the same period, the level of competition with Japan and the United States decreased overall, but KOTRA interpreted this as “not a relaxation of competition, but a result of competition being concentrated in core industries such as semiconductors, automobiles, and parts, and production bases being dispersed.”

The analysis that competition has shifted to China is in the same context. In 2024, Korea-China semiconductor export competition was 72.2, which was overwhelmingly high among major countries. The Korea Institute for International Economic Policy (KIEP) analyzed that the export competition between Korea and Japan in the materials, parts, and equipment sectors increased from 57.5 in 2001 to 61.3 in 2018. Competition has not disappeared, but has narrowed and intensified from finished products to parts, materials, equipment, and advanced processes.

Therefore, simply reducing tariffs on finished products does not bring much benefit. A significant portion of the tariffs have already been opened through RCEP, and the remaining tariffs are focused on items that both countries want to protect, such as automobiles and machinery. In an analysis submitted to the National Assembly by the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Energy in 2000, it was estimated that if the Korea-Japan FTA was concluded, the deficit with Japan would increase by $6.09 billion and real GDP and welfare would decrease by 0.07% and 0.19%, respectively. This was the calculation behind the suspension of negotiations 20 years ago.

## Three Axes of Cooperation

Discussions about 2026 find practical benefits in places different from then. The first is supply chain and economic security rules. The Korea-Japan Supply Chain Partnership (SCPA), concluded on March 14, includes provisions to notify any signs of disturbance, hold an emergency meeting within 5 days of the request in the event of a disturbance, refrain from taking actions that have a negative impact on the other country's supply chain, and promote joint exploration and investment in key minerals. In July 2019, Japan changed the export of three items, hydrogen fluoride, fluorinated polyimide, and photoresist, to individual permits and excluded Korea from the whitelist in August of that year, and the experience of taking four years to restore the original condition in March 2023 and the whitelist in June has become a document.

The second is materials, parts, equipment (maintenance) and cutting-edge processes. A report by the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry analyzed that the deficit with Japan in the small and medium-sized furniture sector will increase from $18.4 billion in 2015 to about $23.2 billion in 2025, exceeding the overall deficit with Japan in the same year ($20.6 billion). This means that the entire small and medium-sized business has generated an annual surplus of over $100 billion over the past five years, but the deficit is concentrated in specific upstream items. The government lowered the dependence on imports of materials and materials from Japan from 16.9% in 2019 to 13.9% in 2024, and the dependence on imports of the top 100 items dependent on Japan from 30.6% to 20.2%. Nevertheless, imports of semiconductor manufacturing equipment increased by more than 20% in 2025.

Supply chain risks are not unique to Korea. KIEP analyzed that Japan's dependence on China for semiconductor raw materials is 97% for hydrogen fluoride, 90% for phosphoric acid and polyphosphoric acid, and 89% for silicon carbide. Korea is also highly dependent on certain countries for yellow phosphorus, fluorite, rare gas, and tungsten. Herein lies the practical benefit of two countries with different bottlenecks sharing information and jointly designing stockpiles and replacement technologies.

Movement on the ground is faster than government documents. SK Hynix held its first Partners' Day in Chiba Prefecture, Japan on October 29 and shared the next-generation HBM process roadmap with top executives from 20 companies, including Shin-Etsu, Sumco, JSR, Tokyo Electron, and Disco. On September 22, in Seoul, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and the Hokkaido regional government and economic community held the first Korea-Japan (Hokkaido) semiconductor industry cooperation exchange meeting. Hokkaido, where Lapidus' 2-nano base is located, has a relatively thin preprocessing and back-end process ecosystem, and Korea has that ecosystem.

Third is energy and third country markets. Korea Gas Corporation and Japan's JERA signed an agreement on March 14 to cooperate in the supply and demand of liquefied natural gas (LNG), and a joint press release from the May summit included plans to supply crude oil and petroleum products to each other in emergency situations. Joint entry into third countries is still a business unit. Korea, the United States, and Japan signed a memorandum of cooperation to support the introduction of small modular reactors (SMRs) in the Indo-Pacific region in July, and Indonesia is being considered as the first candidate site. Korea is in charge of construction, the United States is in charge of nuclear reactor design, and Japan is in charge of major equipment manufacturing. The manufacturing base established by Japan through long-term ODA and dedicated industrial complexes in India is also considered a model for Korean companies to use as a reference.

## Two branches of institutionalization: RCEP and CPTPP.

There are two channels that bind cooperation into rules. One is RCEP, which has already come into effect, and the other is CPTPP, which is being considered for membership. According to a report by the Korea International Trade Association, CPTPP accounts for 14.3% of global GDP and has a tariff elimination rate of 99%. Since entry into force, intra-regional exports between the parties have grown at an average annual rate of 3.2%, reaching $618 billion in 2024. If Korea joins, the terms of trade with Japan and Mexico, which do not have an FTA, are expected to improve and the effect of being directly incorporated into the regional value chain is expected.

The government announced that it would begin social discussions and collect opinions regarding CPTPP membership at the Foreign Economy Ministers' Meeting on August 27, 2026. There are two obstacles. Because new membership in the CPTPP is decided unanimously by existing member countries, Japan, which effectively leads the agreement, acts as the gatekeeper. Japan has been demanding that countries applying for membership abolish regulations on importing seafood from eight prefectures, including Fukushima. President Lee Jae-myung said in a Japanese media interview in August 2025 that “restoring people’s trust in Japanese seafood is a priority,” and the government’s stance is to maintain regulations for the time being.

Bilateral FTA is the next issue. Japan has preferred multilateral agreements such as CPTPP over bilateral FTAs, and negotiations with Korea have not officially resumed for 20 years. Professor Kwon Hyuk-wook of Nippon University said, “If we were to pursue it again now, a realistic goal would be to create an FTA of a slightly higher level than simple tariff elimination.” This means that rules of origin, certification/standards, services/investment, and labor movement are the real issues rather than tariffs.

## Counterargument: Who pays the cost?

The distribution of costs is as clear as the benefits of expansion. First, it is the agricultural and fisheries industry. The Korea Succession Farmers' Central Association issued a statement on August 27 and urged a halt to discussions, saying, “Joining the CPTPP could have a significant impact on domestic agriculture due to the additional opening of the agricultural product market.” The Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs also expressed concern about a significant impact on the agricultural sector. CPTPP's level of openness to agricultural products is higher than that of RCEP, and the scope of concessions for sensitive items such as rice and livestock products is expected to be the biggest variable in the negotiations.

Second, there is a fall in the manufacturing industry. A computable general equilibrium (CGE) analysis published in the academic journal Asia-Pacific Studies in 2025 estimated that the Korea-Japan FTA would increase Korea's real GDP by 0.37% and welfare by $2.937 billion, while Japan's GDP would increase by 0.14% and welfare by $7.535 billion. However, by industry, production in the machinery industry alone decreased by 1.11%, while electronics (1.23%), processed food (1.12%), and textiles and clothing (0.83%) increased. This is a different result from the concerns raised in the early 2000s that electronics, steel, and chemical production would decline, but the structure of shocks concentrated on specific industries, such as machinery, remains.

Third, it is a small and medium-sized business. If the tariffs on Japanese intermediate goods are lowered, the cost for companies that demand them will be lowered, but pressure will increase on price competition for small and medium-sized companies that produce domestically produced substitute products. At the time of RCEP, KDI Nara Economy described this effect as a “double-edged sword” and pointed out that it could conflict with the policy of domestic production of small and medium-sized materials. If the profits come from the procurement costs of large corporations and the costs are concentrated on small and medium-sized suppliers, political support will weaken even if the overall benefits are large.

Fourth, there is political risk. The 2019 export regulations showed that even if there is a system, it can become powerless if politics overturn it. The actual size of the safety net will be determined by whether the SCPA’s ‘refrain from taking actions that negatively affect the mutual supply chain’ clause is a recommendation or a binding promise that binds consultation and dispute resolution procedures in case of violation.

## Four things to check

- **Sensitive Item Concessions** — To what extent are automobiles, machinery, rice, livestock, and marine products opened, and how long is the grace period? The first number is how CPTPP handles items excluded from RCEP.
- **Origin Cumulative** — Supply chain cooperation will lead to tariff benefits only when full cumulative regulations that go beyond the bilateral accumulation between Korea and Japan and extend to ASEAN, Australia, and New Zealand are introduced.
- **Binding force of crisis clause** — Whether notification of disturbance, emergency meeting within 5 days, and refraining from action are declarations or obligations. Are there consultation and dispute resolution procedures in case of violation?
- **Profit Distribution** — Increasing accessibility to the Trade Adjustment Support System and designing response investment and workforce transition for small and medium-sized enterprises.

## Tariffs are already low, all that remains is the rules

The purpose of the Korea-Japan FTA has changed from 20 years ago. It moved from a document that opened the market to rules that ensured that it would not be cut off. The deficit of $20.6 billion in 2025 is not a number caused by the weakness of Korea's manufacturing industry. This is the result of a division of labor structure in which the more semiconductors are made, the more Japanese equipment and materials must be purchased. The goal is not to eliminate that structure, but a realistic goal is to have a meeting held within 5 days if it is cut off and an alternative supply line to operate.

The $1 trillion synergy proposed by Choi Tae-won, Chairman of the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry, is not yet a verified estimate but a mid- to long-term goal. Some point out that the investment effects, cost savings, and realization period for each field were not disclosed. So what we need to check now is not the slogan but the schedule. When are applications for CPTPP membership submitted, how many times a year does the Korea-Japan Industry and Trade Policy Dialogue take place, and do emergency meeting requests actually work? The results of the table reopened after 20 years will remain as those three records.
